# caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

Vite plugin for [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper): React component prop metadata on a virtual module, updated through HMR as components change.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

docgen.components['Button'].props
```

Extraction runs on OXC through [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi): about 50ms cold across 21 real component libraries and about 2ms for an incremental single-file update. Requires Vite 7 or 8.

Options, benchmarks and migration notes: https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper

License: AGPL-3.0-or-later.

# caliper-docgen-core

Core library for [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper): extracts React component props from TypeScript with [OXC](https://oxc.rs). No TypeScript compiler program and no type-checking pass, so a cold run over 21 real component libraries takes about 50ms.

Pipeline: parse files in parallel, merge the symbol data, resolve each component's props, return the extraction output. Whenever it degrades it emits a `Diagnostic` rather than failing silently.

This crate is pure extraction logic: no terminal output, no async. The command-line tool is [`caliper-docgen`](https://crates.io/crates/caliper-docgen), and the Node bindings are [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi).

Docs: https://docs.rs/caliper-docgen-core. Architecture notes and known gaps: https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper

License: AGPL-3.0-or-later.

caliper-docgen

React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax. > **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete. ## Why `react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system that takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish. OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass: - **Cold extraction, 21 real component libraries:** 50ms ([full breakdown](docs/benchmarks.md)) - **Incremental single-file update:** ~2ms — react-docgen-typescript has no equivalent API; every edit re-pays the full cold cost The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet. ## Install > Not yet on npm. No prebuilt per-platform binaries exist yet — build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper cd caliper pnpm install pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi run build:napi # builds the native addon for your platform pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin build ``` Use `pnpm run build:napi`, not a bare `cargo build` — it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s loader expects it. Migrating off `react-docgen-typescript`? See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) for what's compatible today. ## Vite plugin ```ts // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from 'vite' import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react' import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })], }) ``` Metadata is available on the `virtual:caliper-docgen` module and pushed via HMR as components change: ```ts import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen' docgen.components['Button'].props // { // variant: { // type: { kind: 'literalUnion', members: ['default', 'destructive', 'outline'], hasDefault: true }, // required: false, // defaultValue: { value: '"default"', computed: false }, // description: '', // }, // ... // } ``` ## CLI A single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and `--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there. `caliper-docgen` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that execs the platform-appropriate compiled binary — no reimplemented logic, so there's exactly one place CLI behavior can drift. ```bash # Once published: npx caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # From source today: ./target/release/caliper-docgen (after cargo build --release) # One-shot extraction caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # Inspect a single file caliper-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx # Watch mode caliper-docgen watch --src src/ # Shell completions caliper-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_caliper-docgen # Full HTML attribute expansion instead of the default curated subset caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --html-attributes full ``` Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `reactVersion`, `crossPackage`, and more — see `crates/cli/src/config.rs` for the full schema) instead of CLI flags. ## Output shape ```json { "components": { "Button": { "displayName": "Button", "filePath": "src/components/Button.tsx", "props": { "variant": { "type": { "kind": "literalUnion", "members": ["default", "destructive", "outline"], "hasDefault": true }, "required": false, "defaultValue": { "value": "\"default\"", "computed": false }, "description": "Visual style variant.", "tags": {} } }, "inheritance": [ { "typeName": "ButtonHTMLAttributes", "htmlElement": "button", "omitted": [], "totalProps": 147 } ], "notableInherited": { "onClick": { "type": { "kind": "eventHandler", "eventType": "MouseEvent" }, ... }, "disabled": { "type": { "kind": "boolean" }, ... } }, "discriminantProp": null } }, "diagnostics": [], "stats": { "filesParsed": 3, "durationMs": 12, "dtsCacheHits": 2, ... } } ``` ## Supported patterns | Pattern | Example | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | Function components | `function Button(props: ButtonProps)` | | Arrow components | `const Button = (props: ButtonProps) => ...` | | `React.forwardRef` | `forwardRef(...)` | | HOC-wrapped | `styled(Base)` | | Interface inheritance | `interface ButtonProps extends HTMLAttributes` | | Intersection aliases | `type ButtonProps = BaseProps & { variant?: string }` | | `Omit` / `Pick` | `type ButtonProps = Omit` | | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` | | `VariantProps` | `VariantProps` (CVA / TV / PandaCSS) | | Discriminated unions | MUI-style `variant: 'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'standard'` | | JSDoc tags | `@description`, `@default`, `@deprecated`, `@internal` | ## Repository ``` crates/core/ pure extraction logic (no I/O, no async, Send + Sync) crates/binding/ thin NAPI wrapper over core crates/cli/ clap + miette CLI packages/napi/ caliper-docgen-napi (dev binary loader + TS types) packages/vite-plugin/ caliper-docgen-vite-plugin packages/cli/ caliper-docgen (npx wrapper — execs crates/cli's binary, no reimplemented logic) apps/validate/ accuracy comparison harness (react-docgen, rdt, ours) fixtures/ real library .d.ts/.tsx files (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, etc.) ``` ## Contributing [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — setup, code style, commit conventions. [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) — pipeline, modules, key design decisions. ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

Yes, that matches how callisto is set up, and caliper is currently different. I haven't changed anything; this is the call to make first.

**Callisto's licensing**
- **Copyright:** `LICENSE` is FSL-1.1-MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Gabriel Castro (Orin DX)".
- **Split:** the workspace is `FSL-1.1-MIT` (becomes MIT two years after each version's release), except `callisto-model`, which is plain `MIT`.
- **Why the split:** it's the library other code depends on.

**Caliper's licensing**
- Everything is `AGPL-3.0-or-later`: the workspace `Cargo.toml`, 13 `package.json` files, `deny.toml`, the root README, and the READMEs I just wrote in #45.

**What to know before switching**
- **Published versions:** 0.2.1 is already out under AGPL on crates.io and npm. That's permanent for those versions, so the first FSL release would be 0.2.2.
- **Relicensing:** this is fine if you're the sole copyright holder. Check that no outside contributions exist beyond dependabot (the workspace `authors` field says "contributors", but I haven't audited commits).
- **Adoption:** FSL isn't OSI open source, and it bars competing commercial use. For a tool design systems will install into their toolchains, that may matter. AGPL has its own friction for companies.

**My suggestion:** mirror callisto. `caliper-docgen-core` and the npm packages that expose it become `MIT`, like `callisto-model`, and the CLI, napi binding and Vite plugin become `FSL-1.1-MIT`. Say if you'd rather make everything FSL, or everything MIT.

**What it touches:** `LICENSE` (copied into the published crates), the workspace and per-crate `license`, all `package.json` files, the READMEs, `deny.toml`, and the root README's license section. I'd put it in its own PR or fold it into #45, since both ship in 0.2.2 anyway.

Which split do you want, and should it go in #45 or its own PR?

Dependency-aware, changeset-driven versioning and releases for Cargo, npm, and PyPI monorepos.

--- Callisto turns per-package changesets into a version plan for Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI workspaces. It reads native manifests to decide which dependents need updates, then prepares the files and release operations for review. ## A change through Callisto Suppose `service` depends on a Cargo crate `core` at `^0.2`. A contributor records a minor change to `core`: ```sh callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API" callisto version --dry-run ``` With the default cascade policy, the plan is: | Package | Before | Planned change | | --- | --- | --- | | `core` | `0.2.0` | `0.3.0` from the changeset | | `service` | `1.4.2`, requires `core ^0.2` | `1.4.3` from the default patch cascade; requirement updated to `^0.3` | | Unrelated npm or Python package | Its current version | No bump just because it shares the repo | The dependency requirement triggers the `service` bump; sharing a repo does not. Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Explicit version groups can couple packages that should move together. - `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs for review and commit. - The release workflow uses native publishers and coordinates configured tags, GitHub releases, and assets. Package owners retain their hooks and credentials. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; changesets["Changesets

This registry-only example publishes a crate and creates a tag; it does not build assets or create a GitHub Release. See [releasing](docs/releasing.md) for CI and product releases. ```bash # 1. Record a pending change against a package callisto add --package cargo/my-crate:minor --summary "Add authentication middleware" # 3. See pending changesets and the version bumps they imply callisto status # 4. Consume changesets, bump manifests, update changelogs and lockfiles callisto version # 6. Commit the staged release changes; release requires a clean checkout git commit -m "chore(release): version packages" # 7. Preview, then publish callisto release --dry-run callisto release ``` Run `callisto --help` for prerelease mode, snapshots, CI checks, JSON output, and shell completions. ## Documentation - [Guide](docs/how-callisto-works.md): release model, example, and supported layouts. - [Releasing](docs/releasing.md): local and CI workflows, limits, and recovery. - [Publishing](docs/publishing.md): registry credentials. - [Configuration](docs/config.md) and [errors](docs/errors.md): references. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [security](SECURITY.md): project information. ## License Mixed: `callisto-model` is MIT; the rest of the workspace is [FSL-1.1-MIT](LICENSE) (becomes MIT two years after each version's release). Ten cooperating plugins covering the full development lifecycle, connected by shared JSON schemas and a common verification gate.

Use this when you're building non-trivial software with AI coding agents and need to know every acceptance criterion was implemented and tested — not assumed. The specific problem: agents working across long sessions silently drop criteria as context compresses. Specs live on disk. Agents read from disk. Drift is detectable, not silent.

--- ## Wisp Plugins — the Lifecycle Ecosystem Ten plugins, each a specialist persona covering one stage of the development lifecycle — together they're **Wisp Plugins**, the agent-side companions to the [Wisp](https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp) project-intelligence library. Lifecycle handoffs use typed artifacts where applicable. The plugins are composable: install only the personas your workflow needs. **The primary flow** — one direction, no side-taps: ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; we["Weaver
capture need"] -->|"requirement@1"| va["Vanguard
research"] va -->|"research-report@1"| sc["Scribe
specify"] mu["Muse
component spec"] -->|"spec@1"| na["Navigator
plan"] sc -->|"spec@1"| na na -->|"plan@1"| sm["Smith
implement"] sm -->|"verified change"| co["Courier
ship"] co -.->|"next need"| we class we,mu source class va,sc,sm engine class na router class co output ``` **Verification** — Sentinel and Ranger attach to the flow above but aren't stops in its sequence; the muted dashed boxes below are the same personas shown only as attachment points: ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; sc2["Scribe"]:::store sm2["Smith"]:::store co2["Courier"]:::store se{{"Sentinel
independent gate"}} ra{{"Ranger
defect audit"}} sc2 -.->|"spec@1"| se sm2 -.->|"code + verdict@3"| se sm2 -.->|"implementation-review@2"| sc2 se -.->|"verdict@3"| co2 sm2 -->|"live code"| ra ra -.->|"finding-report@2"| sc2 class se,ra router ``` ![Define](https://img.shields.io/badge/-Define-6366f1) ![Design](https://img.shields.io/badge/-Design-8b5cf6) ![Build](https://img.shields.io/badge/-Build-3b82f6) ![Verify](https://img.shields.io/badge/-Verify-f59e0b) ![Ship](https://img.shields.io/badge/-Ship-10b981) ![Meta](https://img.shields.io/badge/-Meta-64748b) *Pill-shaped nodes are cross-cutting checkpoints, not sequence stops. Solid arrows are direct handoffs; dashed arrows are verification side-channels. Ranger's input is the live codebase Smith just wrote, not a schema handoff — the one solid arrow in the second diagram.* ======ARCH

Callisto Architecture

Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

--- ## Invariants 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST; `package.json` is fingerprinted for indent style and line endings before a `serde_json` (`preserve_order`) round trip. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent and grandparent directories) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 6. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. Full list: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). Design decisions, with the options they rejected and why: [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md). ## Crate map ``` Layer 1 (leaf) callisto-model Layer 2 (I/O) callisto-manifests Layer 3 (engine) callisto-graph Layer 4 (surface) callisto-cli Dev-only callisto-fixtures ``` | Crate | License | Depends on | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`callisto-model`](crates/callisto-model) | MIT | none | Domain primitives (`PackageId`, `Version`, `Severity`, `Changeset`, `PreState`), `atomic_write`, `ApplyPermit`, the `CommandRunner`/`DependencyResolver` trait seams; `format`: `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` parser/writer; `vcs`: `GitAccess`, every Git operation as a subprocess through `CommandRunner` | | [`callisto-manifests`](crates/callisto-manifests) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model | `Manifest` trait; format-preserving Cargo/npm/PyPI manifest editors | | [`callisto-graph`](crates/callisto-graph) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests | Dependency graph, cascade engine, version planning, release execution; `conventional`: Conventional Commit parsing and bump inference; `changelog`: Markdown changelog rendering | | [`callisto-cli`](crates/callisto-cli) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph | `clap` CLI surface, `miette` diagnostic rendering | | [`callisto-fixtures`](crates/callisto-fixtures) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) | Multi-ecosystem test corpus and in-memory test doubles | Dependencies only point down the layers (`cli` → `graph` → `manifests` → `model`). Nothing in Layer 1–3 depends on `callisto-cli`. ## Data flow ``` Workspace::load config::load -> config::resolve callisto.toml -> ResolvedConfig ManifestWalkResolver::build discover (ProjectLocator), read manifests (Manifest), assign ids, attach platform packages, apply per-package config GroupTable::resolve bind [[fixed-group]] / [[linked-group]] members plan_version -> VersionPlan (in memory) aggregate changesets + opt-in commit inference -> severity per package run_cascade dependents (runtime, build, optional, peer; never dev), groups, pre mode -> target version per package, with its reasons version --emit-decision derives and validates the decision in memory, before apply

caliper-docgen

React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax. > **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete. ## Why `react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system that takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish. OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass: - **Cold extraction, 21 real component libraries:** 50ms ([full breakdown](docs/benchmarks.md)) - **Incremental single-file update:** ~2ms — react-docgen-typescript has no equivalent API; every edit re-pays the full cold cost The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet. ## Install ```bash npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen # CLI, with the prebuilt binary for your platform npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin # Vite plugin cargo install caliper-docgen # CLI from crates.io ``` To build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper cd caliper pnpm install pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi run build:napi # builds the native addon for your platform pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin build ``` Use `pnpm run build:napi`, not a bare `cargo build` — it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s loader expects it. Migrating off `react-docgen-typescript`? See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) for what's compatible today. ## Vite plugin ```ts // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from 'vite' import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react' import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })], }) ``` Metadata is available on the `virtual:caliper-docgen` module and pushed via HMR as components change: ```ts import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen' docgen.components['Button'].props // { // variant: { // type: { kind: 'literalUnion', members: ['default', 'destructive', 'outline'], hasDefault: true }, // required: false, // defaultValue: { value: '"default"', computed: false }, // description: '', // }, // ... // } ``` ## CLI A single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and `--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there. `caliper-docgen` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that execs the platform-appropriate compiled binary — no reimplemented logic, so there's exactly one place CLI behavior can drift. ```bash # Once published: npx caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # From source today: ./target/release/caliper-docgen (after cargo build --release) # One-shot extraction caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # Inspect a single file caliper-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx # Watch mode caliper-docgen watch --src src/ # Shell completions caliper-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_caliper-docgen # Full HTML attribute expansion instead of the default curated subset caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --html-attributes full ``` Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `reactVersion`, `crossPackage`, and more — see `crates/cli/src/config.rs` for the full schema) instead of CLI flags. ## Output shape ```json { "components": { "Button": { "displayName": "Button", "filePath": "src/components/Button.tsx", "props": { "variant": { "type": { "kind": "literalUnion", "members": ["default", "destructive", "outline"], "hasDefault": true }, "required": false, "defaultValue": { "value": "\"default\"", "computed": false }, "description": "Visual style variant.", "tags": {} } }, "inheritance": [ { "typeName": "ButtonHTMLAttributes", "htmlElement": "button", "omitted": [], "totalProps": 147 } ], "notableInherited": { "onClick": { "type": { "kind": "eventHandler", "eventType": "MouseEvent" }, ... }, "disabled": { "type": { "kind": "boolean" }, ... } }, "discriminantProp": null } }, "diagnostics": [], "stats": { "filesParsed": 3, "durationMs": 12, "dtsCacheHits": 2, ... } } ``` ## Supported patterns | Pattern | Example | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | Function components | `function Button(props: ButtonProps)` | | Arrow components | `const Button = (props: ButtonProps) => ...` | | `React.forwardRef` | `forwardRef(...)` | | HOC-wrapped | `styled(Base)` | | Interface inheritance | `interface ButtonProps extends HTMLAttributes` | | Intersection aliases | `type ButtonProps = BaseProps & { variant?: string }` | | `Omit` / `Pick` | `type ButtonProps = Omit` | | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` | | `VariantProps` | `VariantProps` (CVA / TV / PandaCSS) | | Discriminated unions | MUI-style `variant: 'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'standard'` | | JSDoc tags | `@description`, `@default`, `@deprecated`, `@internal` | ## Repository ``` crates/core/ pure extraction logic (no I/O, no async, Send + Sync) crates/binding/ thin NAPI wrapper over core crates/cli/ clap + miette CLI packages/napi/ caliper-docgen-napi (dev binary loader + TS types) packages/vite-plugin/ caliper-docgen-vite-plugin packages/cli/ caliper-docgen (npx wrapper — execs crates/cli's binary, no reimplemented logic) apps/validate/ accuracy comparison harness (react-docgen, rdt, ours) fixtures/ real library .d.ts/.tsx files (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, etc.) ``` ## Contributing [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — setup, code style, commit conventions. [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) — pipeline, modules, key design decisions. ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

CLI A single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and `--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there. `caliper-docgen` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that execs the platform-appropriate compiled binary — no reimplemented logic, so there's exactly one place CLI behavior can drift. ```bash # Once published: npx caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # From source today: ./target/release/caliper-docgen (after cargo build --release) # One-shot extraction caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # Inspect a single file caliper-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx # Watch mode caliper-docgen watch --src src/ # Shell completions caliper-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_caliper-docgen # Full HTML attribute expansion instead of the default curated subset caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --html-attributes full ``` Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `reactVersion`, `crossPackage`, and more — see `crates/cli/src/config.rs` for the full schema) instead of CLI flags. ## Output shape ```json { "components": { "Button": { "displayName": "Button", "filePath": "src/components/Button.tsx", "props": { "variant": { "type": { "kind": "literalUnion", "members": ["default", "destructive", "outline"], "hasDefault": true }, "required": false, "defaultValue": { "value": "\"default\"", "computed": false }, "description": "Visual style variant.", "tags": {} } }, "inheritance": [ { "typeName": "ButtonHTMLAttributes", "htmlElement": "button", "omitted": [], "totalProps": 147 } ], "notableInherited": { "onClick": { "type": { "kind": "eventHandler", "eventType": "MouseEvent" }, ... }, "disabled": { "type": { "kind": "boolean" }, ... } }, "discriminantProp": null } }, "diagnostics": [], "stats": { "filesParsed": 3, "durationMs": 12, "dtsCacheHits": 2, ... } } ``` ## Supported patterns | Pattern | Example | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | Function components | `function Button(props: ButtonProps)` | | Arrow components | `const Button = (props: ButtonProps) => ...` | | `React.forwardRef` | `forwardRef(...)` | | HOC-wrapped | `styled(Base)` | | Interface inheritance | `interface ButtonProps extends HTMLAttributes` | | Intersection aliases | `type ButtonProps = BaseProps & { variant?: string }` | | `Omit` / `Pick` | `type ButtonProps = Omit` | | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` | | `VariantProps` | `VariantProps` (CVA / TV / PandaCSS) | | Discriminated unions | MUI-style `variant: 'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'standard'` | | JSDoc tags | `@description`, `@default`, `@deprecated`, `@internal` | ## Repository ``` crates/core/ pure extraction logic (no I/O, no async, Send + Sync) crates/binding/ thin NAPI wrapper over core crates/cli/ clap + miette CLI packages/napi/ caliper-docgen-napi (dev binary loader + TS types) packages/vite-plugin/ caliper-docgen-vite-plugin packages/cli/ caliper-docgen (npx wrapper — execs crates/cli's binary, no reimplemented logic) apps/validate/ accuracy comparison harness (react-docgen, rdt, ours) fixtures/ real library .d.ts/.tsx files (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, etc.) ``` ## Contributing [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — setup, code style, commit conventions. Fast React component prop extraction. Parses TypeScript with OXC, no type-checking pass.

React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax. > **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete. ## Why `react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system that takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish. OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass: - **Cold extraction, 21 real component libraries:** 50ms ([full breakdown](docs/benchmarks.md)) - **Incremental single-file update:** ~2ms — react-docgen-typescript has no equivalent API; every edit re-pays the full cold cost The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet. ## Install ```bash npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen # CLI, with the prebuilt binary for your platform npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin # Vite plugin cargo install caliper-docgen # CLI from crates.io ``` To build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper cd caliper pnpm install pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi run build:napi # builds the native addon for your platform pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin build ``` Use `pnpm run build:napi`, not a bare `cargo build` — it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s loader expects it. Migrating off `react-docgen-typescript`? See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) for what's compatible today. ## Vite plugin ```ts // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from 'vite' import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react' import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })], }) ``` Metadata is available on the `virtual:caliper-docgen` module and pushed via HMR as components change: ```ts import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen' docgen.components['Button'].props // { // variant: { // type: { kind: 'literalUnion', members: ['default', 'destructive', 'outline'], hasDefault: true }, // required: false, // defaultValue: { value: '"default"', computed: false }, // description: '', // }, // ... // } ``` ## CLI A single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and `--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there. `caliper-docgen` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that execs the platform-appropriate compiled binary — no reimplemented logic, so there's exactly one place CLI behavior can drift. ```bash # Once published: npx caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # From source today: ./target/release/caliper-docgen (after cargo build --release) # One-shot extraction caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # Inspect a single file caliper-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx # Watch mode caliper-docgen watch --src src/ # Shell completions caliper-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_caliper-docgen # Full HTML attribute expansion instead of the default curated subset caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --html-attributes full ``` Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `reactVersion`, `crossPackage`, and more — see `crates/cli/src/config.rs` for the full schema) instead of CLI flags. ## Output shape ```json { "components": { "Button": { "displayName": "Button", "filePath": "src/components/Button.tsx", "props": { "variant": { "type": { "kind": "literalUnion", "members": ["default", "destructive", "outline"], "hasDefault": true }, "required": false, "defaultValue": { "value": "\"default\"", "computed": false }, "description": "Visual style variant.", "tags": {} } }, "inheritance": [ { "typeName": "ButtonHTMLAttributes", "htmlElement": "button", "omitted": [], "totalProps": 147 } ], "notableInherited": { "onClick": { "type": { "kind": "eventHandler", "eventType": "MouseEvent" }, ... }, "disabled": { "type": { "kind": "boolean" }, ... } }, "discriminantProp": null } }, "diagnostics": [], "stats": { "filesParsed": 3, "durationMs": 12, "dtsCacheHits": 2, ... } } ``` ## Supported patterns | Pattern | Example | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | Function components | `function Button(props: ButtonProps)` | | Arrow components | `const Button = (props: ButtonProps) => ...` | | `React.forwardRef` | `forwardRef(...)` | | HOC-wrapped | `styled(Base)` | | Interface inheritance | `interface ButtonProps extends HTMLAttributes` | | Intersection aliases | `type ButtonProps = BaseProps & { variant?: string }` | | `Omit` / `Pick` | `type ButtonProps = Omit` | | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` | | `VariantProps` | `VariantProps` (CVA / TV / PandaCSS) | | Discriminated unions | MUI-style `variant: 'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'standard'` | | JSDoc tags | `@description`, `@default`, `@deprecated`, `@internal` | ## Repository ``` crates/core/ pure extraction logic (no I/O, no async, Send + Sync) crates/binding/ thin NAPI wrapper over core crates/cli/ clap + miette CLI packages/napi/ caliper-docgen-napi (dev binary loader + TS types) packages/vite-plugin/ caliper-docgen-vite-plugin packages/cli/ caliper-docgen (npx wrapper — execs crates/cli's binary, no reimplemented logic) apps/validate/ accuracy comparison harness (react-docgen, rdt, ours) fixtures/ real library .d.ts/.tsx files (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, etc.) ``` ## Contributing [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — setup, code style, commit conventions. [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) — pipeline, modules, key design decisions. ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# caliper-docgen-core

The extraction library behind [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper). It reads React components from TypeScript with [OXC](https://oxc.rs) and reports their props, with no TypeScript compiler program and no type-checking pass.

It parses files in parallel, merges symbols across them, and resolves each component's props. When it can't resolve something it returns a `Diagnostic` instead of failing silently. There is no terminal output and no async, so it embeds cleanly.

Most people want a front end instead: the [`caliper-docgen`](https://crates.io/crates/caliper-docgen) CLI, or the Node bindings [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi).

API docs: [docs.rs/caliper-docgen-core](https://docs.rs/caliper-docgen-core). Architecture and known gaps: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

# caliper-docgen

Extract React component props from the command line. Built on [OXC](https://oxc.rs), so there is no type-checking pass.

```bash
cargo install caliper-docgen
caliper-docgen extract --src src --format rdt
```

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `extract` | Writes every component's props to stdout or `--out` |
| `watch` | Re-extracts on change |
| `inspect <Component>` | Shows one component's props as a table |
| `check` | Exits non-zero on errors, for CI (`--strict` also fails on warnings) |
| `schema` | Prints the JSON Schema of the output |

`--format` is `canonical`, `rdt` (the `react-docgen-typescript` shape) or `toon` (compact, for LLM agents). Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts`, or in the file passed with `--config`.

Prefer npm? `npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen` installs the same binary.

Extraction is in [`caliper-docgen-core`](https://crates.io/crates/caliper-docgen-core). Docs, benchmarks and migration notes: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

[FSL-1.1-MIT](LICENSE). Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.

# caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

A Vite plugin that exposes your React components' props on a virtual module and updates it through HMR as you edit.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

docgen.components['Button'].props
```

Extraction runs on OXC through [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi), so a single-file update takes about 2ms. Requires Vite 7 or 8. The module uses the canonical output format, not the `react-docgen-typescript` shape.

Docs and benchmarks: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

FSL-1.1-MIT. Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.

# caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

A Vite plugin that exposes your React components' props on a virtual module and updates it through HMR as you edit.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

docgen.components['Button'].props
```

Extraction runs on OXC through [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi), so a single-file update takes about 2ms. Requires Vite 7 or 8. The module uses the canonical output format, not the `react-docgen-typescript` shape.

Docs and benchmarks: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

FSL-1.1-MIT. Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.

The license and the README rewrite are both on PR #45 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/45), still a draft. Don't merge it until the 0.2.1 npm publish finishes. I haven't checked #45's CI yet.

**License (FSL-1.1-MIT, like callisto)**
- **Text:** `LICENSE` is callisto's text, "Copyright (c) 2026 Gabriel Castro (Orin DX)".
- **Where applied:** the workspace and every `package.json`, `deny.toml`, and the LICENSE copies in the two published crates.
- **Checks:** `cargo deny check licenses` passes.
- **Published versions:** 0.2.1 and earlier stay AGPL, so 0.2.2 is the first FSL release. The changeset says so.

**READMEs**
- **Root README:** now follows callisto's layout: hero, one bold line, badges, one worked example, one diagram, install, quick start, docs list and a short license section. The old Status banner, output dump, repo tree and marketing-ish lines are gone.
- **Real output:** the worked example uses output I generated from the actual CLI, not invented JSON.
- **Corrections:** the old README's `inspect src/.../Button.tsx` was wrong, because `inspect` takes a component name (`inspect Button --src src`). I also corrected the HTML-attribute default to the curated subset; `--html-attributes full` is what matches `react-docgen-typescript`.
- **Other READMEs:** the five crate and package READMEs are shorter and consistent. I checked their commands and flags against `--help`.
- **`ARCHITECTURE.md`:** I haven't touched it. Restyling it like callisto's is a bigger pass if you want it.

**Release:** the npm publish loop is still going. The CLI platform packages are done, and the log shows it re-running for the `caliper-docgen` owner package at 19:04. After the owner packages, the napi ones follow. I'll report when it finishes or stops.

Yes. The READMEs install fine, but they don't answer the questions a user has after installing. Here is what's missing and what I'd add.

**Gaps**
- **Vite plugin:** the README documents `srcDirs` only. The options type has `exclude`, `reactVersion` (`'react18' | 'react19'`) and `skipHtmlProps` too. It also doesn't say what shape `docgen.components` has or what the HMR payload contains.
- **napi:** the README says it "exposes the extractor" but never names a function or shows a call. `index.d.ts` exports the output types, such as `ComponentEntry`, `ParsedProp`, `PropType` and `Diagnostic`, and none of that is explained.
- **CLI:** no reference for flags like `--src`, `--out`, `--format`, `--html-attributes` (`curated`, `full`, `none`), `--react-version`, `--cache-dir`, `--extra-builtins`, `--no-cross-package`, or the exit codes of `check`.
- **Config:** nothing documents `docgen.config.ts` fields. The only reference is the Rust source.
- **Output:** the root README no longer shows the canonical output shape. `PropType` has about a dozen kinds (literal unions, event handlers, objects, opaque with a reason), and none are explained.
- **`docs/` is internal:** it holds status, edge cases and root-cause notes. Callisto has user guides (`how-callisto-works`, `config`, `errors`) that its README links to; caliper has none.

**One bug found while checking:** the Vite plugin's public options type is still named `OxcDocgenOptions`. My rename missed it because the old name was `OxcDocgen...` rather than `OxcReactDocgen...`. That needs fixing before 0.2.2.

**What I'd add**
1. `docs/cli.md`: commands, flags, exit codes.
2. `docs/config.md`: every `docgen.config.ts` field with defaults.
3. `docs/output.md`: the canonical shape, `PropType` kinds, diagnostics, and how `rdt` differs.
4. `docs/vite-plugin.md` and `docs/node-api.md`: options, the virtual module, and the napi functions with a short example each.
5. Package READMEs that carry their own key options and link to those guides.

I'd write it from the code and `--help`, check each example by running it, and keep the style short. It all goes in #45 or a follow-up, so 0.2.2 ships with real docs.

Do you want me to go ahead, in #45 or a separate PR? A separate PR keeps #45 reviewable.

})() { orin dx } caliper Reads React component props from TypeScript source, without a type checker. build built, unpublished Build from source GitHub { the job } Why Caliper the problem To read props, react-docgen-typescript (RDT) builds a whole TypeScript program. On a design system that takes seconds, and every edit pays it again. what it does Caliper parses with OXC in Rust and resolves props from the syntax tree, file by file, in parallel. What it can’t resolve without a type checker, it marks as opaque and says why. build built, unpublished orin-dx/caliper stage built, unpublished family build source github.com/orin-dx/caliper { get it } Get Caliper Build from source with Rust 1.94 or later. The binary still carries its working name. 01 $ git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper && cd caliper 02 $ cargo build --release -p oxc-react-docgen 03 $ ./target/release/oxc-react-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json { see it } A shadcn Button, read cva variants become literal unions. No type checker involved. The source, trimmed const buttonVariants = cva ( "…" , { 
 variants : {

 } , 
 } )

 extends React . ButtonHTMLAttributes < HTMLButtonElement > ,

 } 
 const Button = React . forwardRef < HTMLButtonElement , ButtonProps > ( … ) The variant prop, from Caliper’s snapshot test "variant" : {

`caliper-docgen` reads your components and reports each one's props: type, required or optional, default, and JSDoc. It is a faster alternative to `react-docgen-typescript` for Storybook, docs sites, and LLM tooling.

`react-docgen-typescript` builds a full TypeScript `Program`, which takes seconds on a mid-size design system. Caliper parses files in parallel with OXC and skips the type checker.

|                                       | Caliper                                | `react-docgen-typescript` |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Cold run, 21 real component libraries | 50ms ([breakdown](docs/benchmarks.md)) | seconds                   |
| Single-file update                    | about 2ms                              | full cold cost            |

- For `caliper-docgen` specifically: one extra child-process spawn on top of that, since the harness shells out to the compiled binary from inside tha

| ------------------------- | -----------------: | ------: | -------: | -----------: |
| `caliper-docgen`          |  2.963 s ± 0.157 s | 2.759 s |  3.208 s |         1.00 |
| `react-docgen`            |  3.387 s ± 0.524 s | 3.046 s |  4.510 s | 1.14× slower |
| `react-docgen-typescript` | 10.374 s ± 1.317 s | 9.196 s | 13.156 s | 3.50× slower |

(hyperfine, 10 runs each, 2 warmup runs)

--- `caliper-docgen` reads your components and reports each one's props: type, required or optional, default, and JSDoc. It is a faster alternative to `react-docgen-typescript` for Storybook, docs sites, and LLM tooling. `react-docgen-typescript` builds a full TypeScript `Program`, which takes seconds on a mid-size design system. - **Homepage:** the crate and npm `homepage` fields now point at https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/, with the GitHub repo as `repository`. The root README links the project page.
- **Benchmarks:** the README claimed "50ms vs seconds", which compared different things. It now quotes the same figures as the site and `docs/benchmarks.md`:

  | Run | Time |
  | --- | --- |
  | Caliper binary alone | 50.5ms |
  | Caliper through the Node harness | 2.96s |
  | `react-docgen` through the Node harness | 3.39s |
  | `react-docgen-typescript` through the Node harness | 10.37s |

**Stale on the site page** (checked against what's live):
- It says "built, unpublished", with "Get Caliper: Build from source". After the release it should say published, with `npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen` and `cargo install caliper-docgen`.
- All five command examples and the build steps use the old name `oxc-react-docgen`, and `cargo build -p oxc-react-docgen` no longer exists. They should be `caliper-docgen`.
- It still says "The binary still carries its working name", which is no longer true.

If you tell me where the site source lives, I can update it once the release lands.

**Release:** the npm loop is at attempt 14, waiting on `caliper-docgen-napi-darwin-x64`, with four more napi platform packages and the three owner packages after that. I haven't started the broader docs pass (CLI, config, output and Vite plugin guides) or the `OxcDocgenOptions` rename; both are waiting on your go-ahead.

2	
3	The extraction library behind [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper). It reads React components from TypeScript with [OXC](https://oxc.rs) and reports their props, with no TypeScript compiler program and no type-checking pass.
4

### Cold extraction, all three tools under equal footing

react-docgen and react-docgen-typescript can only run inside a Node process — there's no "direct binary" form for them to compare against. This second number runs **all three** through the same harness instead (`pnpm exec tsx <script>`, one process per tool, whole corpus per run) — the fairest apples-to-apples comparison available.

Two costs affect all three equally, plus one extra for us:

- A `proto → pnpm → tsx → Node` startup tax, common to all three tools

**Read this pair of numbers together, not separately:**

- The first number (50ms) is what actually happens in a real build.
- The harness-equalized number (2.96s vs 3.39s vs 10.37s) exists only to give react-docgen and react-docgen-typescript a fair shot at the same measurement methodology. Most of those ~3 seconds is Node/tsx/pnpm/proto startup cost, unrelated to any tool's actual extraction logic.
- The **3.5× advantage over react-docgen-typescript holds under either framing**.
- The advantage over react-docgen looks small here only because both numbers are swamped by identical harness overhead — see the per-file numbers below for what's actually happening once that's stripped away.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build identical inputs for all three tools: a filtered mirror of each project's component source.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT=/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp
CORPUS=$ROOT/bench-corpus
OUT=$ROOT/bench-inputs
REPO=/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/release-0.2.0
mkdir -p "$OUT/lists" "$OUT/tsconfigs"

mirror() {
  local name=$1 srcdir=$2
  local dest="$OUT/$name"
  rm -rf "$dest"; mkdir -p "$dest"
  rsync -a --prune-empty-dirs \
    --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='__tests__' --exclude='__snapshots__' --exclude='test' --exclude='tests' \
    --exclude='stories' --exclude='__stories__' --exclude='demo' --exclude='__demo__' --exclude='docs' \
    --exclude='e2e' --exclude='dist' --exclude='build' --exclude='.storybook' --exclude='examples' \
    --exclude='*.test.*' --exclude='*.spec.*' --exclude='*.stories.*' --exclude='*.story.*' --exclude='*.d.ts' \
    --include='*/' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --exclude='*' \
    "$CORPUS/$srcdir/" "$dest/"
  find "$dest" -name '*.tsx' -type f | sort > "$OUT/lists/$name.txt"
  cat > "$OUT/tsconfigs/$name.json" <<EOF
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "noEmit": true, "types": [],
    "paths": {
      "react": ["$REPO/node_modules/@types/react"],
      "react/jsx-runtime": ["$REPO/node_modules/@types/react/jsx-runtime"],
      "react/jsx-dev-runtime": ["$REPO/node_modules/@types/react/jsx-dev-runtime"]
    }
  }
}
EOF
  printf '%-14s ts+tsx files: %-5s component-entry .tsx: %-5s size: %s\n' "$name" \
    "$(find "$dest" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" "$(wc -l < "$OUT/lists/$name.txt" | tr -d ' ')" "$(du -sh "$dest" | cut -f1)"
}

mirror chakra chakra-ui/packages/react/src
mirror shadcn shadcn-ui/apps/v4
mirror antd ant-design/components
mirror spectrum react-spectrum/packages

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Whole-process wall time per tool per project. Plain node scripts (no pnpm/tsx), so startup is ~40ms for everyone.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT=/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp
IN=$ROOT/bench-inputs
RES=$ROOT/bench-results
BIN=/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/release-0.2.0/target/release/caliper-docgen
mkdir -p "$RES"
: > "$RES/counts.tsv"

for NAME in "$@"; do
  echo "=== $NAME $(date -u +%H:%M:%S)"
  # counts (one untimed run each)
  $BIN extract --src "$IN/$NAME" --format canonical --json > "$RES/$NAME.curated.json" 2>/dev/null
  $BIN extract --src "$IN/$NAME" --format canonical --html-attributes full --json > "$RES/$NAME.full.json" 2>/dev/null

  hyperfine -w 2 -r 15 --style basic -N --export-json "$RES/$NAME.caliper-full.time.json" \

  hyperfine -w 1 -r 5 --style basic -N --export-json "$RES/$NAME.rdg.time.json" \

    "node $ROOT/bench/rdt-run.mjs $IN/lists/$NAME.txt $IN/tsconfigs/$NAME.json" > /dev/null 2>&1
done
echo "ALL DONE $(date -u +%H:%M:%S)"

import json, re, sys, os

res = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results'
inp = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'

    try:
        r = json.load(open(path))['results'][0]
        return r['mean'] * 1000, r['stddev'] * 1000
    except Exception:
        return None, None


def caliper_counts(path):
    try:
        raw = open(path).read()
        d = json.loads(raw[raw.index('{'):])
        comps = d['components']
        return len(comps), sum(len(c.get('props', {})) for c in comps.values()), len(d.get('diagnostics', []))
    except Exception:
        return None, None, None


def tool_counts(path):
    try:
        t = open(path).read()
        m = re.search(r'components=(\d+) props=(\d+)', t)
        return int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    except Exception:
        return None, None

    return f'{m:.0f}ms' if m < 1000 else f'{m / 1000:.2f}s'

import json, re

res = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results'
inp = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
names = ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']


def wall(path):
    s = json.load(open(path))['results'][0]['summary']
    return s['time_wall_clock']['mean'] * 1000, s['time_wall_clock']['stddev'] * 1000, s['memory_peak_resident']['mean'] / 1048576


def fmt(ms):
    return f'{ms:.0f}ms' if ms < 1000 else f'{ms / 1000:.2f}s'


def counts_rdt(path):
    raw = open(path).read()
    d = json.loads(raw[raw.index('{'):])
    return len(d), sum(len(c.get('props', {})) for c in d.values())


def counts_canon(path):
    raw = open(path).read()
    d = json.loads(raw[raw.index('{'):])
    return len(d['components']), sum(len(c.get('props', {})) for c in d['components'].values()), len(d.get('diagnostics', []))


def counts_txt(path):
    m = re.search(r'files=(\d+) components=(\d+) props=(\d+)(?: failedFiles=(\d+))?', open(path).read())
    return tuple(int(x) if x else 0 for x in m.groups())


print('### Time (whole process, mean of 15 runs for Caliper, 5 for the Node tools) and peak memory\n')

print('\n### Speedup\n')
print('| Project | vs react-docgen (default) | vs react-docgen-typescript (rdt + full attrs) |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: |')
for n in names:
    cur = wall(f'{res}/{n}.caliper-curated.time.json')[0]
    rf = wall(f'{res}/{n}.caliper-rdtfmt.time.json')[0]
    rdg = wall(f'{res}/{n}.rdg.time.json')[0]

On five large React codebases Caliper is 10 to 37 times faster than the other two tools. The speedup is real, but the tools did different amounts of work, so I'd treat it as an upper bound. The full tables are in `/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results/summary.md`.

**Setup:** Apple M5 Max. I shallow-cloned each project (never executed) and mirrored its `.ts`/`.tsx` source minus tests, stories, demos, docs and `.d.ts` files. All three tools read the same files. I used plain `node` scripts, not `pnpm`/`tsx`, so startup is about 40ms for everyone. Caliper ran 15 times per project and the Node tools 5. `react-docgen-typescript` got all files in one call, which is its fastest mode.

| Project | Files | Caliper | `react-docgen` | `react-docgen-typescript` | Speedup vs RDT | Peak memory (Caliper / RDT) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mantine | 339 | 45ms | 1.27s | 1.27s | 28× | 37 / 451 MB |
| chakra | 126 | 30ms | 484ms | 576ms | 19× | 34 / 301 MB |
| antd | 295 | 51ms | 1.88s | 811ms | 16× | 48 / 392 MB |
| shadcn | 1,240 | 67ms | 1.55s | 1.22s | 18× | 50 / 591 MB |
| spectrum | 1,076 | 121ms | 2.06s | 1.24s | 10× | 78 / 516 MB |

**Caveats:**
- **Different amounts of work.** Caliper produced far fewer props than `react-docgen-typescript`. For shadcn it reported 1,005, against 188,338 for RDT; for Mantine, 682 against 98,000.
  - The projects' dependencies aren't installed, so Caliper left their external types unresolved (434 to 10,852 warnings per project).
  - Mantine's own `ElementProps` helper also doesn't resolve.
  - On the repo's shadcn button in isolation, Caliper does expand to 290 props, so the expansion works when the types resolve.
- **Component counts differ too.** Caliper found 113 components in Mantine, `react-docgen` 314, RDT 394. The counts differ by tool, and I haven't checked which are correct. This measures speed, not accuracy.
- **Missing dependencies cut both ways:** `react-docgen-typescript` also couldn't resolve external packages, so part of its work was skipped too. The comparison is fair on inputs, not on outputs.
- **`react-docgen`** failed on 25 of Mantine's 339 files, which I counted as parse failures.

**What I'd do before publishing any of this:** rerun on two or three projects with dependencies installed (using `--ignore-scripts`, since these are untrusted repos), so every tool resolves the same types. Until then I'd quote the speedup as "10 to 37×, with Caliper resolving less" rather than a headline number. I haven't added any of it to the README or docs. Do you want me to run the installed-dependencies version?

**Release:** the npm loop is on attempt 17. `caliper-docgen-napi-linux-x64-gnu` is visible, with `win32-x64-msvc` and the three owner packages still to go.

import json, re, sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

res = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results'
inp = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
names = ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']
verbose = len(sys.argv) > 1


def clean(name):
    return re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', name)


def own(fileName, root):
    return fileName.startswith(root) and '/node_modules/' not in fileName


tot = Counter()
print('| Project | RDT components with own props | found by Caliper | RDT own props | reported by Caliper | of those: component missing | component found, prop missing | required flag differs |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
examples = {}
for n in names:
    root = f'{inp}/{n}/'
    rdt = json.load(open(f'{res}/{n}.rdt.dump.json'))
    raw = open(f'{res}/{n}.caliper.dump.json').read()
    cal = json.loads(raw[raw.index('{'):])['components']
    cmap = defaultdict(dict)  # (file, name) -> props
    for k, c in cal.items():
        cmap[(c['filePath'], clean(c['displayName']))] = c['props']
    comp_total = comp_found = props_total = props_found = miss_comp = miss_prop = req_diff = 0
    missed = []
    for comp in rdt:
        key = (comp['file'], comp['name'])
        mine = {p: v for p, v in comp['props'].items() if own(v['parent'], root)}
        if not mine:
            continue
        comp_total += 1
        props_total += len(mine)
        got = cmap.get(key)
        if got is None:
            miss_comp += len(mine)
            missed.append((len(mine), comp['name'], comp['file'].replace(root, ''), 'component not found'))
            continue
        comp_found += 1
        lost = [p for p in mine if p not in got]
        miss_prop += len(lost)
        props_found += len(mine) - len(lost)
        for p in mine:
            if p in got and bool(got[p].get('required')) != mine[p]['required']:
                req_diff += 1
        if lost:
            missed.append((len(lost), comp['name'], comp['file'].replace(root, ''), 'props missing: ' + ', '.join(lost[:5])))
    print(f'| {n} | {comp_total} | {comp_found} ({100 * comp_found // max(comp_total, 1)}%) | {props_total} | {props_found} ({100 * props_found // max(props_total, 1)}%) | {miss_comp} | {miss_prop} | {req_diff} |')
    examples[n] = sorted(missed, reverse=True)[:6]
    for k, v in (('comp_total', comp_total), ('comp_found', comp_found), ('props_total', props_total), ('props_found', props_found)):
        tot[k] += v

print()
print(f"All five: {tot['comp_found']}/{tot['comp_total']} components, {tot['props_found']}/{tot['props_total']} own props ({100 * tot['props_found'] // tot['props_total']}%)")
print()
for n in names:
    print(f'Largest gaps, {n}:')
    for count, name, f, why in examples[n]:
        print(f'  {count:3d}  {name:28s} {f[:60]:60s} {why[:80]}')

lastPrompt: But are we reporting the important props or is there critical gaps in the reported output?

content.text:
Yes, there are critical gaps, and they matter more than the speed numbers. When Caliper reports a prop it is accurate, but on some large libraries it misses most components entirely. I compared each tool's output on the same files. The tables are in `/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results/accuracy.md`, with `react-docgen-typescript` as the reference. I counted only props declared in the project's own source, not inherited DOM attributes.

| Project | Components found | Own props reported |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| shadcn | 93% | 91% |
| react-spectrum | 94% | 95% |
| antd | 53% | 40% |
| chakra | 8% | 12% |
| mantine | 11% | 1% |

**What holds up**
- On shadcn and react-spectrum, which use plain `forwardRef`/function components, Caliper covers over 90%.
- Across the 6,475 props it reported for components both tools found, the required flag differed in only 1. I did not compare types, defaults or descriptions.

**What's missing**
- **Mantine:** the library declares most components with `factory<…Factory>()`, `genericFactory<…>()` and similar. Caliper doesn't recognize that pattern, so it misses nearly the whole core, including Select, MultiSelect, TagsInput and NumberInput (about 140 props each). Mantine's own `ElementProps<'button'>` helper also doesn't resolve.
- **Chakra v3:** it finds 8% of components. Even standard `forwardRef` ones come back with props missing (ButtonGroup drops `align`, `justify`, `wrap` and `size`). I didn't dig into why.
- **antd:** the 40% overstates the gap. Much of the miss is helper functions like `genLinkStyle` that RDT counts as components with 237 props each, which are false positives. I did not separate those from real misses.
- **Small misses elsewhere:** shadcn drops `className`/`data-slot` on some sub-components, and spectrum loses props on a few (DateRangePicker).

**Limits of this comparison**
- Dependencies weren't installed, which hurts Caliper's cross-file resolution most.
- RDT's "own props" count is inflated, because Mantine repeats shared style props on every component. So read the component-found column as more reliable than the props column.

**What this means for what we say about speed:** the 10 to 37× numbers hold for libraries like shadcn and react-spectrum, but on Mantine and Chakra part of Caliper's speed comes from skipping components. I wouldn't put a headline speedup in the README until the factory patterns are handled or listed as known gaps in `docs/edge-cases.md`.

**Suggested next steps:** recognize Mantine's factory family (it's a widely used library) and look into the Chakra misses, then rerun this with dependencies installed. I can start with Mantine if you want. I haven't added any of these numbers to the repo.

**Release:** the npm loop is running attempt 18, and `caliper-docgen-napi-win32-x64-msvc` is now visible. Only the three owner packages remain after it.

lastPrompt: Why is it taking so many loops??? That is ridiculous

content.text:
The loops come from npm and callisto interacting badly on brand-new package names. We have 13 new npm packages, and each one costs a run. It is nearly finished now: attempt 20 is publishing the last package, `caliper-docgen-vite-plugin`.

**Why one package per run**
1. npm accepts a first publish of a new package name but takes about two minutes to show it, and says so: "Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available." It also creates a `0.0.0-stage` placeholder in the meantime.
2. Callisto checks the registry seconds after each publish. It retries for only about a minute, then stops with E157 ("published, but does not yet show it").
3. Re-running adopts what landed and publishes the next package, which hits the same wait. Thirteen new names means thirteen cycles, plus the earlier token, tag and secret failures.

**Why it won't repeat:** this only happens the first time a package name is published. From 0.2.2 onward the names exist, so versions should appear within seconds and the verification should pass in one run. I haven't confirmed that, and it is the first thing to check on the next release.

**Why it took so long:** the loop waited for each package to appear before re-running, so each round cost about 2 to 4 minutes. I could have shortened this by publishing the platform packages myself with `npm publish`, but that would bypass callisto's receipt and provenance, so I stayed on its recovery path.

**Upstream issue worth filing:** callisto's verification window is shorter than npm's propagation time for new packages. The retry window should be longer or configurable, and it should keep publishing independent packages instead of stopping at the first lag error.

I'll confirm the receipt and the registries when attempt 20 finishes.

Settings can also live in a `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `reactVersion`, `crossPackage`, and more). `caliper-docgen --help` lists the rest, including `schema` for the JSON Schema of the output.

## Vite plugin

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

docgen.components['Button'].props
```

The module updates through HMR as components change. The plugin and the `caliper-docgen-napi` binding expose the canonical format only, not the `react-docgen-typescript` shape.

## Supported patterns

| Pattern                       | Example                                                           |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Function and arrow components | `function Button(props: ButtonProps)`                             |
| `React.forwardRef`            | `forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(...)`                 |
| Wrapped components            | `styled(Base)<ButtonProps>`                                       |
| Interface inheritance         | `interface ButtonProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>` |
| Intersections, `Omit`, `Pick` | `type ButtonProps = Omit<InputProps, 'value'>`                    |
| `ComponentPropsWithoutRef`    | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>`                              |
| `VariantProps`                | `VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants>` (CVA, TV, PandaCSS)         |
| Discriminated unions          | `variant: 'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'standard'`                   |
| JSDoc tags                    | `@description`, `@default`, `@deprecated`, `@internal`            |

## Documented/by-design limitations (listed for completeness, not new findings)

- Ariakit's `Props<T, O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>` generic pattern is unmatched at the chain level — `composes` stays empty for 6 of the 10 outlier components tracked in `docs/benchmarks.md`. Matches the already-documented gap.
- Mapped types, conditional types, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do — tracked in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` and `rdt-coverage.md`'s known-gaps table.
- Multi-root/monorepo ambient-global (`lib.dom.d.ts` etc.) resolution only inspects `options.src_dirs.first()` — if the first `src_dir` can't resolve `typescript` but a later one could, ambient lookups silently return empty for the whole run. Currently treated
- TOON's format is deliberately lossy relative to canonical JSON (truncated unions, no length cap on descriptions) but this isn't stated in the module's own doc comment — a documentation gap, not a behavior bug.

# 0006. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver, not a leaf patcher

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-09-26

## Context

The structural resolver can't substitute generics through alias chains or evaluate conditional and mapped types. Ten components account for 2,696 of the 2,720 props missing against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) in the 2026-07-25 baseline (`docs/benchmarks.md`). ADR 0004 deferred a fix until TypeScri

TypeScript 7.0 has no programmatic API. 7.1 adds one, available now as `tsc --api` in `typescript@next`. RDT's own algorithm runs on it and returned exactly RDT's props on 13 components (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`).

## Decision

Add an opt-in semantic resolver that runs RDT's algorithm on `tsc --api` and merges its result into the structural one per component. Structural stays the default and the fallback.

- `crates/core` defines an owned-data semantic result and does the merge. It stays free of I/O.
- A feature-gated crate spawns `tsc --api`, speaks its protocol and owns the process. Rust spawns it, in the CLI and the NAPI addon alike. The JS client is not involved.
- We pin an exact `typescript` build and check its version at startup, because the protocol has no version handshake.

## Consequences

- Components the structural resolver can't finish get RDT's prop set without a new heuristic per gap.
- The API is `typescript/unstable/*` and still changing. Pinning limits the damage, but a 7.1 change can force rework.
- The backend costs a process per run, so it is off by default.
- Users need `typescript` 7.1 or later. Without it, extraction still succeeds and emits a diagnostic.
- tsc sees a dependency edit only when told, so `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types don't fit `PropType` losslessly, and `ExtractionOutput` has no schema version. A follow-up ADR decides the representation.

## Alternatives considered

- **Replace `Opaque` leaves with tsc answers** (ADR 0004's model). `OpaqueDetail` holds only a raw string and a reason, and can't be built or inspected outside `crates/core`. Some types resolve to `Named` on purpose with no diagnostic (bare generic parameters, TypeScript utility types), so no leaf m
- **Call the JS client through NAPI.** The CLI is a standalone binary that uses Node only to load `docgen.config.ts`, the binding never calls into JS, and the resolver is synchronous rayon code.
- **Node sidecar**, as `config.rs` does for `docgen.config.ts`. It adds a process hop and a Node dependency. It is the fallback if protocol churn outpaces a Rust client.
- **Vendor typescript-go internals**, as tsgolint does. The repo was closed on 2026-08-20 and the API is the supported surface.
- **TypeScript 7 LSP.** Not evaluated further, because the API exposes each query the algorithm needs directly.
## Mechanism clusters

### 1. Resolver give-up constructor discipline `[corrected]`

**Root cause (narrowed on verification):** the original claim — "6 of ~10 `Opaque` construction sites bypass the named constructor" — overstated the blast radius. Verification found only **3 sites gen

**Mechanism (rewritten — the original was unsound):** the original proposal — make `ResolvedChain`'s bare/`Default` construction private, and restructure `PropType::Opaque { raw, reason }` into a tupl

1. **Reverse-dependency violation.** `known.rs` owns roughly 7 of the real `PropType::Opaque` construction sites and is required by `AGENTS.md`'s "no reverse dependencies" rule to never depend on `res
2. **`ResolvedChain` privacy is close to a non-issue, and harmful if forced.** The struct and its fields are already private to the `resolver` module tree — unreachable from outside `resolver/` today.

**Corrected mechanism:** scope the fix to exactly the 3 confirmed sites. Add a small helper — callable wherever `ResolveState` is already in scope, which all 3 sites qualify for — e.g. `ResolvedChain:

**Resolves:** `resolver-chain-cycle-detected-default`, `resolver-func-multiparam-no-diagnostic`, `resolver-literalunion-as-props-base` (P2 items in `edge-cases.md`).

**ADR:** No — enforcing an existing pattern, not introducing a new one.

### 2. Extractor missing give-up signal channel

**Root cause:** `classify_type_alias`, `extract_type_name_from_type`, and the component-detector `.or_else()` chains in `visit.rs` are `Option`-returning `?`-chains over AST shapes with no way to dist

They're mostly separate. The Mantine misses are two different problems, and only one of them is v1 work.

**1. Components not found: separate, can go first.** `try_forward_ref`, `try_hoc_wrapped` and `try_fc_annotation` in `crates/core/src/extractor/component.rs` all match by callee name or annotation. Mantine's `genericFactory<MultiSelectFactory>((_props) => …)` matches none of them, because the props come from the generic argument, not a typed parameter. `MultiSelectFactory` is `Factory<{ props: MultiSelectProps; ref; … }>`, so the fix is syntactic:
- recognize `factory`, `genericFactory` and `polymorphicFactory` calls with a type argument;
- resolve the alias;
- take the `props` member of the payload.

The semantic backend can't fix this. ADR 0006 merges `tsc`'s answer into components the structural pass already detected, and a component Caliper never found gets no merge. It's a small, self-contained change with its own tests, and the same pass can add other component-factory shapes.

**2. Props not resolved: this is the v1 work.** Where a component is found but its props are incomplete, the cause is the structural resolver, which can't substitute generics through alias chains or evaluate conditional and mapped types. That is what ADR 0006 exists to solve. The probable cases are Mantine's `ElementProps<'input', 'size' | …>` and Chakra's `HTMLChakraProps<'div'>`, but I haven't confirmed either. `crates/tsc-client` exists, and `docs/type-checker-integration.md` lists the lifecycle gates still open.

**Chakra is not diagnosed yet.** It found only 8% of components, and standard `forwardRef` ones came back with props missing. I don't know whether that's detection, resolution or the missing dependencies. It needs a short investigation before I can place it.

**Why the tests didn't catch this:** the repo's validation is 13 hand-picked components and single-file fixtures per library, so it never exercised a whole library the way the benchmark did. A cheap guard is to add a few whole-library checks (say Mantine and Chakra source) with a minimum component-recall threshold in CI.

**Suggested order**
1. Factory-component detection (Mantine), with fixtures taken from Mantine's real declarations.
2. A half-day Chakra diagnosis, to sort it into detection or resolution.
3. A recall check against a whole-library mirror, so regressions show up.

Yes, and the data supports thinking in shapes. About 72% of the misses on the five projects are one shape, not separate library quirks.

**Corrected numbers.** My first comparison counted hooks, `generateMetadata` and style helpers as components. It also failed to match default exports and `displayName` assignments by name. With fairer matching (same file, normalized name or overlapping props, and only PascalCase non-hook names):

| Project | Components found | Declared props reported |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| shadcn | 98% | 93% |
| react-spectrum | 98% | 97% |
| antd | 88% | 81% |
| mantine | 29% | 2% |
| chakra | 9% | 13% |

So antd is mostly fine. The earlier 53% was a matching artifact, and the Mantine and Chakra problem is real but narrower than I first reported.

**The dominant pattern.** A PascalCase constant is initialized by a wrapper call, with the props carried as a type argument:

| Shape | Misses |
| --- | ---: |
| `withContext<…>` and `withRootProvider<…>` (Chakra) | 386 |
| `factory`, `polymorphicFactory`, `genericFactory` (Mantine) | 215 |
| `tableElement<T>`, `createEdgeComponent` | 11 |
| call with no type argument (`createIconLoader`, `lazy`) | 7 |
| plain arrow function | 29 |
| nothing named that in the source (naming and `displayName` mismatches) | 67 |

**The fix is a rule, not a list of names.** A wrapper-call detector:
- It looks for a PascalCase `const X = someCall<…>(…)` and takes the props from whichever type argument resolves to an object type with members. It also handles the payload form, where the props are in a `props` member of an object type argument (Mantine's `Factory<{ props: X }>`).
- It excludes known non-component creators (`createContext`, `useRef`, `createStore`) and requires `.tsx`.
- Every inferred component emits a diagnostic naming the wrapper, so nothing is silent.
- A `docgen.config.ts` entry, e.g. `componentWrappers`, says where the props type is for wrappers the rule gets wrong.

The semantic backend (v1) is for the cases with no type argument, like `createIconLoader("x")`, where the props come from the callee's return type.

**Making it stick:**
1. One small fixture per declaration shape, taken from the real libraries, each with a snapshot test.
2. A repeatable "whole-library recall" script (the one I just wrote) that classifies misses by shape. Run it when adding a library, and gate on a recall threshold.

**Left open:** the 29 plain arrow functions and the 67 name mismatches. They're small, but they're standard shapes, so I'd look at them next.

**A correction owed:** #45 already merged with my earlier figures in `docs/edge-cases.md` (Mantine 11%, Chakra 8%, antd's shape missing). The README caveat is still accurate but the edge-cases numbers are now wrong. I'd fix that in the PR that adds the wrapper detector, with the revised counts above.

Want me to start the wrapper detector on a branch?

<overview>
Vanguard builds a documented evidence base before committing to a solution direction. It separates what is known from what is assumed, surfaces contradictions, and delivers a recommendation a spec writer can act on directly.

One skill, one pipeline — not a menu of separately-invokable modes. `recon` maps sources (internal specs/docs/code, dependency manifests, external references), `reader` reads only what the map points at, `synthesizer` resolves the findings into one report, `risk-assessor` reviews the resulting approach. | **risk-assessor** | Risk prioritizer | sonnet / medium | Given a proposed approach or research-report@1, identifies and prioritizes technical risks with mitigations. |
