1	# Pipeline orchestration
2	
3	**Source:** `crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs`, `crates/core/src/pipeline/discover.rs`, `crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs`, `crates/core/src/cache.rs`, `crates/core/src/import_map.rs`, `crates/core/src/panic_guard.rs`, `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`
4	
5	This is the orchestration layer: it owns nothing about _how_ a component is parsed or resolved (that's `extractor/` and `resolver/`), only _when_ and _in what order_ files get discovered, parsed, merged, and resolved, and how failures at any step degrade instead of propagating.
6	
7	## The 6-phase data flow
8	
9	`extract_with_global()` (`pipeline/mod.rs:223`) is the single implementation shared by both `extract()` (cold, one-shot) and `WatchSession::initialize()` (the first run inside a watch session). Every phase below runs exactly once per call:
10	
11	- **Phase 0 — validate.** Checks `options.src_dirs` isn't empty and that at least one entry exists on disk. Sequential, trivial cost. Exists specifically so a typo'd `--src` produces an `Error` diagnostic instead of a silent zero-component, zero-diagnostic run (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6).
12	- **Phase 1 — discover.** `discover_files()` walks `src_dirs` via the `ignore` crate, filters to `.ts`/`.tsx`, applies built-in and user excludes, canonicalizes each path, then sorts and dedups. Sequential — it's I/O-bound directory walking, not CPU work worth parallelizing, and the final sort is required for the determinism invariant below.
13	- **Phase 2 — parse (parallel).** `src_files.par_iter().map(...)` via rayon. Each file either hits the `.d.ts` cache or gets parsed fresh by `extractor::parse_file`. This is the phase worth parallelizing: OXC parsing is pure CPU work, one file is fully independent of another, and this is typically the dominant cost of a run. Every closure body is wrapped in `panic_guard::contain_panic`.
14	- **Phase 3 — merge (+3.5/3.6), sequential.** Each file's `SourceData` (plus any plugin `on_file_extracted` mutation) is folded into one `GlobalSourceData` via hash-map insertions. This phase is sequential specifically because it's cheap (hash-map inserts, not real work) and because `GlobalSourceData` is a single shared structure being built incrementally — parallelizing it would require synchronization that costs more than the merge itself. Phase 3.5 (Full HTML-attribute mode) and Phase 3.6 (ambient TS lib files) extend the same merge with `@types/react` and `lib.es5.d.ts`/`lib.dom.d.ts`, both going through `merge_cached_dts_file` so their diagnostics aren't dropped (see Invariant 3).
15	- **Phase 4 — resolve (parallel).** `mappings.par_iter().map(|m| resolve_component(m, &ctx))`, again via rayon, again each closure wrapped in `contain_panic`. `ResolutionContext` wraps `Arc<GlobalSourceData>` so every thread reads the same immutable snapshot; per this crate's `AGENTS.md`, all resolver inputs must be owned or `Arc`-wrapped since rayon may run this on any thread.
16	- **Phase 5 — collect/dedup/serialize.** Sequential fold of `(ComponentEntry, Vec<Diagnostic>)` pairs into the output `BTreeMap`, running the display-name collision/disambiguation logic (Invariant 1) and each plugin's `on_component_resolved` hook, then persisting the DTS cache and building `ExtractionStats`.
17	
18	**Why parallel exactly at phases 2 and 4, nowhere else:** those are the only two phases doing embarrassingly-parallel, side-effect-free-per-item CPU work over an already-known-size collection. Discovery is I/O-walk-bound: merge and collect both build one shared structure incrementally, which is cheaper done sequentially than synchronized.
19	
20	## Watch mode's incremental model
21	
22	`WatchSession` (`pipeline/watch.rs`) keeps `global` (`ArcSwap<GlobalSourceData>`), `reverse_deps` (`ArcSwap<ReverseDeps>`), and `component_cache: DashMap<String, ComponentEntry>` alive across many `update_file()` calls. `initialize()` runs one full cold `extract_with_global(options, true)`. `initialize()` is idempotent under a `Mutex<bool>` guard, with `.unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` recovering from a poisoned lock rather than propagating a second panic (ADR 0005, "defense in depth").
23	
24	`update_file(changed)` does _not_ rerun the 6-phase pipeline. It:
25	
26	1. Re-parses only `changed`.
27	2. Patches `global` via `ArcSwap::rcu` (read-copy-update) — `remove_file` then `merge`, retried automatically if another `update_file` call raced the swap.
28	3. Looks up `reverse_deps.affected(changed)` — a BFS over the reverse import graph — to find every file transitively affected by this one change.
29	4. Re-resolves only the `ComponentMapping`s belonging to affected files, in parallel, against the freshly-swapped `global`.
30	5. Replaces (not appends) this file's diagnostics in a `DashMap<Utf8PathBuf, Vec<Diagnostic>>`, so a since-fixed error doesn't linger in `snapshot()` forever.
31	
32	`ReverseDeps` is built once at `initialize()` time from `global.import_map`, by string-appending each relative import specifier onto its consuming file's parent directory and probing `.ts`/`.tsx`/`/index.ts`/`/index.tsx` suffixes with no filesystem I/O (an approximation, not a real resolve). **It is never rebuilt within a session** — see Known Gaps below.
33	
34	## Key types (verbatim)
35	
36	```rust
37	pub struct ReverseDeps {
38	    pub(super) inner: FxHashMap<Utf8PathBuf, Vec<Utf8PathBuf>>,
39	}
40	```
41	
42	```rust
43	pub struct WatchSession {
44	    pub options: PipelineOptions,
45	    pub global: ArcSwap<GlobalSourceData>,
46	    pub reverse_deps: ArcSwap<ReverseDeps>,
47	    pub component_cache: DashMap<String, ComponentEntry>,
48	    pub diagnostics: DashMap<Utf8PathBuf, Vec<Diagnostic>>,
49	    ambient_global_files: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<Utf8PathBuf>>,
50	    initialized: Mutex<bool>,
51	}
52	```
53	
54	```rust
55	pub fn contain_panic<T>(label: &str, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, Diagnostic>
56	```
57	
58	```rust
59	pub trait DocgenPlugin: Send + Sync {
60	    fn name(&self) -> &str;
61	    fn on_file_extracted(&self, _file_path: &camino::Utf8Path, _data: &mut SourceData) {}
62	    fn on_component_resolved(&self, _entry: &mut ComponentEntry) {}
63	}
64	```
65	
66	## Invariants
67	
68	1. **Component output keys are `display_name`, disambiguated to `"{name} ({file_path})"` on the 2nd+ occurrence of that name — this still collides for a genuine 3-way-or-more same-name-same-file duplicate.** Phase 5 tracks a `seen_names: HashMap<String, u32>` counter per base name; the _first_ occurrence gets the bare name, every later occurrence gets the disambiguated key. Since `file_path` is unique per file, two different libraries shipping a same-named `Button.tsx` never collide (each gets a distinct disambiguated key) — but three or more literal duplicate declarations of the same component in the _same file_ (`function Button() {}` repeated) all key identically after the first, and `components.insert` silently overwrites unless its `Option<ComponentEntry>` return is checked. It is checked (see `pipeline/mod.rs:456`), which is what turns this residual case into a `ComponentKeyCollision` diagnostic rather than a silent drop — but the entry itself is still lost from the map, only the _fact_ of the loss is preserved. See `test_duplicate_component_declarations_in_one_file_emit_a_collision_diagnostic`.
69	
70	2. **`discover_files` must dedup identical canonical paths _before_ they become separate `ComponentMapping`s — the Phase-5 collision check alone cannot catch a 2-directory overlap.** Two overlapping `src_dirs` (e.g. `["./src", "./src/components"]`) walk the same physical file twice. Because the two resulting mappings key _differently_ under Invariant 1's numbering scheme (first occurrence → bare name, second → disambiguated name), they never collide at `insert` and would both silently appear as separate output entries. The actual fix is the `files.sort(); files.dedup();` at the end of `discover_files` (`discover.rs:94-95`), which only works because every path was canonicalized first — an uncanonicalized relative/absolute duplicate pair would sort non-adjacently and evade `dedup()`. See `test_overlapping_src_dirs_two_directories_deduplicates_without_a_duplicate_listing`.
71	
72	3. **Every `.d.ts` merge into `GlobalSourceData` — main-loop, Full-mode `@types/react`, and ambient lib.d.ts — must drain the parsed file's own diagnostics before merging, because `GlobalSourceData` itself has no diagnostics field to catch them later.** Phase 3.5/3.6 route through the shared `merge_cached_dts_file` helper specifically to guarantee this; calling `global.merge()` directly on freshly-parsed data (as Phase 3.5/3.6 originally did) silently drops any excessive-nesting or parse-error diagnostic the extractor raised while parsing that file. See `merge_cached_dts_file_does_not_drop_parse_diagnostics`.
73	
74	4. **Discovery output is deterministic across OS/filesystem: sorted, deduplicated, and canonicalized.** This is load-bearing for two independent reasons: diagnostic ordering and dedup-winner-selection in Phase 5 are reproducible only because rayon's `.collect()` on a `par_iter()` preserves input order and the sequential merge/resolve phases iterate that same order; and `parent.fileName` in resolver output would otherwise differ depending on whether `--src` was given relative or absolute, or what the invocation cwd was.
75	
76	5. **`ReverseDeps` is built once, at `WatchSession::initialize()`, from a fully-merged `GlobalSourceData` — never partially, never mid-session.** `ReverseDeps::build` needs `global.import_map` to already reflect Phase 3.5/3.6's merges (ambient globals, `@types/react`) to be complete; building it from a hand-rolled partial `GlobalSourceData` (a bug this code carried previously — see the doc comment on `extract_with_global`) silently produced an incomplete reverse graph that `update_file`'s BFS then propagated changes through incorrectly.
77	
78	6. **A cache-persistence failure (`DtsCache::save_to_disk`) must degrade to `DiagnosticSeverity::Info`, never `Warning`.** `Warning` would flip `docgen check --strict`'s exit code to 1 purely because the _next_ run will have to re-parse `.d.ts` files — extraction output for _this_ run is completely correct either way. This is a deliberate severity choice, not an oversight; the comment at `cache.rs:143-148` explicitly calls out this is the same class of spurious exit-code flip already fixed once elsewhere in the resolver.
79	
80	7. **Anything reachable from a rayon `.map()` closure or a `DocgenPlugin` hook call must be wrapped in `panic_guard::contain_panic`, individually, per item — not once around the whole batch.** The `.map()` closures at Phase 2 and Phase 4 wrap their _entire bodies_; `PluginRegistry::run_on_file_extracted`/`run_on_component_resolved` wrap _each individual plugin call_, not the surrounding loop, so one misbehaving plugin degrades only itself and every other registered plugin still runs (see `a_panicking_plugin_is_contained_and_tagged_with_its_name_others_still_run`). Violating the per-item granularity (e.g. wrapping the whole `.collect()` instead of each closure invocation) reintroduces the exact failure mode ADR 0005 was written to close: one bad file/plugin/component poisons the whole batch.
81	
82	8. **`update_file`'s `changed` path must be canonicalized the same way `discover_files` canonicalizes at cold-start, or the reverse-dependency lookup silently finds nothing.** `discover_files` resolves symlinks via the `ignore` walker (e.g. macOS's `/var` → `/private/var`), so every key already stored in `global`/`reverse_deps` is in that resolved form. A raw file-watcher-reported path that skips `canonicalize_best_effort` looks up the wrong key in `reverse_deps.affected()` and returns an empty affected-set with no error at all — not a crash, a silent under-update.
83	
84	## Locked design decisions
85	
86	- **Two rayon parallel phases, everything else sequential.** Already covered above under "the 6-phase data flow" — restated here because it's the decision most likely to look "obviously improvable" by parallelizing merge/collect too. Don't: both are cheap relative to parse/resolve, and both build one shared mutable structure whose synchronization cost would exceed the sequential cost.
87	- **DTS cache keys on `(path, size, mtime_ns)`, not a content hash.** A cheap stat-only check is the entire point of this cache's speed advantage; a content hash closes the residual staleness gap (Known Gaps below) but was deliberately rejected as disproportionate to the problem's real frequency — see `cache.rs:196-204`'s doc comment and `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` line 140, which additionally notes that _if_ this is ever revisited, a fast non-cryptographic hash (xxhash/CRC) over bytes already being read for size would be the right scope, not a full cryptographic hash.
88	- **`contain_panic` uses `AssertUnwindSafe` internally, not at call sites.** Plugin hooks pass `&mut SourceData`/`&mut ComponentEntry`, and `&mut T` is unconditionally `!UnwindSafe` in std — requiring callers to prove unwind-safety themselves would make every call site either not compile or need its own `AssertUnwindSafe`. The justification is structural, not incidental: `SourceData`/`ComponentEntry` have no interior mutability (`Cell`/`RefCell`), so a caught panic mid-operation can't leave an observably-torn half-write behind — the whole operation's output is simply discarded. See ADR 0005 and `panic_guard.rs:14-19`.
89	- **`ComponentMapping`/`GlobalSourceData` construction happens once per cold run and is reused, immutable, across all of Phase 4's parallel resolve closures via `Arc`.** `ResolutionContext::new(global.clone(), options)` wraps the `Arc<GlobalSourceData>` once outside the `par_iter()`, not per-item — this is the mechanism that makes "all resolver inputs must be owned or `Arc`-wrapped" (crates/core/AGENTS.md) actually cheap rather than merely correct.
90	- **Plugin hooks are two narrow extension points (`on_file_extracted`, `on_component_resolved`), not a general AST-transform API.** Deliberately modeled after `michi`'s zero-dep trait pattern and `callisto`'s modular design (see `plugin.rs`'s module doc) — the hook surface is intentionally small so panic-containment and ordering guarantees stay easy to reason about per plugin.
91	
92	## Known gaps
93	
94	Cross-referencing `docs/edge-cases.md` and `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` for pipeline-specific findings — fixed vs. still open:
95	
96	**Fixed** (all have regression tests in `pipeline/mod.rs`'s test module):
97	
98	- Permission-denied subtrees and non-UTF8 filenames silently dropped during discovery — now surfaced as `IoError` diagnostics (`discover.rs`).
99	- Empty `src_dirs` bypassing the "missing dirs" diagnostic due to a `!is_empty()` boolean-logic bug — now its own distinct diagnostic message.
100	- Component-key collisions and overlapping-`src_dirs` duplication — see Invariants 1 and 2.
101	- No panic-containment anywhere in the repo — closed by ADR 0005 / `panic_guard.rs`, covering rayon closures, plugin hooks, and (per the ADR) NAPI entry points.
102	- `WatchSession::initialize()` previously hand-rebuilt `GlobalSourceData`, skipping Phase 3.5/3.6 merges — fixed by routing through the same `extract_with_global` the cold path uses (see Invariant 5 and the doc comment at `pipeline/mod.rs:212-222`).
103	- Phase 3.5/3.6 dropping parse diagnostics on direct `global.merge()` calls — see Invariant 3.
104	
105	**Still open** (deliberately deferred, not oversights):
106	
107	- **DTS cache mtime+size staleness on coarse-resolution filesystems** (`docs/edge-cases.md` P0-2, `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` line 140). An edit landing in the same tick as a prior write _and_ producing an identical file length is served a stale cache hit. Scoped to `.d.ts` files only; not recommended for immediate action per the root-cause doc — see the Locked Design Decisions entry above for what a future fix should look like if ever revisited.
108	- **`ReverseDeps` is not incrementally updated within a watch session.** Only structural changes (a new `WatchSession`, i.e. restarting) rebuild it; adding or removing an import inside an existing file during a session leaves the reverse graph stale for that edge until the session restarts. This is stated directly in the `WatchSession` doc comment (`watch.rs:41-46`) as a known limitation, not derived from the edge-cases audit.
109	- **`watch --out` write failures are silently discarded** and writes are non-atomic (`docs/edge-cases.md` line 72-73; `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` line 139). This is CLI-layer (`cli/commands/watch.rs`), outside this subsystem's scope (`crates/core` non-negotiable #6 doesn't reach the CLI), but it directly affects how trustworthy `WatchSession`'s output is once it leaves this module.
110	- **LSP `Content-Length` header has no upper bound before allocation** (`docs/edge-cases.md` P1-2) — CLI-layer (`cli/commands/lsp.rs`), noted here only because it's adjacent to watch-mode's session lifecycle, not because it's part of this subsystem.

Because the two resulting mappings key _differently_ under Invariant 1's numbering scheme (first occurrence → bare name, second → disambiguated name), they never collide at `insert` and would both silently appear as separate output entries. The actual fix is the `files.sort(); files.dedup();` at the end of `discover_files` (`discover.rs:94-95`), which only works because every path was canonicalized first — an uncanonicalized relative/absolute duplicate pair would sort non-adjacently and evade `dedup()`. See `test_overlapping_src_dirs_two_directories_deduplicates_without_a_duplicate_listing`.

3. **Every `.d.ts` merge into `GlobalSourceData` — main-loop, Full-mode `@types/react`, and ambient lib.d.ts — must drain the parsed file's own diagnostics before merging, because `GlobalSourceData` itself has no diagnostics field to catch them later.** Phase 3.5/3.6 route through the shared `merge_cached_dts_file` helper specifically to guarantee this; calling `global.merge()` directly on freshly-parsed data (as Phase 3.5/3.6 originally did) silently drops any excessive-nesting or parse-error diagnostic the extractor raised while parsing that file. See `merge_cached_dts_file_does_not_drop_parse_diagnostics`.

4. **Discovery output is deterministic across OS/filesystem: sorted, deduplicated, and canonicalized.** This is load-bearing for two independent reasons: diagnostic ordering and dedup-winner-selection in Phase 5 are reproducible only because rayon's `.collect()` on a `par_iter()` preserves input order and the sequential merge/resolve phases iterate that same order; and `parent.fileName` in resolver output would otherwise differ depending on whether `--src` was given relative or absolute, or what the invocation cwd was.

5. **`ReverseDeps` is built once, at `WatchSession::initialize()`, from a fully-merged `GlobalSourceData` — never partially, never mid-session.** `ReverseDeps::build` needs `global.import_map` to already reflect Phase 3.5/3.6's merges (ambient globals, `@types/react`) to be complete; building it from a hand-rolled partial `GlobalSourceData` (a bug this code carried previously — see the doc comment on `extract_with_global`) silently produced an incomplete reverse graph that `update_file`'s BFS then propagated changes through incorrectly.

6. **A cache-persistence failure (`DtsCache::save_to_disk`) must degrade to `DiagnosticSeverity::Info`, never `Warning`.** `Warning` would flip `docgen check --strict`'s exit code to 1 purely because the _next_ run will have to re-parse `.d.ts` files — extraction output for _this_ run is completely correct either way. This is a deliberate severity choice, not an oversight; the comment at `cache.rs:143-148` explicitly calls out this is the same class of spurious exit-code flip already fixed once elsewhere in the resolver.

7. **Anything reachable from a rayon `.map()` closure or a `DocgenPlugin` hook call must be wrapped in `panic_guard::contain_panic`, individually, per item — not once around the whole batch.** The `.map()` closures at Phase 2 and Phase 4 wrap their _entire bodies_; `PluginRegistry::run_on_file_extracted`/`run_on_component_resolved` wrap _each individual plugin call_, not the surrounding loop, so one misbehaving plugin degrades only itself and every other registered plugin still runs (see `a_panicking_plugin_is_contained_and_tagged_with_its_name_others_still_run`). Violating the per-item granularity (e.g. wrapping the whole `.collect()` instead of each closure invocation) reintroduces the exact failure mode ADR 0005 was written to close: one bad file/plugin/component poisons the whole batch.

8. **`update_file`'s `changed` path must be canonicalized the same way `discover_files` canonicalizes at cold-start, or the reverse-dependency lookup silently finds nothing.** `discover_files` resolves symlinks via the `ignore` walker (e.g. macOS's `/var` → `/private/var`), so every key already stored in `global`/`reverse_deps` is in that resolved form. ## Locked design decisions

- **Two rayon parallel phases, everything else sequential.** Already covered above under "the 6-phase data flow" — restated here because it's the decision most likely to look "obviously improvable" by parallelizing merge/collect too. Don't: both are cheap relative to parse/resolve, and both build one shared mutable structure whose synchronization cost would exceed the sequential cost.
- **DTS cache keys on `(path, size, mtime_ns)`, not a content hash.** A cheap stat-only check is the entire point of this cache's speed advantage; a content hash closes the residual staleness gap (Known Gaps below) but was deliberately rejected as disproportionate to the problem's real frequency — see `cache.rs:196-204`'s doc comment and `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` line 140, which additionally notes that _if_ this is ever revisited, a fast non-cryptographic hash (xxhash/CRC) over bytes already being read for size would be the right scope, not a full cryptographic hash.
- **`contain_panic` uses `AssertUnwindSafe` internally, not at call sites.** Plugin hooks pass `&mut SourceData`/`&mut ComponentEntry`, and `&mut T` is unconditionally `!UnwindSafe` in std — requiring callers to prove unwind-safety themselves would make every call site either not compile or need its own `AssertUnwindSafe`. The justification is structural, not incidental: `SourceData`/`ComponentEntry` have no interior mutability (`Cell`/`RefCell`), so a caught panic mid-operation can't leave an observably-torn half-write behind — the whole operation's output is simply discarded. See ADR 0005 and `panic_guard.rs:14-19`.
- **`ComponentMapping`/`GlobalSourceData` construction happens once per cold run and is reused, immutable, across all of Phase 4's parallel resolve closures via `Arc`.** `ResolutionContext::new(global.clone(), options)` wraps the `Arc<GlobalSourceData>` once outside the `par_iter()`, not per-item — this is the mechanism that makes "all resolver inputs must be owned or `Arc`-wrapped" (crates/core/AGENTS.md) actually cheap rather than merely correct.
- **Plugin hooks are two narrow extension points (`on_file_extracted`, `on_component_resolved`), not a general AST-transform API.** Deliberately modeled after `michi`'s zero-dep trait pattern and `callisto`'s modular design (see `plugin.rs`'s module doc) — the hook surface is intentionally small so panic-containment and ordering guarantees stay easy to reason about per plugin.

Cross-referencing `docs/edge-cases.md` and `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` for pipeline-specific findings — fixed vs. still open:

**Fixed** (all have regression tests in `pipeline/mod.rs`'s test module):

- Permission-denied subtrees and non-UTF8 filenames silently dropped during discovery — now surfaced as `IoError` diagnostics (`discover.rs`).
- Empty `src_dirs` bypassing the "missing dirs" diagnostic due to a `!is_empty()` boolean-logic bug — now its own distinct diagnostic message.
- Component-key collisions and overlapping-`src_dirs` duplication — see Invariants 1 and 2.
- No panic-containment anywhere in the repo — closed by ADR 0005 / `panic_guard.rs`, covering rayon closures, plugin hooks, and (per the ADR) NAPI entry points.
- `WatchSession::initialize()` previously hand-rebuilt `GlobalSourceData`, skipping Phase 3.5/3.6 merges — fixed by routing through the same `extract_with_global` the cold path uses (see Invariant 5 and the doc comment at `pipeline/mod.rs:212-222`).
- Phase 3.5/3.6 dropping parse diagnostics on direct `global.merge()` calls — see Invariant 3.

**Still open** (deliberately deferred, not oversights):

- **DTS cache mtime+size staleness on coarse-resolution filesystems** (`docs/edge-cases.md` P0-2, `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` line 140). An edit landing in the same tick as a prior write _and_ producing an identical file length is served a stale cache hit. Scoped to `.d.ts` files only; not recommended for immediate action per the root-cause doc — see the Locked Design Decisions entry above for what a future fix should look like if ever revisited.
- **`ReverseDeps` is not incrementally updated within a watch session.** Only structural changes (a new `WatchSession`, i.e. restarting) rebuild it; adding or removing an import inside an existing file during a session leaves the reverse graph stale for that edge until the session restarts. This is stated directly in the `WatchSession` doc comment (`watch.rs:41-46`) as a known limitation, not derived from the edge-cases audit.
- **`watch --out` write failures are silently discarded** and writes are non-atomic (`docs/edge-cases.md` line 72-73; `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` line 139). This is CLI-layer (`cli/commands/watch.rs`), outside this subsystem's scope (`crates/core` non-negotiable #6 doesn't reach the CLI), but it directly affects how trustworthy `WatchSession`'s output is once it leaves this module.
- **LSP `Content-Length` header has no upper bound before allocation** (`docs/edge-cases.md` P1-2) — CLI-layer (`cli/commands/lsp.rs`), noted here only because it's adjacent to watch-mode's session lifecycle, not because it's part of this subsystem.

Each `parse_file()` call gets its own OXC allocator. No AST node escapes the function — all extracted data is owned, heap-allocated types. This is what makes the rayon parallelism safe.

The watch path reuses analysis across file changes. A single-file update calls `parse_file()` on the changed file and re-resolves only the affected components.

The current `WatchSession` publishes related state through separate containers: `ArcSwap<GlobalSourceData>`, `ArcSwap<ReverseDeps>`, a mutex-protected named-type index, and `DashMap`s for source data, components, and diagnostics. Individual updates are synchronized, but `snapshot()` can combine values from different moments because there is no aggregate revision identity or single publication point. Create/delete/rename also remains a documented session-rebuild path.

### Target watch publication invariant

Move all query-visible watch state into one immutable `WatchRevision`: global source data, named-type indexes, component cache, diagnostics, and revision/content identity. An update builds the replacement off to the side and publishes one `Arc<WatchRevision>` only after every stage succeeds. A failed update leaves the prior complete revision published.

Gate that target with clean/incremental equivalence. Generated modify, edit-revert, repeated-edit, and session-rebuild create/delete/rename sequences must produce the same canonical components, enums, resolution outcomes, and diagnostics as a fresh extraction over the resulting files. Concurrent tests must prove readers receive an old-complete or new-complete revision, never a mixture. Per-run timing counters are excluded from canonical comparison.

1	# Pipeline orchestration
2	
3	**Source:** `crates/core/src/pipeline/mod.rs`, `crates/core/src/pipeline/discover.rs`, `crates/core/src/pipeline/watch.rs`, `crates/core/src/cache.rs`, `crates/core/src/import_map.rs`, `crates/core/src/panic_guard.rs`, `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`
4	
5	This is the orchestration layer: it owns nothing about _how_ a component is parsed or resolved (that's `extractor/` and `resolver/`), only _when_ and _in what order_ files get discovered, parsed, merged, and resolved, and how failures at any step degrade instead of propagating.
6	
7	## The 6-phase data flow
8	
9	`extract_with_global()` (`pipeline/mod.rs:223`) is the single implementation shared by both `extract()` (cold, one-shot) and `WatchSession::initialize()` (the first run inside a watch session). Every phase below runs exactly once per call:
10	
11	- **Phase 0 — validate.** Checks `options.src_dirs` isn't empty and that at least one entry exists on disk. Sequential, trivial cost. Exists specifically so a typo'd `--src` produces an `Error` diagnostic instead of a silent zero-component, zero-diagnostic run (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6).
12	- **Phase 1 — discover.** `discover_files()` walks `src_dirs` via the `ignore` crate, filters to `.ts`/`.tsx`, applies built-in and user excludes, canonicalizes each path, then sorts and dedups. Sequential — it's I/O-bound directory walking, not CPU work worth parallelizing, and the final sort is required for the determinism invariant below.
13	- **Phase 2 — parse (parallel).** `src_files.par_iter().map(...)` via rayon. Each file either hits the `.d.ts` cache or gets parsed fresh by `extractor::parse_file`. This is the phase worth parallelizing: OXC parsing is pure CPU work, one file is fully independent of another, and this is typically the dominant cost of a run. Every closure body is wrapped in `panic_guard::contain_panic`.
14	- **Phase 3 — merge (+3.5/3.6), sequential.** Each file's `SourceData` (plus any plugin `on_file_extracted` mutation) is folded into one `GlobalSourceData` via hash-map insertions. This phase is sequential specifically because it's cheap (hash-map inserts, not real work) and because `GlobalSourceData` is a single shared structure being built incrementally — parallelizing it would require synchronization that costs more than the merge itself. Phase 3.5 (Full HTML-attribute mode) and Phase 3.6 (ambient TS lib files) extend the same merge with `@types/react` and `lib.es5.d.ts`/`lib.dom.d.ts`, both going through `merge_cached_dts_file` so their diagnostics aren't dropped (see Invariant 3).
15	- **Phase 4 — resolve (parallel).** `mappings.par_iter().map(|m| resolve_component(m, &ctx))`, again via rayon, again each closure wrapped in `contain_panic`. `ResolutionContext` wraps `Arc<GlobalSourceData>` so every thread reads the same immutable snapshot; per this crate's `AGENTS.md`, all resolver inputs must be owned or `Arc`-wrapped since rayon may run this on any thread.
16	- **Phase 5 — collect/dedup/serialize.** Sequential fold of `(ComponentEntry, Vec<Diagnostic>)` pairs into the output `BTreeMap`, running the display-name collision/disambiguation logic (Invariant 1) and each plugin's `on_component_resolved` hook, then persisting the DTS cache and building `ExtractionStats`.
17	
18	**Why parallel exactly at phases 2 and 4, nowhere else:** those are the only two phases doing embarrassingly-parallel, side-effect-free-per-item CPU work over an already-known-size collection. Discovery is I/O-walk-bound: merge and collect both build one shared structure incrementally, which is cheaper done sequentially than synchronized.
19	
20	## Watch mode's incremental model
21	
22	`WatchSession` (`pipeline/watch.rs`) keeps `global` (`ArcSwap<GlobalSourceData>`), `reverse_deps` (`ArcSwap<ReverseDeps>`), and `component_cache: DashMap<String, ComponentEntry>` alive across many `update_file()` calls. `initialize()` runs one full cold `extract_with_global(options, true)`. `initialize()` is idempotent under a `Mutex<bool>` guard, with `.unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` recovering from a poisoned lock rather than propagating a second panic (ADR 0005, "defense in depth").
23	
24	`update_file(changed)` does _not_ rerun the 6-phase pipeline. It:
25

- **Watch output equals a cold extract.** After any edit, creation, rename or deletion, a watch session's snapshot has the same components, enums and diagnostics as `extract` over the same files. Before, edits to a dependency reached through a barrel or a `../` import were missed, deleted files' components stayed until restart, excluded files such as stories added components, a disambiguated component's edit could land under another component's key, and the first run's diagnostics were dropped from later snapshots.
- **Precise re-resolution.** Each component records the files, project-wide names and module resolutions its props depended on; a change re-resolves exactly the components it can affect.
- **`IncrementalUpdate` gains `revision`, `updatedKeys` and `removedKeys`,** so a consumer can apply an update to a keyed map and drop removed entries.

- Resolve diagnostics are ordered by file and source position.

Stacked on #74. Part 1 of 3 for the watch-mode findings in the v1 review (core). The CLI and Vite/NAPI fixes follow as separate stacked PRs.

## Problem

Watch mode kept its own state in separate containers and re-resolved by a string-built reverse import graph. Verified defects:

- Edits to a dependency reached through a barrel or a `../` import never reached the component.
- New import edges added mid-session were never tracked.
- Deleted files' components stayed until restart.
- Excluded files (stories, tests) added components.
- A disambiguated component's edit could land under another component's key.
- The first run's diagnostics were missing from later snapshots.
- A snapshot could mix state from two updates.

## Change

- **One revision type.** `pipeline/revision.rs` owns the cold build (`Revision::cold`), the incremental step (`Revision::next`) and `assemble()`. `extract()`, `WatchSession::initialize()` and `WatchSession::rebuild()` all use `cold`. Keys, plugin hooks, diagnostics and stats come from one function.
- **Atomic publication.** `WatchSession` holds `ArcSwapOption<Revision>` plus a writer mutex. An update builds the next revision off to the side and stores it once, so readers never block and never see a mixture.
- **Recorded dependencies** (`resolver/deps.rs`). A thread-local recorder scoped to one `resolve_component` call collects three kinds of dependency:
  - **Files read** (interface, alias and template lookups; re-export walks; resolved import targets). These re-resolve on an edit, create or delete of that file.
  - **Bare enum and const-array names**, which are looked up project-wide. These re-resolve when the changed file declared that name before or after the change.
  - **Module resolution.** This re-resolves on creation of a new source file.
- **Changed paths are filtered like discovery** (`discover::is_source_file`). A missing file is a deletion; another read error keeps the previous declarations and records an `IoError`.
- **`IncrementalUpdate`** gains `revision`, `updatedKeys` and `removedKeys`.

## Verification

- **New test** `every_kind_of_change_leaves_the_snapshot_equal_to_a_cold_extract`. After each of 14 steps it asserts that components, enums and diagnostics equal a cold `extract()`. The steps cover:
  - a dependency edit two hops away
  - a barrel edit
  - an own-file edit and a rename
  - a cross-file name collision
  - an excluded story
  - "stops being a component"
  - a syntax error and its fix
  - a dependency delete and restore
  - a const array read by bare name
  - creation of a module an import was missing
  - a file move
- **Mutation checks.** Disabling each recorder fails the sequence test:
  - file recording fails 5 tests, including this one
  - bare-name recording fails the "const array read by bare name" step
  - module-resolution recording fails the "restore it" step
- **Rewritten tests.** Tests that pinned the old behavior now assert the new contract:
  - "deleted components linger" became "deleting a file removes its components and re-resolves dependents"
  - "missing file → `IoError`" in the CLI tests now uses an unreadable (non-UTF-8) file
- **Cold output** compared to #74's build on the five calibration corpora:
  - mantine, antd and shadcn: byte-identical
  - chakra and spectrum: identical components and enums, and the same diagnostic multiset. Resolve diagnostics are now ordered by file, then source position; before, they followed extractor emission order. #5 canonicalizes diagnostic order anyway.
- **Watch repros** (`watch --out`): dependency edit, barrel edit and `../` edit each match the cold extract. All three were stale before.
- **Incremental timing** on Mantine (median of 7):

  | Edited file | Before | After |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Leaf `Badge.tsx` | 8.3 ms, 1 component | 13.5 ms, 1 component |
  | `Box.tsx` | 9.5 ms, 1 component (stale) | 60 ms, 246 dependents |
  | `create-vars-resolver.ts` | 8 ms, 0 components (stale) | 59 ms, 229 dependents |

  The leaf-edit overhead is the copy-on-write revision plus a full output assemble.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and all 708 workspace tests pass.

## Breaking (Rust API, 0.x minor)

- `WatchSession`'s fields other than `options` are removed, and so is the `ReverseDeps` type.
- `rebuild()` is new.
- A deleted file now produces a removal, not an `IoError`.

## Not in this PR

- The CLI writes `--out` at start, and `r` calls `rebuild()` (4b).
- NAPI and Vite: removals, key matching, virtual-module invalidation, build-watch refresh (4c).
- Watch does not observe `tsconfig.json`, `package.json` or `node_modules` changes; this is documented as a known gap.

Stacked on #74. Part 1 of 3 for the watch-mode findings in the v1 review (core). The CLI and Vite/NAPI fixes follow as separate stacked PRs.

## Problem

Watch mode kept its own state in separate containers and re-resolved by a string-built reverse import graph. Verified defects:

- Edits to a dependency reached through a barrel or a `../` import never reached the component.
- New import edges added mid-session were never tracked.
- Deleted files' components stayed until restart.
- Excluded files (stories, tests) added components.
- A disambiguated component's edit could land under another component's key.
- The first run's diagnostics were missing from later snapshots.
- A snapshot could mix state from two updates.

## Change

- **One revision type.** `pipeline/revision.rs` owns the cold build (`Revision::cold`), the incremental step (`Revision::next`) and `assemble()`. `extract()`, `WatchSession::initialize()` and `WatchSession::rebuild()` all use `cold`. Keys, plugin hooks, diagnostics and stats come from one function.
- **Atomic publication.** `WatchSession` holds `ArcSwapOption<Revision>` plus a writer mutex. An update builds the next revision off to the side and stores it once, so readers never block and never see a mixture.
- **Recorded dependencies** (`resolver/deps.rs`). A thread-local recorder scoped to one `resolve_component` call collects three kinds of dependency:
  - **Files read** (interface, alias and template lookups; re-export walks; resolved import targets). These re-resolve on an edit, create or delete of that file.
  - **Bare enum and const-array names**, which are looked up project-wide. These re-resolve when the changed file declared that name before or after the change.
  - **Module resolution.** This re-resolves on creation of a new source file.
- **Changed paths are filtered like discovery** (`discover::is_source_file`). A missing file is a deletion; another read error keeps the previous declarations and records an `IoError`.
- **`IncrementalUpdate`** gains `revision`, `updatedKeys` and `removedKeys`.

## Verification

- **New test** `every_kind_of_change_leaves_the_snapshot_equal_to_a_cold_extract`. After each of 14 steps it asserts that components, enums and diagnostics equal a cold `extract()`. The steps cover:
  - a dependency edit two hops away
  - a barrel edit
  - an own-file edit and a rename
  - a cross-file name collision
  - an excluded story
  - "stops being a component"
  - a syntax error and its fix
  - a dependency delete and restore
  - a const array read by bare name
  - creation of a module an import was missing
  - a file move
- **Mutation checks.** Disabling each recorder fails the sequence test:
  - file recording fails 5 tests, including this one
  - bare-name recording fails the "const array read by bare name" step
  - module-resolution recording fails the "restore it" step
- **Rewritten tests.** Tests that pinned the old behavior now assert the new contract:
  - "deleted components linger" became "deleting a file removes its components and re-resolves dependents"
  - "missing file → `IoError`" in the CLI tests now uses an unreadable (non-UTF-8) file
- **Cold output** compared to #74's build on the five calibration corpora:
  - mantine, antd and shadcn: byte-identical
  - chakra and spectrum: identical components and enums, and the same diagnostic multiset. Resolve diagnostics are now ordered by file, then source position; before, they followed extractor emission order. #5 canonicalizes diagnostic order anyway.
- **Watch repros** (`watch --out`): dependency edit, barrel edit and `../` edit each match the cold extract. All three were stale before.
- **Incremental timing** on Mantine (median of 7):

  | Edited file | Before | After |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Leaf `Badge.tsx` | 8.3 ms, 1 component | 13.5 ms, 1 component |
  | `Box.tsx` | 9.5 ms, 1 component (stale) | 60 ms, 246 dependents |
  | `create-vars-resolver.ts` | 8 ms, 0 components (stale) | 59 ms, 229 dependents |

  The leaf-edit overhead is the copy-on-write revision plus a full output assemble.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and all 708 workspace tests pass.

## Breaking (Rust API, 0.x minor)

- `WatchSession`'s fields other than `options` are removed, and so is the `ReverseDeps` type.
- `rebuild()` is new.
- A deleted file now produces a removal, not an `IoError`.

## Not in this PR

- The CLI writes `--out` at start, and `r` calls `rebuild()` (4b).
- NAPI and Vite: removals, key matching, virtual-module invalidation, build-watch refresh (4c).
- Watch does not observe `tsconfig.json`, `package.json` or `node_modules` changes; this is documented as a known gap.

21:`main()` (`main.rs:175-203`) is the **sole `std::process::exit` call site** in the crate. Every command handler returns a `Result<i32>` (or hardcodes `0` inline for the three that don't call the pipeline), and `main()` maps a non-zero return to `process::exit(exit_code)` after the match. This is stated explicitly in `cmd_extract`'s doc comment (`extract.rs:6-9`) and repeated in `cmd_check`'s (`check.rs:6-8`): keeping the exit decision out of command handlers is what makes it testable — `cmd_extract`/`cmd_check`/`cmd_inspect`/`cmd_watch` all have unit tests that call the handler directly and assert on the returned `i32`, without needing a subprocess harness or capturing a real process exit.
25:1. **`main()` is the only place that terminates the process for the normal command path.** No command handler may call `std::process::exit` directly for its own success/failure signaling — doing so would make that handler untestable via a plain function call and would bypass whatever cleanup happens between `match` and the final `if exit_code != 0`. (The one deliberate exception is `watch.rs`'s raw-mode keyboard thread, which calls `std::process::exit(0)` on `q`/`ctrl-c` — see Locked Design Decisions.)
27:2. **No `println!`/`eprintln!` in a command handler for anything the user is meant to read as structured or reusable output — route it through `output.rs`.** `output.rs`'s own module doc states `print_summary` and `print_diagnostics` always write to **stderr**, specifically so `caliper-docgen extract | jq .` never sees human-readable text interleaved with the JSON payload on stdout. Breaking this by adding a stray `println!` in a command handler would silently corrupt every pipe-to-`jq` workflow. (Note: `inspect.rs` and `watch.rs`'s startup banner use raw `println!` directly rather than going through `output.rs` — see Known Gaps; the _stdout-is-payload-only_ half of this invariant still holds for those, since neither writes JSON to stdout by default.)
33:5. **`ExtractionOutput::exit_code(strict: bool) -> i32` is the single source of truth for the 0/1/2 exit-code mapping, and every command that reports it must call this method rather than re-deriving the check.** The mapping (`core/types/output.rs:42-55`): `Error` present → `2`; `Warning` present and `strict` → `1`; `Warning` present and not `strict` → `0`; `Info`-only or clean → `0`. `extract`, `check`, `watch`, and `inspect` all now call this one method (see Locked Design Decisions — this was a real duplication bug, fixed).
37:7. **`watch`'s exit code must come from the session's cumulative snapshot, not the current file-change event's own diagnostics.** `watch.rs:142-143` explicitly sources `watch_exit_code` from `session_inner.snapshot()` — the whole tree's current diagnostic state — rather than from just the `update` returned by `update_file(&utf8)` for this one edit. The comment at that call site spells out why: sourcing from the per-event delta would let a clean edit to file A reset the tracked exit code to 0 even though file B, untouched in this event, still has an unresolved error.
39:8. **`watch`'s output-file writes are atomic (`write_atomic`, `watch.rs:17-39`): temp file in the same directory, then `rename`.** A mid-write failure (disk full, permission revoked) must never leave the `--out` path holding truncated JSON, since some other process (a bundler, a dev-server file watcher) may be reading that path concurrently and can't tell a half-written file from a valid empty one.
49:**Exit-code logic lives in `core/types/output.rs`, not the CLI crate, despite `crates/core/AGENTS.md`'s "no terminal/display code in `crates/core`" rule.** This looks like a rule violation at first glance — exit codes are a very CLI-flavored concept. It isn't: `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` cluster 11 documents that this was originally a _doc-comment convention re-typed per command_ (`extract.rs` and `check.rs` each independently implemented the same 0/1/2 check with syntactically different code, and `cmd_watch` used to return `()` with `main.rs` hardcoding exit `0` for that arm, and `cmd_inspect` never touched `output.diagnostics` at all). The fix — `impl ExtractionOutput { pub fn exit_code(&self, strict: bool) -> i32 }` in core — was deliberately scoped as "pure data-in/data-out, same category as the existing `html_element()` helper," which is why it doesn't violate the core/no-terminal-code rule: `exit_code()` computes an `i32` from data, it doesn't print anything or touch a terminal. Do not "fix" this by moving the logic into the CLI crate; that would resurrect the exact duplication cluster 11 documents.
51:**Only `check` exposes `--strict` as a CLI flag; `extract`, `watch`, and `inspect` always call `exit_code(false)`.** This asymmetry is intentional but only loosely documented. `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` cluster 11 explicitly preserves it ("note `check.rs` additionally supports a `--strict` warnings-escalate-to-1 path that `extract.rs`'s args have no equivalent flag for today; preserve that distinction rather than assuming the two commands' checks are fully identical"), and `docs/edge-cases.md` P3-1 separately flags the consequence: "`watch` always exits 0 regardless of extraction errors — fine for an interactive dev loop, but a footgun if ever run non-interactively (CI, pre-commit)." So the asymmetry is a deliberate, load-bearing design choice for `check` (whose whole purpose per its doc comment is "For CI"), but it is **not** independently justified anywhere for why `extract`/`watch`/`inspect` shouldn't also grow a `--strict` flag — P3-1 marks it as an accepted-but-unresolved gap rather than a closed decision. Treat "should `extract --strict` exist" as an open question, not a settled one, if it comes up again.
57:**`watch`'s keyboard-input thread calls `std::process::exit(0)` directly on `q`/ctrl-c** (`watch.rs:101-104`), which is the one deliberate exception to Invariant 1. It's spawned as a detached `std::thread::spawn` reading raw terminal events in a loop with no owned `JoinHandle` the main thread waits on — there's no `Result<i32>` return path back to `main()` from inside that thread, and disabling raw mode (`crossterm::terminal::disable_raw_mode()`) before exiting is itself part of why the exit happens inline rather than via a channel-and-return.
79:- **`docs/edge-cases.md` P3-1** (still open, cross-referenced above under Locked Design Decisions): the exit-code contract is fully enforced for `extract`/`check`, but `watch` always exits based on its own cumulative snapshot rather than ever being run non-interactively with a documented CI contract, and there's no `--strict` equivalent for `extract`/`watch`/`inspect` — only `check` has one. This is flagged as intentional-for-now but not independently justified beyond `check`'s explicit CI purpose.
80:- **`inspect.rs` and `watch.rs`'s startup banner bypass `output.rs`**, using raw `println!` calls directly for their tabular/banner output rather than routing through `output.rs`'s helpers (Invariant 2's note). This doesn't violate the stdout-is-payload-only half of the "no terminal code outside output.rs" rule in practice (neither writes JSON to stdout by default), but it is a literal deviation from `crates/cli/AGENTS.md`'s "never `println!` in command handlers" rule as stated, worth flagging as a possible follow-up rather than treating as settled.

25:1. **`main()` is the only place that terminates the process for the normal command path.** No command handler may call `std::process::exit` directly for its own success/failure signaling — doing so would make that handler untestable via a plain function call and would bypass whatever cleanup happens between `match` and the final `if exit_code != 0`. (The one deliberate exception is `watch.rs`'s raw-mode keyboard thread, which calls `std::process::exit(0)` on `q`/`ctrl-c` — see Locked Design Decisions.)
27:2. **No `println!`/`eprintln!` in a command handler for anything the user is meant to read as structured or reusable output — route it through `output.rs`.** `output.rs`'s own module doc states `print_summary` and `print_diagnostics` always write to **stderr**, specifically so `caliper-docgen extract | jq .` never sees human-readable text interleaved with the JSON payload on stdout. Breaking this by adding a stray `println!` in a command handler would silently corrupt every pipe-to-`jq` workflow. (Note: `inspect.rs` and `watch.rs`'s startup banner use raw `println!` directly rather than going through `output.rs` — see Known Gaps; the _stdout-is-payload-only_ half of this invariant still holds for those, since neither writes JSON to stdout by default.)
33:5. **`ExtractionOutput::exit_code(strict: bool) -> i32` is the single source of truth for the 0/1/2 exit-code mapping, and every command that reports it must call this method rather than re-deriving the check.** The mapping (`core/types/output.rs:42-55`): `Error` present → `2`; `Warning` present and `strict` → `1`; `Warning` present and not `strict` → `0`; `Info`-only or clean → `0`. `extract`, `check`, `watch`, and `inspect` all now call this one method (see Locked Design Decisions — this was a real duplication bug, fixed).
37:7. **`watch`'s exit code must come from the session's cumulative snapshot, not the current file-change event's own diagnostics.** `watch.rs:142-143` explicitly sources `watch_exit_code` from `session_inner.snapshot()` — the whole tree's current diagnostic state — rather than from just the `update` returned by `update_file(&utf8)` for this one edit. The comment at that call site spells out why: sourcing from the per-event delta would let a clean edit to file A reset the tracked exit code to 0 even though file B, untouched in this event, still has an unresolved error.
39:8. **`watch`'s output-file writes are atomic (`write_atomic`, `watch.rs:17-39`): temp file in the same directory, then `rename`.** A mid-write failure (disk full, permission revoked) must never leave the `--out` path holding truncated JSON, since some other process (a bundler, a dev-server file watcher) may be reading that path concurrently and can't tell a half-written file from a valid empty one.

Do not "fix" this by moving the logic into the CLI crate; that would resurrect the exact duplication cluster 11 documents.
51:**Only `check` exposes `--strict` as a CLI flag; `extract`, `watch`, and `inspect` always call `exit_code(false)`.** This asymmetry is intentional but only loosely documented. `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` cluster 11 explicitly preserves it ("note `check.rs` additionally supports a `--strict` warnings-escalate-to-1 path that `extract.rs`'s args have no equivalent flag for today; preserve that distinction rather than assuming the two commands' checks are fully identical"), and `docs/edge-cases.md` P3-1 separately flags the consequence: "`watch` always exits 0 regardless of extraction errors — fine for an interactive dev loop, but a footgun if ever run non-interactively (CI, pre-commit)." Treat "should `extract --strict` exist" as an open question, not a settled one, if it comes up again.

input.content:
Stacked on #75. Part 2 of 3 for the watch-mode findings in the v1 review (CLI).

## Problem

- **`--out` was first written on the first file change.** A consumer started alongside `watch` had nothing to read until an edit happened. This is also why the review's repro scripts raced.
- **`r` called `initialize()`.** After the first call that just returns the current snapshot, so `r` re-extracted nothing.
- **Every TypeScript event rewrote `--out`,** including excluded stories and paths outside the source dirs. That can trigger downstream watchers for no change.
- **Interactive sessions staircased their output.** crossterm's raw mode clears `OPOST`, so a printed `\n` no longer returns to column 0. Confirmed on a pty: output modes were `ONLCR` only.

## Change

- **One `publish` helper.** It tracks the exit code from the whole snapshot and rewrites `--out`. It is used at startup, on each change and on `r`.
- **`r` calls `WatchSession::rebuild()`,** prints the summary and publishes. This covers `tsconfig.json`, `package.json` and `node_modules` changes, which the watcher cannot see.
- **`handle_change` skips events that produced no new revision,** using the new `WatchSession::revision()`. It reports removed keys alongside updated ones.
- **`keep_output_processing` turns `OPOST | ONLCR` back on** after `enable_raw_mode` (unix, via rustix termios). Input stays raw.

## Verification

- Unit tests:
  - `--out` is written by `start_session`
  - `r` picks up a component and an unreadable file that no event reported, and rewrites `--out`
  - an excluded story event writes nothing and leaves the revision at 1
  - a deleted file's component is removed from `--out`
- Process tests:
  - `watch_writes_out_before_any_change` matches `extract`
  - `r_extracts_a_terminal_session_again` runs on a pty
  - `raw_mode_keeps_newline_translation_for_output` failed before the fix (`OutputModes(ONLCR)`) and passes after
- `edit_until_out_is_written` now waits for the startup write, then for the edit. Without that it raced the initial extraction. `commands` passed 3 runs in a row.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean; all 713 workspace tests pass.

1	import type { Plugin, ResolvedConfig, ViteDevServer, HotUpdateOptions } from 'vite'
2	import * as napi from 'caliper-docgen-napi'
3	import type { ExtractionOutput, IncrementalUpdate } from 'caliper-docgen-napi'
4	
5	const VIRTUAL_ID = 'virtual:caliper-docgen'
6	const RESOLVED_VIRTUAL_ID = `\0${VIRTUAL_ID}`
7	
8	export interface CaliperDocgenOptions {
9	  srcDirs: string[]
10	  exclude?: string[]
11	  skipHtmlProps?: boolean
12	}
13	
14	export function caliperDocgen(options: CaliperDocgenOptions): Plugin {
15	  let sessionId: number
16	  let root: string
17	  let command: 'build' | 'serve' | undefined
18	  // `vite build --watch`: Rollup's buildEnd hook fires once per rebuild, not
19	  // once when the watch process actually shuts down — closeWatcher is the
20	  // correct once-per-process hook for that. See buildEnd's own comment below.
21	  let isWatchBuild = false
22	  let resolvedSrcDirs: string[] = []
23	  let currentOutput: ExtractionOutput = {
24	    components: {},
25	    enums: {},
26	    diagnostics: [],
27	    stats: {
28	      componentsExtracted: 0,
29	      componentsSkipped: 0,
30	      filesParsed: 0,
31	      dtsFilesParsed: 0,
32	      dtsCacheHits: 0,
33	      durationMs: 0,
34	      tier1Count: 0,
35	      tier3Count: 0,
36	      opaqueCount: 0,
37	    },
38	  }
39	  // Holds the in-flight init promise so hotUpdate can await it before first incremental call.
40	  let initPromise: Promise<void> | null = null
41	  // Per-file monotonic sequence guard: two overlapping hotUpdate calls for
42	  // the same file (e.g. a rapid double-save) can have their async NAPI
43	  // calls resolve out of order. Without this, an older call finishing last
44	  // would silently overwrite currentOutput/the HMR payload with stale data
45	  // even though a newer call already applied fresher results.
46	  let hotUpdateSeq = 0
47	  const latestSeqByFile = new Map<string, number>()
48	
49	  function napiOptions() {
50	    return {
51	      srcDirs: resolvedSrcDirs,
52	      exclude: options.exclude,
53	      htmlAttributes: options.skipHtmlProps ? ('none' as const) : undefined,
54	    }
55	  }
56	
57	  // configureServer (dev-only) is where cold extraction normally runs and
58	  // populates `currentOutput` for the virtual module. Vite never calls
59	  // configureServer during `vite build`, so without this, a production
60	  // build's virtual module always resolved to the empty placeholder below.
61	  async function coldExtract(): Promise<boolean> {
62	    const json = await napi.initializeSession(sessionId, napiOptions())
63	    try {
64	      currentOutput = JSON.parse(json) as ExtractionOutput
65	      return true
66	    } catch (error) {
67	      console.error('[caliper-docgen] Failed to parse initializeSession output:', error)
68	      return false
69	    }
70	  }
71	
72	  function isSrcFile(file: string): boolean {
73	    return (file.endsWith('.tsx') || file.endsWith('.ts')) && resolvedSrcDirs.some((dir) => file.startsWith(`${dir}/`))
74	  }
75	
76	  return {
77	    name: 'caliper-docgen',
78	
79	    configResolved(config: ResolvedConfig) {
80	      ;({ root, command } = config)
81	      isWatchBuild = command === 'build' && Boolean(config.build?.watch)
82	      // A trailing slash (relative `'src/'`, or an already-absolute dir
83	      // ending in `/`) must be stripped here — isSrcFile's `startsWith(`${dir}/`)`
84	      // check would otherwise require a double slash no real file path has,
85	      // silently excluding every file under that srcDir from HMR.
86	      resolvedSrcDirs = options.srcDirs.map((d) => {
87	        const abs = d.startsWith('/') ? d : `${root}/${d}`
88	        return abs.endsWith('/') ? abs.slice(0, -1) : abs
89	      })
90	      // sessionId is foundational to every other hook, so a failure here
91	      // can't be swallowed the way coldExtract's failures are — log for
92	      // discoverability, then rethrow so Vite's own config-resolution fails
93	      // loudly instead of every later hook failing confusingly against an
94	      // undefined sessionId.
95	      try {
96	        sessionId = napi.createSession(napiOptions())
97	      } catch (error) {
98	        console.error('[caliper-docgen] createSession failed:', error)
99	        throw error
100	      }
101	    },
102	
103	    // Build-only counterpart to coldExtract() in configureServer; see that comment.
104	    async buildStart() {
105	      if (command !== 'build') return
106	      try {
107	        await coldExtract()
108	      } catch (error) {
109	        console.error('[caliper-docgen] initializeSession failed:', error)
110	      }
111	    },
112	
113	    configureServer(server: ViteDevServer) {
114	      // Vite guarantees configResolved fires before configureServer;
115	      // sessionId and resolvedSrcDirs are safe to use here.
116	      //
117	      // This hook must return its teardown function synchronously — it can't
118	      // be `async` or `await` coldExtract() here without breaking that contract,
119	      // so the fire-and-forget .then()/.catch() chain below is intentional,
120	      // not an oversight.
121	      /* oxlint-disable promise/prefer-await-to-then, promise/always-return, promise/prefer-await-to-callbacks */
122	      initPromise = coldExtract()
123	        .then((ok) => {
124	          if (!ok) return
125	          // environments.client.hot is Vite 6+ API; cast avoids typing fight across patch versions
126	          ;(server as any).environments?.client?.hot?.send('caliper-docgen:ready', {
127	            components: currentOutput.components,
128	          })
129	        })
130	        .catch((error: unknown) => {
131	          console.error('[caliper-docgen] initializeSession failed:', error)
132	        })
133	      /* oxlint-enable promise/prefer-await-to-then, promise/always-return, promise/prefer-await-to-callbacks */
134	
135	      // buildEnd isn't called in dev mode — this is the only reliable cleanup hook.
136	      return () => {
137	        napi.closeSession(sessionId)
138	      }
139	    },
140	
141	    async hotUpdate(opts: HotUpdateOptions) {
142	      // Vite 6+ supplies this.environment in the hotUpdate context.
143	      // We cast rather than annotating `this:` to avoid fighting the Plugin interface's
144	      // declared this-type across different Vite patch versions.
145	      // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
146	      const env = (this as any).environment as
147	        | { name: string; hot: { send(event: string, data?: unknown): void } }
148	        | undefined
149	
150	      if (!env || env.name !== 'client') return
151	      if (!isSrcFile(opts.file)) return
152	
153	      if (initPromise) await initPromise
154	
155	      const seq = ++hotUpdateSeq
156	      latestSeqByFile.set(opts.file, seq)
157	
158	      const json = await napi.extractFileIncremental(opts.file, sessionId, napiOptions())
159	
160	      // A newer hotUpdate call for this same file has already taken over —
161	      // its own result (in flight or already applied) is authoritative, so
162	      // applying this now-stale one would be a straight regression. Drop it
163	      // silently rather than race it, for both the success and the
164	      // malformed-JSON fallback path below.
165	      if (latestSeqByFile.get(opts.file) !== seq) return
166	
167	      let update: IncrementalUpdate
168	      try {
169	        update = JSON.parse(json) as IncrementalUpdate
170	      } catch (error) {
171	        console.error('[caliper-docgen] Failed to parse extractFileIncremental output:', error)
172	        env.hot.send('caliper-docgen:update', { file: opts.file, updatedComponents: [], diagnostics: [] })
173	        return
174	      }
175	
176	      for (const comp of update.updatedComponents) {
177	        currentOutput.components[comp.displayName] = comp
178	      }
179	
180	      env.hot.send('caliper-docgen:update', {
181	        file: opts.file,
182	        updatedComponents: update.updatedComponents,
183	        diagnostics: update.diagnostics,
184	      })
185

200	      // In `vite build --watch`, this fires once per rebuild (Rollup's own
201	      // build-hook contract), not once at process shutdown. Closing here
202	      // would make every rebuild after the first auto-vivify a brand new
203	      // session on its next buildStart (the Rust binding creates one for

# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.

    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build

test-rust:
    name: Test / Rust
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@1168f6810a3cb30a3514bf5756a3b7f0422c6df8 # v2.87.28
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest
      # The cli config tests spawn `node --import=tsx/esm`, and tsx is a devDependency of apps/validate.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: just test-rust

    name: Test / TypeScript / Node ${{ matrix.node }}

      matrix:
        node: ["24", "26"]

AGENTS.md:42:1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
CONTRIBUTING.md:51:**`crates/binding`** — thin NAPI wrapper. Owns the async runtime (tokio) and exposes the five NAPI functions (`extractAll`, `createSession`, `initializeSession`, `extractFileIncremental`, `closeSession`). No business logic.
docs/root-cause-analysis.md:50:**Root cause:** Zero `catch_unwind` anywhere in the repo (confirmed by grep). The three async NAPI entry points (`extract_all`, `extract_file_incremental`, `initialize_session`) are only panic-safe by _accident_ — they happen to run inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, whose `JoinError` catches the unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not a decision anyone made. # caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

A Vite plugin that exposes your React components' props on a virtual module and updates it through HMR as you edit.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

docgen.components['Button'].props
```

Extraction runs on OXC through [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi), so a single-file update takes about 2ms. Requires Vite 7 or 8. The module uses the canonical output format, not the `react-docgen-typescript` shape.

Docs and benchmarks: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

FSL-1.1-MIT. Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.

input.content:
Stacked on #76. Part 3 of 3 for the watch-mode findings in the v1 review (Vite plugin and NAPI).

## Problem

- **The virtual module was never invalidated after its first load.** Edits reached the HMR event but never the module.
- **The plugin kept its own copy of the output, keyed by display name.** As a result:
  - a disambiguated `Button (src/b/Button.tsx)` was written to `Button`
  - removals were never applied
  - enums and diagnostics went stale
- **`vite build --watch` served the first build's output on every rebuild.** `hotUpdate` never fires in a build, and `initializeSession` returns the existing snapshot. Source files no bundle module imports never triggered a rebuild at all.
- **A failed extraction during `vite build` was logged, and the build shipped an empty virtual module.**
- **The integration tier against the real binding has been failing since #71, unnoticed.** CI never ran it. Its fixture `Button` returned a plain object, which has no render evidence.

## Change

- **`load()` serves the session's current output** (`initializeSession` returns the current revision) and awaits a cold extraction still in flight. The plugin no longer keeps its own copy.
- **`hotUpdate`:**
  - sends `{ file, revision, updatedKeys, updatedComponents, removedKeys, diagnostics }`
  - skips changes that produced no new revision
  - invalidates the virtual module and returns `[...opts.modules, virtual]`, so HMR reaches its importers and Fast Refresh still handles the edited file
- **Build watch:**
  - `buildStart` registers each source dir with `this.addWatchFile` and awaits pending changes
  - `watchChange` applies each changed source file to the session
  - the cold extraction runs once per session
- **`this.error` on extraction failure,** in `buildStart` and `load`.
- **CI:**
  - a new `test-integration` job (`just test-integration`) builds the native binding and runs the plugin against it
  - `NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true` makes a missing binary fail instead of skip
  - the job is added to the required `CI` gate

## Verification

- **Unit tests (39), rewritten for the new contract.** They cover:
  - keyed payloads, including a rename
  - invalidating and returning the virtual module
  - no-op revisions sending nothing
  - diagnostics-only changes still reloading
  - out-of-order same-file calls
  - `load` and `buildStart` failing through `this.error`
  - `addWatchFile` per source dir
  - `watchChange` applied before the next rebuild's load
- **Integration on the real binding (5):**
  - the fixtures render again
  - new: a dependency edit and a deletion through `hotUpdate` produce `[{updatedKeys: ['Button']}, {removedKeys: ['Card']}]`, and the virtual module matches
  - new: a production `vite build` bundles the extracted output
- `just lint` is clean, `tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `cargo test -p caliper-docgen-napi` passes 15/15.

## Behavior change

A change that cannot be applied (the NAPI call rejects or returns malformed JSON) now logs and sends no event. Before, an empty update event was sent.

## Change

- **`load()` serves the session's current output** (`initializeSession` returns the current revision) and awaits a cold extraction still in flight. The plugin no longer keeps its own copy.
- **`hotUpdate`:**
  - sends `{ file, revision, updatedKeys, updatedComponents, removedKeys, diagnostics }`
  - skips changes that produced no new revision
  - invalidates the virtual module and returns `[...opts.modules, virtual]`, so HMR reaches its importers and Fast Refresh still handles the edited file
- **Build watch:**
  - `buildStart` registers each source dir with `this.addWatchFile` and awaits pending changes
  - `watchChange` applies each changed source file to the session
  - the cold extraction runs once per session
- **`this.error` on extraction failure,** in `buildStart` and `load`.
- **CI:**
  - a new `test-integration` job (`just test-integration`) builds the native binding and runs the plugin against it
  - `NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true` makes a missing binary fail instead of skip
  - the job is added to the required `CI` gate

## Verification

- **Unit tests (39), rewritten for the new contract.** They cover:
  - keyed payloads, including a rename
  - invalidating and returning the virtual module
  - no-op revisions sending nothing
  - diagnostics-only changes still reloading
  - out-of-order same-file calls
  - `load` and `buildStart` failing through `this.error`
  - `addWatchFile` per source dir
  - `watchChange` applied before the next rebuild's load
- **Integration on the real binding (5):**
  - the fixtures render again
  - new: a dependency edit and a deletion through `hotUpdate` produce `[{updatedKeys: ['Button']}, {removedKeys: ['Card']}]`, and the virtual module matches
  - new: a production `vite build` bundles the extracted output
- `just lint` is clean, `tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `cargo test -p caliper-docgen-napi` passes 15/15.

## Behavior change

A change that cannot be applied (the NAPI call rejects or returns malformed JSON) now logs and sends no event. Before, an empty update event was sent.

"""Duplicate-diagnostic rate per corpus. Usage: diag_dupes.py BIN"""
import collections, json, subprocess, sys

110:- **Diagnostics are wrong.** Initial diagnostics are never seeded. A dependent's diagnostics are filed under the edited file's key, so fixed errors linger and others duplicate.
111-- **Deleting a file leaves its component and an `IO_ERROR` forever.** The Error-severity `IO_ERROR` pins the exit code at 2. A test asserts the stale entry.
112-- **`update_file` skips cold-path filters:** discovery excludes (an edited `*.stories.tsx` adds `StoryOnly`), `excludePrefixes` and both plugin hooks.
113-- **CLI:**
114-  - `watch --out` is not written until the first change.
115-  - `r` "re-extract" does not re-extract.
116-- **Vite:**
117-  - no removals
118-  - display-name keys collide with Rust's disambiguated keys
119-  - enums and diagnostics never refresh
120-  - the virtual module is never invalidated
121-  - `build --watch` stays stale
122-  - build failures are swallowed into an empty module, exit 0
--
134:### E. The diagnostics model has no identity (P1)
135-
136:- **82–97% of diagnostics are exact duplicates.** Confirmed:
137-
138-  | Corpus | Duplicates | Total |
139-  | --- | ---: | ---: |
140-  | Mantine | 23,163 | 23,787 |
141-  | Ant Design | 4,634 | 5,062 |
142-  | react-spectrum | 11,480 | 13,936 |
143-
144-  One conditional type is reported 13,358 times. Diagnostics are 9.1 MB of Mantine's 23.5 MB JSON. The same leaf is also double-reported within a component.
145-- **No attribution or position.** Diagnostics carry no component and, apart from skips, no position.
146-- **Misleading help text.** "Enable typescript-go" points at an option that doesn't exist.
147-
148:**Structural fix:** identity `(code, file, span, subject)` with dedup, an `affects: [component keys]` list, and per-run memoization of type resolution, which also cuts time.
149-
150-### F. The cache trusts a hand-bumped version (P0)
151-
152-- **Stale cache after extractor changes.** Confirmed in code and git history: #69 changed `SourceData` for identical input without a bump. #54 and others did the same. Cached `.d.ts` results stay stale with no signal.
153-- **The version isn't in the payload.** The manifest and the payload are separate renames, so mixed-version tools sharing a directory can decode wrong data.
154-- **The cache barely helps.** It saves about 7 ms out of 150, and `dtsCacheHits` misreports.
155-
156-**Fix:** key on crate version plus an extractor fingerprint, with a versioned header inside the payload. Or question whether the cache earns its keep at all.
157-
158-### G. Performance at scale (P1/P2)
159-
160-Determinism is clean (six conditions, byte-identical) and so is robustness. Measured costs:

input.content:
Stacked on #77. Part 1 of #5 (diagnostics identity, memoization, cache fingerprint) from the v1 review: family E.

## Problem

- **82–98% of diagnostics were exact duplicates,** one per component that resolved through the same type. One conditional type in Mantine was reported 13,358 times, and diagnostics were a third of Mantine's JSON.
- **A diagnostic didn't say which components it affected.**
- **Two help texts said "Enable typescript-go",** an option that does not exist.

## Change

- **`Diagnostic.affects`:** the output keys of the components whose resolution reported it, sorted. It is omitted from JSON when empty, as for file- and run-level diagnostics.
- **`Revision::assemble` merges diagnostics by identity** (every field except `affects`) through a `DiagnosticSet`, then sorts by file, line, column and message. Severity uses its explicit rank and the code its name. This respects the documented invariant that neither enum's declaration order is an ordering, so no `Ord` is derived.
- **`IncrementalUpdate.diagnostics`** comes from the assembled output: the changed file's diagnostics plus those affecting a re-resolved component.
- **CLI grouping counts one occurrence per affected component,** so `×N` keeps its meaning.
- **Surfaces updated:**
  - JSON schema (`schema` command and its trycmd snapshot)
  - `index.d.ts`
  - TOON output (`affects:` line)
  - the types and pipeline architecture docs
- **Help texts rewritten** to say what the user can do.

## Verification

Compared to the previous build on the five calibration corpora:

| Corpus | Diagnostics | JSON | Median time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mantine | 24,009 → 563 | 24.0 → 15.6 MB | 191 → 170 ms |
| chakra | 4,538 → 583 | 2.3 → 0.8 MB | 35 → 31 ms |
| antd | 5,313 → 473 | 3.6 → 1.9 MB | 45 → 42 ms |
| shadcn | 3,022 → 2,424 | 3.8 → 3.8 MB | 64 → 65 ms |
| spectrum | 14,231 → 2,575 | 11.0 → 6.5 MB | 143 → 137 ms |

- Components and enums are identical on all five corpora.
- The set of distinct diagnostics is identical, ignoring `affects` and the two rewritten help texts. Nothing is lost.
- New tests:
  - `a_diagnostic_shared_by_many_components_is_reported_once_listing_them` asserts the exact `(code, file, affects)` list
  - the plugin-panic test now expects one diagnostic with `affects: [Button, Card]`
  - CLI `a_deduplicated_diagnostic_counts_once_per_affected_component`
- Snapshots: `affects` is added; Panda's duplicated `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` collapses to one.
- The watch sequence test (snapshot == extract) still passes, now including diagnostic order.

# 0003. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-07-22 (retroactive)

## Context

The DTS parse cache persists `SourceData` across runs so unchanged `.d.ts` files don't get re-parsed. `rmp_serde::to_vec`/`from_slice` — the default, and what this project uses — encode structs _positionally_: as an array of field values in declaration order, not a map of field names. A `_named` variant encodes as a map instead, at a size and speed cost we haven't needed to pay.

## Decision

Use plain `rmp_serde::to_vec`/`from_slice`, and treat `SourceData`'s field order as part of the wire format. A `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` constant (`crates/core/src/cache.rs`) gets bumped whenever a field is added anywhere but the end of the struct, removed, or reordered — any change that would shift decode position for cache entries written before the change. A version mismatch discards the whole cache rather than risk decoding an old entry into the wrong field.

## Consequences

- Smaller, faster cache files than named encoding — the whole point.
- Adding a field to `SourceData` (or anything it contains) requires remembering to bump `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` if it isn't appended at the very end. Easy to forget — `const_arrays` (added mid-struct) is exactly the case this version bump was added to cover.
- A forgotten bump doesn't fail loudly. It decodes as plausible-looking but wrong data — the worst kind of bug. There's no compiler check for this; it's a discipline problem, not a type-safety one.
