Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [4. Defer full type-checker integration](0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md) — superseded by 0006.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.

- [7. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default](0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) — do not feature-gate the backend crate, run it by default, or let it replace a structural entry on a clash.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
# NNNN. Short, decision-shaped title

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD

## Context

What forced this? The constraint, not the backstory. 2-4 sentences.

## Decision

What we're doing, stated plainly. A paragraph if it's one thing; a short paragraph plus bullets if it splits into a few discrete parts. Match the shape to the decision — don't pad a simple one or cram a multi-part one into a single block.

## Consequences

What this costs and what it buys. Bullets.

-
-

## Alternatives considered (optional)

Only if something else was a real contender. Name it and say why it lost — don't list every option that was never serious.

# 0008. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21

## Context

Under 0003 the cache is discarded only when someone bumps `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`. Extractor changes that keep `SourceData`'s shape but change its content for the same input (#54, #69) were never bumped, so cached `.d.ts` results stayed stale with no signal. The version also lived only in `manifest.json`, a separate file from the payload, so two tool versions sharing a cache directory could pair one's manifest with the other's data.

## Decision

The payload starts with a header: schema version, crate version, and a fingerprint `build.rs` computes from the crate's sources and, in a workspace build, `Cargo.lock`. Loading decodes the header first and discards the cache unless all three match the running build. The manifest repeats the header for inspection only.

- A cache from another build is discarded silently: that is the expected state after any upgrade.
- A cache from this build that fails to decode is discarded with an `Info` diagnostic.
- `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` still moves when `SourceData`'s shape changes, as 0003 says; the golden test pins that.

## Consequences

- Any code or dependency change invalidates the cache, including in development, with no step to remember.
- A cache never survives an upgrade, even one that changed nothing the cache depends on. The cache saves little time per run, so this costs little.
- Builds from the published crate fingerprint the crate's sources without `Cargo.lock`; the crate version covers the dependency set there.

docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md:90:- **DTS cache keys on `(path, size, mtime_ns)`, not a content hash.** A cheap stat-only check is the entire point of this cache's speed advantage; a content hash closes the residual staleness gap (Known Gaps below) but was deliberately rejected as disproportionate to the problem's real frequency — see `cache.rs:196-204`'s doc comment and `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` line 140, which additionally notes that _if_ this is ever revisited, a fast non-cryptographic hash (xxhash/CRC) over bytes already being read for size would be the right scope, not a full cryptographic hash.
docs/architecture/types-and-output-contract.md:272:**Invariant 11:** `SourceData`'s field _order_ is part of the wire format, not just its field _set_. A `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` constant in `cache.rs` must be bumped whenever a field is added anywhere but the very end of the struct, removed, or reordered — anything that shifts the decode position of fields relative to what an old cache entry on disk was written with. The ADR calls out `const_arrays` (added mid-struct, not appended) as the concrete precedent for exactly the case this version bump exists to cover.
docs/architecture/types-and-output-contract.md:274:**Why this is dangerous rather than merely inconvenient:** a forgotten version bump does not fail loudly. `rmp_serde` will happily decode an old, differently-shaped byte sequence into the new struct shape — every field gets _some_ value, just the wrong one, read from whatever position the old encoding happened to put unrelated data. There's no compiler check and no runtime error; it's "plausible-looking but wrong data," which the ADR explicitly calls "the worst kind of bug." Anyone adding a field to `SourceData`, or to any type nested inside it (`CollectedInterface`, `RawProp`, `CollectedTypeAlias`, `ComponentMapping`, ...) that flows into the cached shape, must check whether it lands at the true end of the struct; if not, `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` needs a bump in the same change.

input.content:
Stacked on #78. Part 2 of #5 from the v1 review: family F (the cache trusts a hand-bumped version).

## Problem

- **The parse cache was discarded only when someone bumped `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.** Extractor changes that keep `SourceData`'s shape but change its content (#54, #69) were never bumped, so cached `.d.ts` results stayed stale with no signal.
- **The version lived only in `manifest.json`,** a separate file from the payload. Two tool versions sharing one cache directory could pair one's manifest with the other's data.
- **`dtsCacheHits` counted only `.d.ts` files inside the source dirs.** TypeScript's lib files, where the cache actually saves work, never counted, so the stat usually read 0. `dtsFilesParsed` was always 0.

## Change

- **`build.rs`** fingerprints the crate's sources and, in a workspace build, `Cargo.lock`, using FNV-1a so it is stable across toolchains.
- **The payload starts with a `CacheHeader`** of schema, crate version and fingerprint, decoded before any entries. The cache loads only on a full match.
  - A different build's cache, or an older layout, is discarded silently; that's expected after any upgrade.
  - A cache from this build whose entries fail to decode is discarded with an `Info` diagnostic. `NotFound` and `NotADirectory` count as absent.
- **The cache counts its own lookups and hits,** which feed `dtsFilesParsed` and `dtsCacheHits`.
- **Data file renamed** to `dts.msgpack`; `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` goes to 13.
- **ADR 0008** records the decision; it adds to 0003 and doesn't reverse it. The pipeline and types docs are updated, and the closed mtime staleness gap moves to "Fixed".

## Verification

- **New cache tests:**
  - a cache from this build is used
  - a different schema, crate version or fingerprint is each discarded with no diagnostic
  - a headerless payload is discarded silently
  - corrupt entries under the current header are discarded with an `Info` `IO_ERROR` that names the directory
  - `counts()` is exact: 3 lookups, 2 hits

Sequential — it's I/O-bound directory walking, not CPU work worth parallelizing, and the final sort is required for the determinism invariant below.
18:**Why parallel exactly at phases 2 and 4, nowhere else:** those are the only two phases doing embarrassingly-parallel, side-effect-free-per-item CPU work over an already-known-size collection. Discovery is I/O-walk-bound: merge and collect both build one shared structure incrementally, which is cheaper done sequentially than synchronized.
89:- **Two rayon parallel phases, everything else sequential.** Already covered above under "the 6-phase data flow" — restated here because it's the decision most likely to look "obviously improvable" by parallelizing merge/collect too. Don't: both are cheap relative to parse/resolve, and both build one shared mutable structure whose synchronization cost would exceed the sequential cost.

input.content:
Stacked on #79. Part 3 of #5 from the v1 review: family G (performance), the resolve and discovery side. Serialization at scale is separate.

## Problem

I profiled Mantine with `sample` over a 200-iteration extraction loop and instrumented the phases of `Revision::cold`.

| Cost | Samples | What happens |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `oxc_resolver::resolve` | ~6,100 | `resolve_import_specifier` resolves the same `(directory, specifier)` again for every component that touches it. |
| `deps::record` (from #75) | ~3,500 | Hashes and compares `Utf8PathBuf` component by component; Rust's `Path` `Hash`/`Eq` iterate components. |
| `NamedTypeIndex`, `ImportResolutionMap`, the re-export walk | ~3,600 | The same path hashing in every lookup. `lookup_interface` and `lookup_type_alias` also allocate `format!("React.{name}")` on every miss. |
| Discovery | ~25 ms | One `realpath` per file, more than parse and merge combined. |

## Change

- **`ResolutionContext::module_resolutions`** caches a `ModuleResolution` (package types, file or error) per `(directory, specifier)`. The cache lives for one run or one watch revision, which builds a fresh context. Dependency recording still happens on every hit.
- **`PathKey`** (`path_key.rs`) wraps a path string that hashes and compares as the string, and implements `Borrow<str>` so lookups take `path.as_str()` without allocating. It is used by:
  - the named-type index
  - the import map, including its own path-keyed copy of the re-export map; `resolve_reexport_chain` no longer takes `global`
  - the dependency recorder

  Paths are canonical, so string equality is path equality.
- **`NamedTypeIndex.react_namespaced`:** the `React.`-qualified fallback runs only for files that declare such names (`@types/react`).
- **Discovery:**
  - walks each directory's canonical path, so only symlinked files are canonicalized
  - uses the `ignore` crate's parallel walker
  - sorts and dedups files, and sorts diagnostics, so the result does not depend on thread order
- **Pipeline doc updated:** parallel phases, and the path-key and module-cache rules.

## Verification

Median of 5 runs, compared to #79's build:

| Corpus | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| react-spectrum | 150 ms | 97 ms |
| Mantine | 180 ms | 146 ms |
| shadcn | 68 ms | 51 ms |
| chakra-ui | 33 ms | 25 ms |
| Ant Design | 44 ms | 34 ms |

- Components, enums and the set of diagnostics are identical on all five corpora.
- Output is byte-identical between repeated runs on all five, so parallel discovery is deterministic.
- Discovery on Mantine drops from ~25 ms to ~7.5 ms.
- After the change, the profile's remaining top frames are file reads in the parse jobs and ~600 samples of string-hashed `deps::record`.
- `just lint` is clean; all 720 workspace tests pass, including the watch sequence test (snapshot == extract).

## Behavior change

An import resolving to a non-UTF-8 path now reports `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT`. Before, it was dropped silently.

mod streaming_serialize_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Every variant, every `OpaqueReason`, and the non-finite numbers.
    fn every_shape() -> Vec<PropType> {
        let reasons = vec![
            OpaqueReason::ConditionalType,
            OpaqueReason::MappedType,
            OpaqueReason::ModuleAugmentation,
            OpaqueReason::RuntimeDependent { function_name: "cva".into() },
            OpaqueReason::UnresolvableImport { specifier: "./missing".into() },
            OpaqueReason::PandaCodegenMissing,
            OpaqueReason::DepthExceeded,
            OpaqueReason::IndexedAccess { expression: "T[\\"k\\"]".into() },
            OpaqueReason::TemplateLiteral { expression: "`a-${B}`".into() },
            OpaqueReason::MultiParamFunction,
            OpaqueReason::UnsupportedExpression,
        ];
        let mut shapes = vec![
            PropType::String,
            PropType::Number,
            PropType::Boolean,
            PropType::Null,
            PropType::Undefined,
            PropType::Any,
            PropType::Never,
            PropType::Unknown,
            PropType::Void,
            PropType::ReactNode,
            PropType::CssProperties,
            PropType::ElementType,
            PropType::SxProps,
            PropType::StringLiteral("a \\"quoted\\" value".into()),
            PropType::NumberLiteral(1.5),
            PropType::NumberLiteral(2.0),
            PropType::NumberLiteral(f64::NAN),
            PropType::NumberLiteral(f64::INFINITY),
            PropType::NumberLiteral(f64::NEG_INFINITY),
            PropType::BoolLiteral(true),
            PropType::Union(vec![PropType::String, PropType::Null]),
            PropType::Intersection(vec![PropType::Number, PropType::Unknown]),
            PropType::Array(Box::new(PropType::Boolean)),
            PropType::Tuple(vec![PropType::Number, PropType::String]),
            PropType::Tuple(vec![]),
            PropType::Object(vec![ObjectField {
                name: "x".into(),
                prop_type: PropType::Union(vec![PropType::String, PropType::Number]),
                required: true,
                description: "The x.".into(),
            }]),
            PropType::Named { name: "Box".into(), args: vec![PropType::StringLiteral("div".into())] },
            PropType::EventHandler { event_type: "MouseEvent".into(), param_name: "event".into() },
            PropType::Ref { element: Some("HTMLDivElement".into()) },
            PropType::Ref { element: None },
            PropType::HtmlAttributes { element: "button".into(), omitted: vec!["type".into()] },
            PropType::LiteralUnion { members: vec!["sm".into(), "lg".into()], has_default: true },
        ];
        shapes.extend(reasons.into_iter().map(|reason| OpaqueDetail::new("Raw<T>", reason)));
        shapes
    }

    #[test]
    fn streamed_bytes_equal_the_value_built_wire_shape_for_every_variant() {
        for shape in every_shape() {
            let streamed = serde_json::to_string(&shape).expect("serialize");
            let reference = serde_json::to_string(&shape.to_tagged_value()).expect("serialize value");
            assert_eq!(streamed, reference, "{shape:?}");
            assert_eq!(PropType::from_tagged_value(&serde_json::from_str(&streamed).unwrap()).map(|p| format!("{p:?}")), Ok(format!("{shape:?}")));
        }
    }
}

input.content:
Stacked on #80. Family G of the v1 review: serialization dominates at scale.

## Problem

`impl Serialize for PropType` called `to_tagged_value()`, which built a `serde_json::Value` (maps, cloned strings) for every node of every prop type and then serialized that tree. On Mantine, writing the 16 MB result took longer than discovery, parse, resolve and assembly combined.

The key order of each object also came from `serde_json::Map`. That follows insertion order only because a transitive dependency (`oxc_resolver`) enables serde_json's `preserve_order` feature. Without it, every prop type's keys would silently switch to sorted order.

input.content:
Stacked on #81. Brings back the generic-alias substitution #73 deferred for cost.

## Problem

When a generic alias was a prop's type, its body was resolved with its own parameter names. `size: StyleProp<MantineSize>` came out as `Value | Value[]`, as though `Value` were a type. On Mantine, 25,624 prop-type leaves were leaked parameter names, mostly the shared style props every Box-based component inherits.

## Change

- **`resolve_named`'s type-alias branch substitutes the call site's arguments** into the alias body (`build_substitution` and `substitute_alias`) before resolving it.
  - The arguments stay pinned to the consuming file.
  - Unfilled parameters are still registered as in scope, so they don't warn.
  - An alias used without arguments is unchanged.

## Verification

- **Leaked parameter-name leaves** (named leaves with no arguments named `T`, `Value`, `Payload`, …):

  | Corpus | Before | After |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Mantine | 25,624 | 72 |
  | react-spectrum | 721 | 111 |
  | chakra-ui | 23 | 4 |
  | Ant Design | 48 | 30 |
  | shadcn | 3 | 3 |

  What remains is mostly generic components' own type parameters (`MultiSelect<Value>`), which react-docgen-typescript also leaves unresolved.
- **Snapshots:** Mantine's `classNames` keys change from `Selectors` to the real selector names, and MUI's `sx` callbacks name `Theme` instead of `T`.
- **New test** `a_generic_alias_in_prop_position_takes_the_call_sites_arguments` pins exact types for a cross-file `StyleProp<Size>` and `Maybe<string>`. Forcing the old path fails it.
- **Cost on Mantine:** 90 → 112 ms. The output grows 23% because types that were placeholders now expand. Spectrum goes 71 → 74 ms; the other corpora are within noise.
- `just lint` is clean; all 722 workspace tests pass.

content.text:
<total_tokens>14087394 tokens left</total_tokens>

Concise output style is active. Be concise: lead with the result, skip preamble and narration, keep only what the user needs.

**On stacking:** you were right that it was broken, but at the base, not in the new PRs. #57 through #82 already formed one chain. #56 (`fix/enum-determinism`) targeted `test/cache-guards`. When that branch was deleted after #53 merged, GitHub closed #56 rather than retargeting it, which left #57 sitting on an orphaned branch. GitHub won't reopen a PR whose base is gone, so I opened **#83** (`fix/enum-determinism` → `main`) to replace it. The stack is now `main ← #83 ← #57 ← … ← #82`. Merge from the bottom up. If "automatically delete head branches" is on, GitHub should retarget each next PR as its base merges.

**On AST and typing vs special cases:** it's a mix. The core is structural, but a layer of name-based rules sits around it.

Decided from structure:
- **What counts as a component:** JSX, hooks or the shape of what it returns (#71), not library names.
- **Wrapper props:** read from the call's type arguments and payload type, not from a list of wrapper names.
- **Type arguments and key sets:** type arguments are typed values (the old string parsers are gone), and `Pick`/`Omit` keys are computed from those types.
- **Everything from this round (#75–#82)** is general machinery and adds no special cases:
  - watch revisions with recorded dependencies
  - one entry per diagnostic
  - the cache fingerprint
  - the speed-ups
  - streamed JSON output
  - generic-alias substitution, which on its own cut leaked parameter names on Mantine from 25,624 to 72

Still decided by name (a count of string-literal name checks per file):

| Where | Count | What it is |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `react_types.rs` | 218 | React built-ins and HTML attribute tables |
| `known.rs` | 55 | Shortcuts for libraries: `SxProps`, `VariantProps`, `cva`, `tv`, Panda |

Some of this is fair, because there's no type checker: React and the TypeScript lib types are a fixed vocabulary. Most of it could be structural instead:
1. **The silence list** becomes "the name is declared in a TypeScript lib or `@types` file". We already load those files.
2. **The wrapper-name rules** become "the argument shows render evidence", which the generic wrapper path already does.
3. **The library shortcuts** move behind the `DocgenPlugin` hook, so the core holds no library names.
4. **A small evaluator** for `keyof` and mapped types over a known, finite set of keys replaces the per-name utility handling. It would also cover `Record` and many of the remaining opaque types.
5. **The React tables** come from `@types/react` when it's installed.

I've added this as task #7. I'd do it before the docs task (#6), measuring recall against react-docgen-typescript and the leaked-name count so nothing regresses. Say if you'd rather keep the order.

"""For each open PR: is the base tip an ancestor of the head, and how many commits does the PR carry?"""
import json, subprocess

REPO = '/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/release-0.2.0'


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.run(['/usr/bin/git', '-C', REPO, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)


prs = json.loads(subprocess.run(
    ['gh', 'pr', 'list', '--state', 'open', '--limit', '80', '--json', 'number,baseRefName,headRefName,title'],
    cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
for pr in sorted(prs, key=lambda p: p['number']):
    base, head = f"origin/{pr['baseRefName']}", f"origin/{pr['headRefName']}"
    on_base = git('merge-base', '--is-ancestor', base, head).returncode == 0
    count = git('rev-list', '--count', f'{base}..{head}').stdout.strip()
    print(f"#{pr['number']:<3} on-base={on_base!s:<5} commits={count:<3} {pr['baseRefName']} <- {pr['headRefName']}")

"""For each branch, list commits whose patch is not in main (git cherry '+'), with a content check by file."""
import subprocess, sys

REPO = '/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/release-0.2.0'


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.run(['/usr/bin/git', '-C', REPO, *args], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

    lines = git('cherry', 'origin/main', ref).splitlines()
    missing = [l.split()[1] for l in lines if l.startswith('+')]
    print(f'== {ref}: {len(lines)} ahead, {len(missing)} with no equivalent patch in main')
    for c in missing:
        subject = git('log', '-1', '--format=%h %ad %s', '--date=short', c).strip()
        # Does main already contain each file exactly as this commit left it?
        files = git('diff-tree', '--no-commit-id', '--name-only', '-r', c).split()
        same = sum(1 for f in files if git('rev-parse', f'{c}:{f}') and git('rev-parse', f'{c}:{f}') == git('rev-parse', f'origin/main:{f}'))
        print(f'   {subject}  [{same}/{len(files)} files identical in main]')

<pasted_content id="d5b8">
# Caliper v1 review — October 21, 2026

My assessment: the work is moving toward the stated architecture, but I would not treat the current PR stack as v1 ready. Claude’s “mix” description is fair. The recent changes replace several brittle mechanisms with structured data and fix real watch and cache defects. The remaining risk is that Caliper can still emit a plausible component or prop type from a name heuristic without knowing what that symbol means. That is more damaging to trust than a diagnosed omission.

I reviewed the current branch tips, PR descriptions and CI, the architecture roadmap and ADRs, and the relevant extractor, resolver, watch, serialization, and Vite paths. I did not change the working tree or run a fresh corpus benchmark. The repository’s Entire session-history search was unavailable because its Keychain access failed, so the historical account below comes from Git and PR evidence.

## What changed, and what the PR queue means

There are 27 open PRs: 25 chained PRs from #58 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/58) through #82 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/82), the 0.2.2 release PR #46 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/46), and Dependabot #84 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/84). #57 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/57) and #83 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/83) merged during this review. The #82 tip has green CI; #84 currently fails lint. Several lower PRs have queued or absent checks, so the green tip is useful evidence for the combined branch, not a substitute for testing the final merge on main.

| Work | Assessment |
|---|---|
| #58–#60 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/60), #68 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/68) | Better diagnostic vocabulary, recorded detection rules, and exact per-shape component/prop tests. Good foundations; the detection model is still spread across rules. |
| #61–#63 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/62), #69 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/69) | Meaningful gains for typed functions, wrapper calls, generic interfaces, and barrels. Wrapper detection remains an inference from arguments and names, rather than callee return semantics. |
| #65 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/65), #72–#74 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/73), #82 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/82) | The strongest semantic progress: structured type arguments, key-set evaluation, and generic substitution. These address causes of incorrect output, not just corpus-specific counts. |
| #66–#67 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/67), #75–#78 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/75) | Removed misleading options and substantially repaired watch parity, atomic snapshots, Vite refresh, and diagnostic aggregation. The incremental delta contract still has a defect described below. |
| #79–#81 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/81) | Build-aware cache invalidation and measured resolver/serialization improvements. The streaming serializer has a strong byte-equivalence test. |
| #70 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/70) | Useful TypeScript 7.1 beta probe and ADR. The checker is still not connected to core, CLI, or NAPI. |

This also corrects several findings from my prior review: the text-based type-argument parser is gone; watch publishes an atomic revision; the Vite virtual module reads the session snapshot; and an unresolved wrapper no longer vanishes merely because it has zero resolved props. Those fixes deserve credit.

## Release-significant findings

### 1. Name-based resolution can override a real local type — high

The resolver checks bare React builtin names before looking up a source declaration. A project-local ReactNode, CSSProperties, or Ref can therefore be classified as React’s type instead of the project’s type. In the props-chain path, TypeScript utility recognition likewise happens before source lookup; a locally declared Partial or Required can be treated as a utility and yield an empty chain. The later “source before known pattern” rule does not protect these earlier exits. This is a direct symbol-identity bug, not a philosophical objection to tables. See named.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/resolver/named.rs#L68-L79) and chain.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs#L65-L83).

Fix before v1: resolve the binding first. Apply a builtin interpretation only when its origin is known, or as an explicit fallback when resolution fails; report that fallback.

### 2. “Render evidence” is useful, but weaker than the claim made for it — high

#71 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/71) reduces false positives. Its implementation still accepts JSX anywhere in a function body, including a nested callback or an expression never returned. It also accepts a returned null, a call whose spelling begins with a capital letter or use, and an element-like return annotation by its rightmost name, without resolving the symbol. A typed FormatName that constructs unused JSX and returns a string can pass the detector. A custom imported type named ReactNode can pass the return-annotation check. See evidence.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/extractor/evidence.rs#L16-L157).

The wrapper path additionally treats a PascalCase argument as a component and chooses a props argument because it is declared locally or ends in Props; it does not establish that the callee returns a component. The rename path still accepts memo, observer, names containing Component or forwardref, withX, and any curried call. See wrapper.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/extractor/wrapper.rs#L81-L197) and component.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/extractor/component.rs#L569-L586).

This matters because #62 explicitly turned the roadmap’s default-off guessing tier on (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/62) based largely on a Mantine comparison. #71’s later measurements (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/71) report 109 Ant Design and 233 Spectrum entries beyond RDT. Those are not automatically false positives—RDT is an imperfect oracle—but they have not been hand-labeled to satisfy the roadmap’s 95% precision gate per family. I would hold further detector expansion until that gate exists.

### 3. The watch snapshot is correct in cases where its incremental event is wrong — high

#75 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/75) tests that a full snapshot matches a cold extraction after edits. The delta is assembled only from freshly resolved components. Consider two components named X in different files. Delete the file whose X held the bare key: the surviving, kept component moves from X (file) to X, but is absent from updatedComponents. The event removes X (file) while the old X remains in a client applying the documented delta. Creating an earlier same-named component produces the inverse loss. The complete virtual-module reload can mask this for one Vite consumer; the public event contract remains wrong. The same delta carries current diagnostics but no explicit removals for diagnostics that disappeared. # Caliper v1 review — October 21, 2026

My assessment: the work is moving toward the stated architecture, but I would not treat the current PR stack as v1 ready. Claude’s “mix” description is fair. The recent changes replace several brittle mechanisms with structured data and fix real watch and cache defects. The remaining risk is that Caliper can still emit a plausible component or prop type from a name heuristic without knowing what that symbol means. That is more damaging to trust than a diagnosed omission.

I reviewed the current branch tips, PR descriptions and CI, the architecture roadmap and ADRs, and the relevant extractor, resolver, watch, serialization, and Vite paths. I did not change the working tree or run a fresh corpus benchmark. The repository’s Entire session-history search was unavailable because its Keychain access failed, so the historical account below comes from Git and PR evidence.

## What changed, and what the PR queue means

There are 27 open PRs: 25 chained PRs from #58 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/58) through #82 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/82), the 0.2.2 release PR #46 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/46), and Dependabot #84 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/84). #57 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/57) and #83 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/83) merged during this review. The #82 tip has green CI; #84 currently fails lint. Several lower PRs have queued or absent checks, so the green tip is useful evidence for the combined branch, not a substitute for testing the final merge on main.

| Work | Assessment |
|---|---|
| #58–#60 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/60), #68 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/68) | Better diagnostic vocabulary, recorded detection rules, and exact per-shape component/prop tests. Good foundations; the detection model is still spread across rules. |
| #61–#63 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/62), #69 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/69) | Meaningful gains for typed functions, wrapper calls, generic interfaces, and barrels. Wrapper detection remains an inference from arguments and names, rather than callee return semantics. |
| #65 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/65), #72–#74 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/73), #82 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/82) | The strongest semantic progress: structured type arguments, key-set evaluation, and generic substitution. These address causes of incorrect output, not just corpus-specific counts. |
| #66–#67 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/67), #75–#78 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/75) | Removed misleading options and substantially repaired watch parity, atomic snapshots, Vite refresh, and diagnostic aggregation. The incremental delta contract still has a defect described below. |
| #79–#81 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/81) | Build-aware cache invalidation and measured resolver/serialization improvements. The streaming serializer has a strong byte-equivalence test. |
| #70 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/70) | Useful TypeScript 7.1 beta probe and ADR. The checker is still not connected to core, CLI, or NAPI. |

This also corrects several findings from my prior review: the text-based type-argument parser is gone; watch publishes an atomic revision; the Vite virtual module reads the session snapshot; and an unresolved wrapper no longer vanishes merely because it has zero resolved props. Those fixes deserve credit.

## Release-significant findings

### 1. Name-based resolution can override a real local type — high

The resolver checks bare React builtin names before looking up a source declaration. A project-local ReactNode, CSSProperties, or Ref can therefore be classified as React’s type instead of the project’s type. In the props-chain path, TypeScript utility recognition likewise happens before source lookup; a locally declared Partial or Required can be treated as a utility and yield an empty chain. The later “source before known pattern” rule does not protect these earlier exits. This is a direct symbol-identity bug, not a philosophical objection to tables. See named.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/resolver/named.rs#L68-L79) and chain.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/resolver/chain.rs#L65-L83).

Fix before v1: resolve the binding first. Apply a builtin interpretation only when its origin is known, or as an explicit fallback when resolution fails; report that fallback.

### 2. “Render evidence” is useful, but weaker than the claim made for it — high

#71 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/71) reduces false positives. Its implementation still accepts JSX anywhere in a function body, including a nested callback or an expression never returned. It also accepts a returned null, a call whose spelling begins with a capital letter or use, and an element-like return annotation by its rightmost name, without resolving the symbol. A typed FormatName that constructs unused JSX and returns a string can pass the detector. A custom imported type named ReactNode can pass the return-annotation check. See evidence.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/extractor/evidence.rs#L16-L157).

The wrapper path additionally treats a PascalCase argument as a component and chooses a props argument because it is declared locally or ends in Props; it does not establish that the callee returns a component. The rename path still accepts memo, observer, names containing Component or forwardref, withX, and any curried call. See wrapper.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/extractor/wrapper.rs#L81-L197) and component.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/extractor/component.rs#L569-L586).

This matters because #62 explicitly turned the roadmap’s default-off guessing tier on (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/62) based largely on a Mantine comparison. #71’s later measurements (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/71) report 109 Ant Design and 233 Spectrum entries beyond RDT. Those are not automatically false positives—RDT is an imperfect oracle—but they have not been hand-labeled to satisfy the roadmap’s 95% precision gate per family. I would hold further detector expansion until that gate exists.

### 3. The watch snapshot is correct in cases where its incremental event is wrong — high

#75 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/75) tests that a full snapshot matches a cold extraction after edits. The delta is assembled only from freshly resolved components. Consider two components named X in different files. Delete the file whose X held the bare key: the surviving, kept component moves from X (file) to X, but is absent from updatedComponents. The event removes X (file) while the old X remains in a client applying the documented delta. Creating an earlier same-named component produces the inverse loss. The complete virtual-module reload can mask this for one Vite consumer; the public event contract remains wrong. The same delta carries current diagnostics but no explicit removals for diagnostics that disappeared. See Revision::next (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/pipeline/revision.rs#L316-L361) and the Vite event contract (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/packages/vite-plugin/src/index.ts#L18-L26).

Add tests that apply every emitted delta to the prior output and compare the result with snapshot(), including name collisions, diagnostic disappearance, and two different files updating concurrently. The Vite plugin guards ordering per file; an older update from another file can still be sent after a newer revision.

### 4. The semantic-backend contract has an unresolved contradiction — high

ADR 0007 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/docs/adr/0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) says a structural entry wins on a clash. The integration design (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/docs/type-checker-integration.md) says checker props replace structural props. That distinction may mean “structural identity wins, checker props may replace,” but the merge contract does not say so. It must specify component identity, field-level precedence, diagnostic retirement, provenance, and what happens when the checker and OXC disagree.

The proposed trigger is also incomplete: it includes “a callee-added prop [the structural pass] cannot see,” yet there is no way for the structural pass to flag an unseen prop. Bare generic names and silent terminal types also avoid degradation diagnostics. Triggering only on visible incompleteness will miss precisely some cases the checker is meant to repair. Finally, schemaVersion should identify the wire schema, not whether discovery ran; mode and provenance need separate fields.

The official TypeScript 7.1 beta announcement (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-1-beta/) now documents typescript/sync, /async, and /fs. Caliper’s beta smoke test is timely, but its own integration document (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/docs/type-checker-integration.md) says full beta parity, Rust-client cost, large-project behavior, and several lifecycle gates remain open. I would settle the merge contract before adding more structural guesses.

### 5. Silent or lossy output remains in named shortcuts — medium to high

The “silent no-op” list leaves utility, DOM, and HTML names unexpanded by spelling, even when their actual declaration or provenance has not been established. known.rs maps React Aria RenderProps to scalar className and style props while deliberately omitting a function-valued form; that can misdescribe a consumer’s accepted values without an opacity diagnostic. See named.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/resolver/named.rs#L131-L174) and known.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/known.rs#L108-L137).

A separate, older path parses tsconfig.json aliases with a hand-written line-comment stripper; block comments or read/parse failure result in no aliases and no diagnostic. That is a common configuration shape and violates the project’s stated “diagnose degradation” rule. See react.rs (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/resolver/react.rs#L153-L205).

### 6. Performance and resource gates need to be applied to the finished feature — medium

#80 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/80) and #81 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/81) show convincing gains. #82 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/82) then increases Mantine’s measured run from 90 to 112 ms and output size by 23% while fixing generic types. That may be a good trade, but it crosses the roadmap’s proposed “15 ms or 20%” regression gate relative to its immediate predecessor. The “25,624 leaked parameter-name leaves to 72” result is strong evidence that substitution is working; it is not a prop-accuracy or end-user correctness metric.

Watch edits now clone the global source/index state and reassemble every output component, including rerunning component plugin hooks, even when only one component is resolved again. #75’s own measurements (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/75) show a Mantine leaf edit rising from 8.3 to 13.5 ms. This is a reasonable correctness-first design, but it needs a large-project latency and memory gate before “fast incremental” becomes a v1 promise. The dependency recorder is thread-local and implicit, so a new resolver lookup can silently omit an invalidation edge unless tested.

For security and robustness, the DTS cache loader (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/crates/core/src/cache.rs#L153-L189) reads and deserializes the entire local cache before applying any entry bound. A malformed or oversized cache can consume substantial memory. I found no basis to call this a remote exploit; it is a resource bound to add if CI or user workspaces may contain untrusted cache files.

## How I would handle Claude’s five proposals

| Proposal | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Replace silence list with “declared in lib or @types” | Use symbol origin, but do not make every dependency declaration terminal. Many @types aliases are precisely what Caliper should follow. Record why resolution stopped. |
| Replace wrapper names with argument render evidence | Insufficient alone. Arguments can be components while the callee returns a string, config, or context. Use callee declaration/signature when structural data permits; otherwise label the result inferred and measure precision. |
| Move library shortcuts to DocgenPlugin | Requires a new boundary. Today’s plugin hooks run after file extraction or after a component is resolved; they cannot decide a type during resolution. Define a version-aware type-resolution adapter/preset before moving these rules. |
| Add a finite keyof/mapped-type evaluator | Yes, within a budget. #73 is a good start. Specify supported finite operations, depth/cost limits, and an opaque diagnostic for unknown keys. Avoid gradually implementing a second TypeScript checker. |
| Read React tables from installed @types/react | Use installed declarations where requested and available, with a curated fallback. A blanket dependency would make the fast default vary with installed React versions and package layout. Binding identity must be fixed first. |

## What would prove Caliper’s value over RDT

The strongest case is fast structural extraction with useful typed output, explicit degradation, and reliable incremental updates, plus an opt-in checker for the cases structural analysis cannot answer. Raw component counts alone do not prove that case. The roadmap currently mixes “own props,” “any props,” source-only mirrors, and different baselines; #71 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/71) itself reports 87% Mantine and 80% Chakra recall(any) while the roadmap (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/docs/projects/architecture-roadmap.md) highlights higher own-prop figures. Publish one reproducible scorecard with both measures, hand-labeled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, diagnostics, wall time, peak RSS, and watch parity. Run it with dependencies installed as well as on source-only mirrors.

The comparison should keep RDT’s actual output as a compatibility oracle, while separately marking RDT mistakes and product-policy differences. The existing benchmark document (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/docs/benchmarks.md) dates to July and the status page (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/blob/1bae571b/docs/STATUS.md) to September; both need a current, reconciled release claim. TypeScript 7’s native checker and 7.1 API make the long-term speed comparison a moving target, so the structured output, diagnostics, and dependable watch contract matter as much as the multiplier.

## Recommended decision

1. Keep the structural fixes and measured serializer improvements. They are substantive, and #82’s substitution addresses a real semantic error.
2. Block a v1 readiness claim on symbol precedence, delta reconstruction, a hand-labeled detector precision gate, and the semantic merge/trigger contract.
3. Freeze new library shortcuts and wrapper heuristics until those gates show which gaps genuinely require them.
4. Land the stack in reviewable cohorts, then run CI and the complete corpus on the resulting main. Treat #46 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/46) as a separate publishing decision: merging it publishes packages. Resolve #84’s (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/84) lint failure independently.

The core concern is justified, but the direction is recoverable: the newest PRs contain genuine architecture work. The v1 risk is allowing the remaining guesses and comparison numbers to stand in for a precise contract about what Caliper knows, infers, and cannot yet resolve.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

# caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

A Vite plugin that exposes your React components' props on a virtual module and updates it through HMR as you edit.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

docgen.components['Button'].props
```

On every change the virtual module reloads with the same output a fresh extraction would give, including removed components, enums and diagnostics. To apply changes yourself, listen for the update event:

```ts
import.meta.hot?.on(
  'caliper-docgen:update',
  ({ revision, updatedKeys, updatedComponents, removedKeys, diagnostics }) => {
    // Delete removedKeys, then set updatedKeys[i] to updatedComponents[i]. Ignore a revision older than one applied.
  },
)
```

In `vite build --watch`, a change to any file under `srcDirs` triggers a rebuild, even one no bundle module imports. A build fails if extraction fails.

Extraction runs on OXC through [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi), so a single-file update takes about 2ms. Requires Vite 7 or 8. The module uses the canonical output format, not the `react-docgen-typescript` shape.

Docs and benchmarks: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

FSL-1.1-MIT. Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.

Stacked on #82. Fixes finding 3 of the October 21 review: the watch snapshot was right, but the incremental event could be wrong.

## Problem

- **A kept component whose key moved was left out of the delta.** Take two components named `X` in different files. Delete the file whose `X` held the bare key: the surviving `X` moves from `X (file)` to `X`. The update carried `removedKeys: ["X (file)"]` but did not update `X`, so a client applying the delta kept the deleted component under `X`. Creating an earlier-sorting `X` lost data the other way.
- **Fixed diagnostics never left a client's list.** `diagnostics` re-sent the changed file's current diagnostics, with no list of removals.
- **The Vite plugin could deliver updates out of order.** It guarded ordering per file only, so an older update from one file could arrive after a newer one from another. Each update is a delta, so order matters.

## Change

- **`Revision::next` reports as updated every key that now points at a different component:**
  - every re-resolved component
  - every kept component whose key changed (`self.keys[id] != next.keys[id]`)

  Both are looked up by `ComponentId`, so this costs one hash lookup per component.
- **Diagnostics:** `IncrementalUpdate.diagnostics` holds the diagnostics a revision added; the new `removed_diagnostics` holds the ones it no longer has. Both are set differences over the assembled outputs.
- **Vite plugin:** `inOrder` queues each change and announces it before the next one starts. Events therefore leave in revision order across files, and a failed change does not block later ones. This replaces the per-file sequence guard. `CaliperDocgenUpdate` gains `removedDiagnostics`.
- **Docs:** the contract is documented on `IncrementalUpdate`, `CaliperDocgenUpdate`, the plugin README and the pipeline doc.

## Verification

- **`every_kind_of_change_leaves_the_snapshot_equal_to_a_cold_extract` now also rebuilds the output from the updates.** At each step it applies every update to a client copy and asserts its components and diagnostics equal `snapshot()`. Four new steps cover:
  - colliding with a component from a file that sorts first
  - deleting the component that holds the bare key
  - breaking the colliding file
  - fixing it

  With the moved-key rule disabled, the test fails at "collide with the moved component from a file that sorts first", which is the review's scenario.
- **Panic tests:** the two tests that relied on an update re-reporting an existing panic now check the snapshot. The panic was already reported by the cold run, so under the new contract it is not "added".
- **Vite unit tests:**
  - a second file's change is not applied until the first is announced
  - events go out as `[2, Button], [3, Input]`
  - a failed change does not block the next

  The integration tier on the native binding passes 5/5.
- `just lint` is clean; all 722 workspace tests and the 39 plugin unit tests pass.

## Breaking

`IncrementalUpdate.diagnostics` now means "added by this revision", and `removedDiagnostics` is new. This affects the NAPI and plugin event payloads.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

Stacked on #87. Fixes finding 1 of the October 21 review: name-based resolution could override a real local type.

## Problem

Several resolver exits matched a name's spelling before looking up what the name was bound to:

- `resolve_named` checked React builtins first.
- `resolve_props_chain` built `Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required` and `PropsWithChildren` (and silently emptied other utilities) before its source lookup.
- `ExtendsRef::Builtin` came from the extractor, which names builtins by spelling before it has seen the whole file.

As a result, a project's own `ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, `Ref`, `Partial` or `Required` was read as React's or TypeScript's type, or produced an empty chain. The later "source before known pattern" rule never ran for these exits.

## Change

`resolver::name_binding(name, file)` classifies a name as declared in this file, imported (with its specifier), or unbound. For a qualified name, the namespace's import decides. Each builtin check now asks this first:

| Check | Builtin meaning applies when |
| --- | --- |
| React builtins (`may_be_react_builtin`) | the name is imported from `react`, `react/*` or `@types/react`, or is unbound; user-configured `extraBuiltins` stay name-based |
| TypeScript lib utilities (`may_be_ts_lib_type`) | the name is unbound; these are globals and never imported |
| Utility synthesis (`may_be_utility`) | `PropsWithChildren` and `PropsWithRef` have React's binding; TypeScript's utilities are unbound |
| `ExtendsRef::Builtin` | the name has React's binding. A different binding resolves as its declaration when `declaration_resolves`. |

**Reported fallback.** If the name is bound elsewhere and that binding can't be resolved (a re-export of React's type, a package not installed), React's meaning is still used, with an `Info` `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` diagnostic naming the binding.

## Verification

- **New tests:**
  - a local `ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, `Partial` and `Required` resolve exactly as declared; forcing the old spelling-first path fails this test
  - `ReactNode` imported from `react`, and `React.ReactNode`, keep React's meaning
  - a `ReactNode` re-exported through `./types` falls back to React's meaning with one diagnostic naming `./types`
- **Corpora, compared to #82's build:**
  - the only output change is Mantine's `style` props, which now name Mantine's own `interface CSSProperties extends React.CSSProperties` (in `Box.types.ts`) instead of React's
  - antd, chakra-ui, shadcn and react-spectrum components are identical. Two regressions from a first draft are covered: `React.PropsWithChildren` must be React's, and spectrum's uninstalled `DOMAttributes` must fall back.
  - the fallback fires 29 times, all on react-spectrum's source-only mirror, for types from `@react-types/shared`, which isn't installed. These guesses were silent before.
- Snapshots are unchanged. `just lint` is clean; all 725 workspace tests pass.
