content.text:
I've finished the PR cleanup and the first two of Codex's high-severity findings. The rest is still open.

**PR cleanup:** the bottom of the stack (#83, #57–#66) was merged, but `main` received different commits for the same changes than the branch #67 was built on, which caused #67's conflict. The conflict was in `pipeline/mod.rs`, where `fix/watch-parity` had refactored code that `main` had in its older form. I resolved it to the branch's version, then merged each branch into the next one up to #82, with no force-pushes. All open PRs are mergeable, and the top of the stack has exactly the same content as before.

**Codex's review:** I checked its high-severity findings against the code, and they hold. Two are fixed, each stacked on the one below:

- **#87, finding 3 (the watch update contract).** A component whose output key moved, because a same-named component in another file appeared or was deleted, was missing from the update. Clients applying updates kept a stale entry. Updates now carry `removedDiagnostics` too, and `diagnostics` only the new ones. The Vite plugin now sends events strictly in revision order across files. The sequence test applies every update and checks the result equals the snapshot; it fails on Codex's exact scenario without the fix.
- **#89, finding 1 (names overriding real types).** A project's own `ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, `Partial` or `Required` is now resolved as that declaration before any builtin meaning applies. If a name is bound to something that can't be found, React's meaning is still used, with a diagnostic; this fires 29 times on react-spectrum, where `@react-types/shared` isn't installed. On the corpora, the only output change is Mantine's own `CSSProperties`, which is correct.
- **Breaking change:** #87 changes `IncrementalUpdate` for NAPI and Vite consumers: `diagnostics` now holds only added ones, alongside the new `removedDiagnostics`.

All 725 tests pass and lint is clean on both branches.

**Still open, from Codex's review:**

| Task | What | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #10 | Count only JSX that's actually returned, plus a hand-labelled precision check per detection rule | I'm holding new detection heuristics until this exists, as Codex advises |
| #11 | Silent degradations: tsconfig comments, the React Aria `RenderProps` shortcut, cache size bound | |
| #6 | ADR on how the TypeScript-checker backend's results merge with structural ones, plus one reproducible scorecard | |
| #7 | Remaining name-based rules | Revised to follow Codex's table, after #10 |

Codex also flags that #82 raised Mantine's run from 90 to 112 ms, past the roadmap's 15 ms / 20% regression gate. It traded time for correctness, but I'd like you to accept that or set the gate before release.

name: stacked-pr-retargeting
description: In caliper, stacked PRs get closed when a parent merges and its branch is deleted; retarget children to main as soon as their parent merges
metadata:

The user wants PRs stacked, and merges them from the bottom while branches get deleted. GitHub then closes any PR whose base branch disappears (it happened to #56 and #89), and commits get rewritten on the way into main, so a closed child cannot simply be reopened.

- #46: the release PR, still waiting on your decision

That includes through conditionals, `&&`, arrays and calls such as `items.map(i => <li/>)` or `createPortal(...)`, and a local initialized with JSX and then returned.

- Across the five calibration corpora this drops one component, antd's `QRcodeStatus`. It returns the result of a render function chosen at runtime, which only its type shows to be an element.

input.content:
Fixes finding 2 of the October 21 review, first half: render evidence was weaker than claimed. The precision gate per detection rule follows in a separate PR.

## Problem

`RenderFinder` accepted any of these as evidence that a function renders:

- JSX anywhere in the function's body, including a nested callback or a value never returned
- an element factory call anywhere
- an element-like return annotation, matched only by its rightmost name

So a typed `FormatName` that builds unused JSX and returns a string passed. So did a function whose return type is a `ReactNode` imported from some other module.

## Change

- **The function's own `return`s decide** (nested functions excluded), or for an arrow, its expression body. A returned value counts when:
  - JSX or an element factory (`createElement`, `cloneElement`, `jsx*`, `createPortal`) is reachable from the value, through conditionals, `&&`, arrays and call arguments (`items.map(i => <li/>)`), but not through an object literal
  - it is a local initialized with such a value (`const content = <div/>; return content`)
  - it is `null`, `children`, or a component call
- **A top-level hook call still counts:** only components and hooks may call hooks, and a PascalCase function is not a hook.
- **Return annotations:** `ReactNode`, `ReactElement`, `ReactPortal` and `JSX.Element` count only when the leftmost name is imported from `react` (or `react/*`) or not imported at all. `ExtractorVisitor::may_be_react` supplies that check to every caller.

## Verification

- **Negative tests** extend `typed_functions_that_never_render_are_declined_with_the_reason`. Each is now declined with its reason:
  - `Label` builds JSX and returns a string
  - `Columns` returns an object of JSX
  - `OnLater` has JSX only in a callback
  - `Typed` is annotated with a `ReactNode` imported from `./my-types`
- **New positive test** `components_whose_returned_value_holds_an_element_are_detected` covers:
  - a returned local
  - `.map(...)`
  - early `null` plus a ternary
  - `&&`
  - an annotation imported from `react`
  - `React.ReactNode`
- **Corpora,** compared to `main`: exactly one component drops, antd's `QRcodeStatus`. It returns `mergedStatusRender(...)`, a render function chosen at runtime, which only its type shows returns an element. I'm accepting that loss as the review advises; the checker backend is the way to recover it.
- Snapshots are unchanged. `just lint` is clean; all 723 workspace tests pass.

"""Count components per detection rule and draw a stratified sample for hand labelling.

Writes sample.json: [{id, corpus, rule, key, file, line_hint, snippet}], up to N per (rule) spread across corpora,
seeded so it is reproducible. Usage: precision_sample.py BIN [N]
"""
import collections, json, random, re, subprocess, sys

BIN = sys.argv[1]
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 25
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
OUT = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/precision'
rng = random.Random(20261021)

by_rule = collections.defaultdict(list)
counts = collections.Counter()
for corpus in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    d = json.loads(subprocess.run([BIN, 'extract', '--src', f'{IN}/{corpus}', '--json'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
    for key, comp in d['components'].items():
        rule = comp.get('detectedBy', '?')
        counts[(corpus, rule)] += 1
        by_rule[rule].append((corpus, key, comp['displayName'], comp['filePath']))

rules = sorted({r for _, r in counts})
print('rule'.ljust(26), ''.join(c.rjust(9) for c in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']), 'total'.rjust(7))
for r in rules:
    row = [counts[(c, r)] for c in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']]
    print(r.ljust(26), ''.join(str(x).rjust(9) for x in row), str(sum(row)).rjust(7))


def snippet(path, name):
    try:
        lines = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read().splitlines()
    except OSError:
        return '', 0
    bare = name.split('.')[-1].split('/')[-1]
    pat = re.compile(r'\b' + re.escape(bare) + r'\b')
    idx = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if pat.search(l) and re.search(r'(const|function|class|let|var|export)', l)), None)
    if idx is None:
        idx = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if pat.search(l)), 0)
    lo, hi = max(0, idx - 3), min(len(lines), idx + 40)
    return '\n'.join(f'{i + 1:5} {lines[i]}' for i in range(lo, hi)), idx + 1


sample = []
for rule, items in sorted(by_rule.items()):
    picked = items if len(items) <= N else rng.sample(items, N)
    for corpus, key, name, path in picked:
        text, line = snippet(path, name)
        sample.append({'id': len(sample), 'corpus': corpus, 'rule': rule, 'key': key, 'name': name, 'file': path,
                       'line': line, 'snippet': text})
import os
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
json.dump(sample, open(f'{OUT}/sample.json', 'w'), indent=1)
print('sampled', len(sample), 'to', f'{OUT}/sample.json')

def snippet(path, name):

        return '', 0
    bare = name.split('.')[-1].split('/')[-1]
    pat = re.compile(r'\b' + re.escape(bare) + r'\b')
    idx = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if pat.search(l) and re.search(r'(const|function|class|let|var|export)', l)), None)

        idx = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if pat.search(l)), 0)
    lo, hi = max(0, idx - 3), min(len(lines), idx + 40)
    return '\n'.join(f'{i + 1:5} {lines[i]}' for i in range(lo, hi)), idx + 1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Draw a reproducible per-rule sample of detected components for precision labelling.

Runs `caliper-docgen extract --json` on every subdirectory of CORPORA, counts components by `detectedBy`, and writes
up to N per rule (seeded) with a source snippet to OUT/sample.json. Label each item `component`, `not_component` or
`unsure`, then report precision per rule as docs/precision.md does.

Usage: scripts/precision-sample.py BIN CORPORA OUT [N]
"""
import collections
import json
import os
import random
import re
import subprocess
import sys

SEED = 20261021


def snippet(path, name):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.read().splitlines()
    except OSError:
        return '', 0
    bare = re.split(r'[./]', name)[-1]
    word = re.compile(r'\b' + re.escape(bare) + r'\b')
    declaration = re.compile(r'\b(const|function|class|let|var|export)\b')
    idx = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if word.search(l) and declaration.search(l)), None)

# Detection precision

How often a component Caliper reports really is one, per detection rule (`detectedBy` in the output). The roadmap's gate is 95% per rule before a rule's detections count toward recall or before the rule is extended.

## Method

`scripts/precision-sample.py` runs `extract` on each corpus, groups components by `detectedBy`, and draws up to 25 per rule with a fixed seed. Each item was labelled `component`, `not_component` or `unsure` from its source: a component is something a consumer can render as `<Name />`.

The 2026-10-21 sample was labelled by four model agents reading each item's snippet and, where needed, the file. Those labels are not yet checked by a human.

## Results, 2026-10-21

Corpora: the five source-only mirrors (Mantine, chakra-ui, Ant Design, shadcn/ui, react-spectrum), with render evidence as in #91.

| Rule | Detected | Sampled | Not a component | Precision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `functionDeclaration` | 2,985 | 25 | 1 | 96% |
| `wrapperTypeArgument` | 701 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `hocWrapper` | 367 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `forwardRef` | 185 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `fcAnnotation` | 119 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `typedFunctionExpression` | 106 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `classComponent` | 4 | 4 | 0 | 100% |

The miss: react-spectrum's `ListBoxDropIndicatorWrapper` is a `(props, ref)` render function handed to `DropIndicatorContext` and called, not rendered.

## What this does and does not show

- No rule shows a precision problem: 1 miss in 154.
- 25 samples cannot establish the 95% gate. With no misses in 25, the 95% lower bound is about 88%; showing 95% needs about 60 clean samples per rule (rule of three). The two inferred rules, `typedFunctionExpression` and `wrapperTypeArgument`, are the ones to grow first.
- Precision only: this says nothing about components Caliper misses (recall) or about whether their props are right.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Draw a reproducible per-rule sample of detected components for precision labelling.

Runs `caliper-docgen extract --json` on every subdirectory of CORPORA, counts components by `detectedBy`, and writes
up to N per rule (seeded) with a source snippet to OUT/sample.json. Label each item `component`, `not_component` or
`unsure`, then report precision per rule as docs/precision.md does.

Usage: scripts/precision-sample.py BIN CORPORA OUT [N]
"""
import collections
import json
import os
import random
import re
import subprocess
import sys

SEED = 20261021


def snippet(path, name):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.read().splitlines()
    except OSError:
        return '', 0
    bare = re.split(r'[./]', name)[-1]
    word = re.compile(r'\b' + re.escape(bare) + r'\b')
    declaration = re.compile(r'\b(const|function|class|let|var|export)\b')
    idx = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if word.search(l) and declaration.search(l)), None)
    if idx is None:
        idx = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if word.search(l)), 0)
    lo, hi = max(0, idx - 3), min(len(lines), idx + 40)
    return '\n'.join(f'{i + 1:5} {lines[i]}' for i in range(lo, hi)), idx + 1


def main():
    binary, corpora, out = sys.argv[1:4]
    per_rule = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 25
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    names = sorted(d for d in os.listdir(corpora) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(corpora, d)))
    by_rule = collections.defaultdict(list)
    counts = collections.Counter()
    for corpus in names:
        run = subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', os.path.join(corpora, corpus), '--json'],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
        for comp in json.loads(run.stdout)['components'].values():
            rule = comp.get('detectedBy', '?')
            counts[(corpus, rule)] += 1
            by_rule[rule].append((corpus, comp['displayName'], comp['filePath']))
    print('rule'.ljust(26) + ''.join(c[:9].rjust(10) for c in names) + 'total'.rjust(8))
    for rule in sorted(by_rule):
        row = [counts[(c, rule)] for c in names]
        print(rule.ljust(26) + ''.join(str(x).rjust(10) for x in row) + str(sum(row)).rjust(8))
    sample = []
    for rule, items in sorted(by_rule.items()):
        for corpus, name, path in items if len(items) <= per_rule else rng.sample(items, per_rule):
            text, line = snippet(path, name)
            sample.append({'id': len(sample), 'corpus': corpus, 'rule': rule, 'name': name, 'file': path,
                           'line': line, 'snippet': text})
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(out, 'sample.json'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        json.dump(sample, f, indent=1)
    print(f'sampled {len(sample)} to {os.path.join(out, "sample.json")}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# Detection precision

How often a component Caliper reports really is one, per detection rule (`detectedBy` in the output). The roadmap's gate is 95% per rule before a rule's detections count toward recall or before the rule is extended.

## Method

`scripts/precision-sample.py` runs `extract` on each corpus, groups components by `detectedBy`, and draws up to 25 per rule with a fixed seed. Each item was labelled `component`, `not_component` or `unsure` from its source: a component is something a consumer can render as `<Name />`.

The 2026-10-21 sample was labelled by four model agents reading each item's snippet and, where needed, the file. Those labels are not yet checked by a human.

## Results, 2026-10-21

Corpora: the five source-only mirrors (Mantine, chakra-ui, Ant Design, shadcn/ui, react-spectrum), with render evidence as in #91.

| Rule | Detected | Sampled | Not a component | Precision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `functionDeclaration` | 2,985 | 25 | 1 | 96% |
| `wrapperTypeArgument` | 701 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `hocWrapper` | 367 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `forwardRef` | 185 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `fcAnnotation` | 119 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `typedFunctionExpression` | 106 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `classComponent` | 4 | 4 | 0 | 100% |

The miss: react-spectrum's `ListBoxDropIndicatorWrapper` is a `(props, ref)` render function handed to `DropIndicatorContext` and called, not rendered.

## What this does and does not show

- No rule shows a precision problem: 1 miss in 154.
- 25 samples cannot establish the 95% gate. With no misses in 25, the 95% lower bound is about 88%; showing 95% needs about 60 clean samples per rule (rule of three). The two inferred rules, `typedFunctionExpression` and `wrapperTypeArgument`, are the ones to grow first.
- Precision only: this says nothing about components Caliper misses (recall) or about whether their props are right.

Finding 2 of the October 21 review, second half: no rule had a measured precision, so the roadmap's 95% gate could not be applied. Independent of #91; both target `main`.

## Change

- **`ComponentEntry.detected_by` (`detectedBy` in JSON):** the extractor rule that recognized the component. Consumers can tell explicit declaration forms (`functionDeclaration`, `forwardRef`, `fcAnnotation`, ...) from inferences (`typedFunctionExpression`, `wrapperTypeArgument`). It is in the JSON schema, `index.d.ts` and the types doc.
- **`DetectionRule` serializes in camelCase.** That changed the parse cache's bytes, because `rmp_serde` encodes enum variants by name (the old doc comment said "by position"), so `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` goes to 14 per the golden test. The doc comment is corrected.
- **`scripts/precision-sample.py`** draws a seeded, per-rule sample with source snippets from any set of corpora.
- **`docs/precision.md`** gives the method, the first results and their limits.

## First results

154 sampled detections across the five calibration corpora: 153 are components.

| Rule | Detected | Sampled | Misses | Precision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `functionDeclaration` | 2,985 | 25 | 1 | 96% |
| `wrapperTypeArgument` | 701 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `hocWrapper` | 367 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `forwardRef` | 185 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `fcAnnotation` | 119 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `typedFunctionExpression` | 106 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `classComponent` | 4 | 4 | 0 | 100% |

The one miss is react-spectrum's `ListBoxDropIndicatorWrapper`, a `(props, ref)` render function that is called, not rendered.

**Limits, stated in the doc:**

- The labels come from model agents reading the source, not yet checked by a human.
- 25 per rule cannot establish 95%: with no misses, the 95% lower bound is about 88%. About 60 clean samples per rule are needed; the two inferred rules should grow first.

## Verification

- All 8 snapshots gain `detectedBy`. The cache golden snapshot changes in its schema line and bytes.
- The trycmd `schema` snapshot gains the enum.
- `just lint` is clean; all 722 workspace tests pass.

input.content:
Finding 2 of the October 21 review, second half: no rule had a measured precision, so the roadmap's 95% gate could not be applied. Independent of #91; both target `main`.

## Change

- **`ComponentEntry.detected_by` (`detectedBy` in JSON):** the extractor rule that recognized the component. Consumers can tell explicit declaration forms (`functionDeclaration`, `forwardRef`, `fcAnnotation`, ...) from inferences (`typedFunctionExpression`, `wrapperTypeArgument`). It is in the JSON schema, `index.d.ts` and the types doc.
- **`DetectionRule` serializes in camelCase.** That changed the parse cache's bytes, because `rmp_serde` encodes enum variants by name (the old doc comment said "by position"), so `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` goes to 14 per the golden test. The doc comment is corrected.
- **`scripts/precision-sample.py`** draws a seeded, per-rule sample with source snippets from any set of corpora.
- **`docs/precision.md`** gives the method, the first results and their limits.

## First results

154 sampled detections across the five calibration corpora: 153 are components.

| Rule | Detected | Sampled | Misses | Precision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `functionDeclaration` | 2,985 | 25 | 1 | 96% |
| `wrapperTypeArgument` | 701 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `hocWrapper` | 367 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `forwardRef` | 185 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `fcAnnotation` | 119 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `typedFunctionExpression` | 106 | 25 | 0 | 100% |
| `classComponent` | 4 | 4 | 0 | 100% |

The one miss is react-spectrum's `ListBoxDropIndicatorWrapper`, a `(props, ref)` render function that is called, not rendered.

**Limits, stated in the doc:**

- The labels come from model agents reading the source, not yet checked by a human.
- 25 per rule cannot establish 95%: with no misses, the 95% lower bound is about 88%. About 60 clean samples per rule are needed; the two inferred rules should grow first.

## Verification

- All 8 snapshots gain `detectedBy`. The cache golden snapshot changes in its schema line and bytes.
- The trycmd `schema` snapshot gains the enum.
- `just lint` is clean; all 722 workspace tests pass.

120	/// Shared, read-only context passed to all resolution functions.
121	/// Arc'd so it can be cheaply shared across rayon threads.
122	pub struct ResolutionContext {
123	    pub global: Arc<GlobalSourceData>,
124	    pub import_map: Arc<ImportResolutionMap>,
125	    /// Fast `(file, name)` index over `global.interfaces`/`type_aliases` and
126	    /// their declared generic type parameters — see `named_type_index.rs`'s
127	    /// module doc for why this exists alongside (not instead of) those flat
128	    /// maps.
129	    pub(crate) named_types: Arc<crate::named_type_index::NamedTypeIndex>,
130	    pub oxc_resolver: Arc<Resolver>,
131	    /// Module resolutions by `(directory, specifier)`. Resolution only reads the file system, which a run treats as
132	    /// fixed, and every component importing from the same directory asks again; a watch revision builds a fresh
133	    /// context, so nothing outlives one revision.
134	    pub(crate) module_resolutions:
135	        dashmap::DashMap<(Box<str>, Box<str>), import::ModuleResolution, rustc_hash::FxBuildHasher>,
136	    pub extra_builtins: FxHashSet<CompactString>,
137	    /// Bare name → full scoped key ("file:name") index over `global.enums`,
138	    /// built once per resolution pass so `resolve_typeof` and
139	    /// `resolve_cva_variant_props` (VariantProps<typeof X>) can do an O(1)
140	    /// lookup instead of a linear scan with a `format!()` allocation per
141	    /// candidate on every reference. Ambiguous bare names (same name in two
142	    /// files) resolve to whichever key `global.enums` yields first during
143	    /// this build pass — the same tie-break the old linear scan produced,
144	    /// since both iterate the same underlying map.
145	    pub enum_bare_index: FxHashMap<CompactString, CompactString>,
146	    /// Same as `enum_bare_index`, but over `global.const_arrays` — for
147	    /// `(typeof X)[number]` on a flat `const X = [...] as const` array.
148	    pub const_array_bare_index: FxHashMap<CompactString, CompactString>,
149	    /// How much of an inherited HTML element's attributes to expose.
150	    pub html_attributes: crate::pipeline::HtmlAttributeMode,
151	    /// Paths to TypeScript's own `lib.es5.d.ts`/`lib.dom.d.ts`, if resolvable
152	    /// from this project (empty otherwise — see `resolve_ts_lib_paths`).
153	    /// Checked as a last-resort fallback when a bare, never-imported name
154	    /// (a real native/DOM global like `Date`) doesn't resolve via the normal
155	    /// same-file lookup — see `import::lookup_interface`/`lookup_type_alias`.
156	    pub ambient_global_files: Vec<Utf8PathBuf>,
157	}
158	
159	impl ResolutionContext {
160	    #[cfg(test)]
161	    pub fn new(global: Arc<GlobalSourceData>, options: &PipelineOptions) -> Self {
162	        let named_types = Arc::new(crate::named_type_index::NamedTypeIndex::build(&global));
163	        Self::build(global, options, compute_ambient_global_files(options), named_types)
164	    }
165	
166	    /// A context over an index and ambient file list the caller already holds. A watch revision patches its
167	    /// `NamedTypeIndex` per edited file; rebuilding it from the whole merged `global` on every save measurably
168	    /// regressed watch latency (see `NamedTypeIndex::remove_file`).
169	    pub fn new_with_cached_ambient_global_files(
170	        global: Arc<GlobalSourceData>,
171	        options: &PipelineOptions,
172	        ambient_global_files: Vec<Utf8PathBuf>,
173	        named_types: Arc<crate::named_type_index::NamedTypeIndex>,
174	    ) -> Self {
175	        Self::build(global, options, ambient_global_files, named_types)
176	    }
177	
178	    fn build(
179	        global: Arc<GlobalSourceData>,
180	        options: &PipelineOptions,
181	        ambient_global_files: Vec<Utf8PathBuf>,
182	        named_types: Arc<crate::named_type_index::NamedTypeIndex>,
183	    ) -> Self {
184	        let alias: Vec<(String, Vec<AliasValue>)> = react::read_tsconfig_paths(options.tsconfig_path.as_deref());
185	
186	        let resolve_options = ResolveOptions {
187	            condition_names: vec!["types".into(), "import".into(), "require".into(), "default".into()],
188	            main_fields: vec!["types".into(), "typings".into(), "module".into(), "main".into()],
189	            extensions: vec![".ts".into(), ".tsx".into(), ".d.ts".into(), ".js".into()],
190	            alias,
191	            ..ResolveOptions::default()
192	        };
193	
194	        let mut enum_bare_index: FxHashMap<CompactString, CompactString> = FxHashMap::default();
195	        // Sorted so a bare name shared by several files binds to the same one regardless of hash order.
196	        let mut enum_keys: Vec<&String> = global.enums.keys().collect();
197	        enum_keys.sort();
198	        for key in enum_keys {
199	            let bare = key.rsplit_once(':').map(|(_, name)| name).unwrap_or(key.as_str());
200	            enum_bare_index.entry(CompactString::from(bare)).or_insert_with(|| CompactString::from(key.as_str()));
201	        }
202	
203	        let mut const_array_bare_index: FxHashMap<CompactString, CompactString> = FxHashMap::default();
204	        let mut const_array_keys: Vec<&String> = global.const_arrays.keys().collect();
205	        const_array_keys.sort();
206	        for key in const_array_keys {
207	            let bare = key.rsplit_once(':').map(|(_, name)| name).unwrap_or(key.as_str());
208	            const_array_bare_index
209	                .entry(CompactString::from(bare))
210	                .or_insert_with(|| CompactString::from(key.as_str()));
211	        }
212	
213	        Self {
214	            import_map: Arc::new(ImportResolutionMap::build(&global)),
215	            named_types,
216	            global,
217	            oxc_resolver: Arc::new(Resolver::new(resolve_options)),
218	            extra_builtins: options.extra_builtins.clone(),
219	            enum_bare_index,
220	            const_array_bare_index,
221	            html_attributes: options.html_attributes,
222	            ambient_global_files,
223	            module_resolutions: Default::default(),
224	        }
225	    }
226	}
227

229	/// options' first source directory, if resolvable — see `resolve_ts_lib_paths`.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.
