allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names

- **`tsconfigPath` is read the way TypeScript reads it:** block and line comments, `extends`, `baseUrl` and `paths` wildcards. Before, a hand-written reader understood only line comments and ignored `extends`. - **A parse-cache file over 256 MB is reported and ignored** rather than read into memory.

input.content:
Fixes finding 5 of the October 21 review, plus the cache resource bound from finding 6. Targets `main`, independent of #91 and #92.

## Problem

- **tsconfig.** `read_tsconfig_paths` stripped only `//` comments, never followed `extends`, and returned no aliases with no diagnostic on any read or parse failure. Because block comments or `extends` are common in tsconfigs, every aliased import then failed one by one, with nothing pointing at the config.
- **React Aria `RenderProps<T>`.** It mapped to a plain-string `className` and plain `style`. It dropped the function form both accept and dropped `children` entirely, with no opacity diagnostic.
- **DTS cache.** The loader read and decoded the whole cache file before any bound was applied.

## Change

- **tsconfig.** `ResolveOptions.tsconfig` hands the config to `oxc_resolver`, which reads comments, `extends`, `baseUrl` and `paths` wildcards as TypeScript does. The hand-written reader and comment stripper are deleted. `Resolver::resolve_tsconfig` validates the file once, and a failure becomes one run-wide warning naming the file.
- **`RenderProps<T>`.** `className`, `style` and `children` are each `value | (values: T) => …`. The function form is an `eventHandler` with event type `T`.
- **Cache size bound.** The loader checks the file's size before reading it; files over 256 MB are reported and ignored. For scale, a measured cache holding all of TypeScript's lib files is 2.9 MB.

## Verification

- **New tests:**
  - `tsconfig_paths_resolve_through_block_comments_and_extends` resolves an `@ui/*` alias through a config with block comments, and through one that gets `paths` via `extends`. The old reader failed both.
  - `an_unusable_tsconfig_is_reported_once`
  - `a_cache_file_over_the_size_limit_is_reported_without_being_read` (uses a sparse file)
- **Corpora:** no output change on any of the five, compared to current `main`. Their components don't reach the `RenderProps` shortcut, and none sets a tsconfig.
- `just lint` is clean; all 727 workspace tests pass.

"""Compare wall time of two binaries on the corpora. Usage: timing.py A B [projects...]"""
import json, subprocess, sys, tempfile

A, B = sys.argv[1:3]
projects = sys.argv[3:] or ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
print('| Project | A ms | B ms |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: |')
for p in projects:
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json') as out:
        subprocess.run(['hyperfine', '-w', '2', '-r', '10', '-N', '--style', 'none', '--export-json', out.name,
                        f'{A} extract --src {IN}/{p} --json', f'{B} extract --src {IN}/{p} --json'],
                       capture_output=True, check=True)
        res = json.load(open(out.name))['results']

        def mean(r):
            return r['summary']['time_wall_clock']['mean'] * 1000 if 'summary' in r else r['mean'] * 1000
        print(f'| {p} | {mean(res[0]):.0f} | {mean(res[1]):.0f} |')

print(f"| Project | recall(own) | recall(any) | props(own) | Caliper comps | extras |")
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
for proj in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    out = subprocess.run([BIN, 'extract', '--src', f'{IN}/{proj}', '--json'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    cal = json.loads(out)['components']
    by_file = {}
    for c in cal.values():
        by_file.setdefault(c['filePath'], []).append((norm(c['displayName']), set(c['props'])))
    rdt = [c for c in json.load(open(f'{RES}/{proj}.rdt.dump.json')) if plausible(c['name'])]
    rdt_names = {(c['file'], norm(c['name'])) for c in rdt}
    own_tot = own_hit = any_tot = any_hit = ptot = phit = 0
    for c in rdt:
        mine = {p for p, v in c['props'].items() if f'bench-inputs/{proj}/' in v['parent'] and '/node_modules/' not in v['parent']}
        cands = by_file.get(c['file'], [])
        named = [props for nm, props in cands if nm == norm(c['name'])]
        if c['props']:
            any_tot += 1
            any_hit += bool(named)
        if mine:
            own_tot += 1
            match = named[0] if named else next((p for nm, p in cands if len(mine & p) >= max(1, len(mine) // 2)), None)
            if match is not None:
                own_hit += 1
                ptot += len(mine)
                phit += len(mine & match)
    extras = sum(1 for c in cal.values() if (c['filePath'], norm(c['displayName'])) not in rdt_names)
    pct = lambda a, b: f'{100 * a / max(b, 1):.0f}%'
    print(f'| {proj} | {pct(own_hit, own_tot)} | {pct(any_hit, any_tot)} ({any_hit}/{any_tot}) | {pct(phit, ptot)} | {len(cal)} | {extras} |')

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

"""Wall time: stored RDT and react-docgen hyperfine results vs a Caliper binary measured now. Usage: vs_rdt.py BIN"""
import json, subprocess, sys, tempfile

BIN = sys.argv[1]
RES = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results'
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'


def mean_ms(path):
    try:
        r = json.load(open(path))['results'][0]
        return r['mean'] * 1000, r.get('max_rss') or r.get('memory_usage_byte', [None])[0] if isinstance(r.get('memory_usage_byte'), list) else None
    except (OSError, KeyError, IndexError):
        return None, None


print('| Corpus | RDT ms | react-docgen ms | Caliper ms (now) | Caliper vs RDT |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
for p in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    rdt, _ = mean_ms(f'{RES}/{p}.rdt.time.json')
    rdg, _ = mean_ms(f'{RES}/{p}.rdg.time.json')
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json') as out:
        subprocess.run(['hyperfine', '-w', '2', '-r', '10', '-N', '--style', 'none', '--export-json', out.name,
                        f'{BIN} extract --src {IN}/{p} --json'], capture_output=True, check=True)
        cal = json.load(open(out.name))['results'][0]['mean'] * 1000
    fmt = lambda v: f'{v:,.0f}' if v else 'n/a'
    ratio = f'{rdt / cal:.0f}x' if rdt else 'n/a'
    print(f'| {p} | {fmt(rdt)} | {fmt(rdg)} | {cal:.0f} | {ratio} |')

# Status

**Updated:** 2026-09-28

Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, cross-package `.d.ts` resolution, watch mode, plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, LSP server scaffold, and bounded atomic DTS caching are all fully implemented and verified.

## Numbers

- 545 Rust tests (77 cli + 443 core unit + 8 snapshot + 1 core compile-fail + 16 napi binding), 36 vitest (33 unit, mocked NAPI + 3 integration against the real native binding — `packages/vite-plugin/tests/integration/`, gated on a locally-built `.node` binary, auto-skips otherwise) — all green
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `unsafe_code = "deny"` enforced workspace-wide
- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)

## Features and improvements

- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap.
- **LSP server scaffold** (`caliper-docgen lsp`) — bounded framing plus initialize/shutdown/exit lifecycle. It currently advertises `hoverProvider: false` and does not serve component prop hovers yet.
- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all three crates (`core`, `cli`, `binding`) — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).

## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker

See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types, mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs.

An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is designed (ADR 0006) but not implemented. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,265/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@next`. Lifecycle (crash/restart/timeout handling for the `tsc --api` process) hasn't started; see `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table.

## Where to look next

- **Edge cases, failure modes, and gaps not yet fixed** → `edge-cases.md` — comprehensive audit of crash/hang risks, silent data loss, and silent correctness bugs across every subsystem, prioritized. Update it as findings get fixed or new ones turn up.
- **Why those gaps happened, and the plan to fix them** → `root-cause-analysis.md` — the edge-case findings collapsed into 11 mechanism-level root causes with concrete fix proposals, plus a Phase 1 task breakdown.
- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`).
- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`
- **Old build-out specs, resolved questions, point-in-time analyses** → `docs/archive/` — historical, not current, kept for reference

### Phase 4: semantic backend (ADR 0006 follow-up)

| Id | Item | Size | Needs | Exit criterion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1 | Re-probe TypeScript 7.1.0-beta: package exports (`typescript/unstable` vs `./sync ./async ./proto ./ast/*`), checker methods, overloads, static sub-components, barrels; update `type-checker-integration.md` | S | none | Entry points and version pin recorded |
| 4.2 | ADR 0007: backend may discover components; always compiled, enabled at runtime (no cargo feature); structural stays default and fallback; trigger policy. Decide additive `schemaVersion` | S | 4.1 | Accepted ADR |
| 4.3 | Wire `tsc-client` into core (owned result type and merge in core, process in the backend crate) | L | 4.2, 2.1 | Failure leaves the structural result plus a diagnostic |
| 4.4 | Discovery by call-signature rule (RDT's algorithm), merge into structural output; covers opaque factories (about 60 declarations) | L | 4.3 | Accuracy gate extended to checker-discovered components |
| 4.5 | Determinism (clean vs incremental) and cost gates with the Rust client | M | 4.4 | Measured on the five corpora with dependencies installed |

### Phase 5: performance and dependencies

| Id | Item | Size | Needs | Exit criterion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1 | Profile allocations and thread scaling (Mantine: 44ms on 18 threads vs 68ms on one) before touching clone sites | S | none | Written profile with the top five sites |
| 5.2 | Parallel discovery; resolve the TypeScript lib once per run; serialize RDT output from typed structs instead of a `json!` tree; avoid per-lookup alias clones | M | 5.1 | Measured gain on the five corpora |
| 5.3 | Replace `watchexec` with `notify` and a debouncer; drop tokio from the CLI; trim tokio and tracing features | M | none | Pty watch test passes; crate count and build time recorded |
| 5.4 | Replace `dashmap` with `Mutex<FxHashMap>` where not on a hot path; benchmark the cache first | S | none | No regression |
| 5.5 | Release profile experiment (`lto = true`, `strip = true`); `mimalloc` for the CLI | S | none | Size and speed recorded; unwinding kept |
| 5.6 | JSON config fast path alongside node and `tsx`; append to `NODE_OPTIONS` instead of overwriting | M | none | Spawn skipped when a JSON config is present |

### Track R: release and product (parallel)

| Id | Item |
| --- | --- |
| R1 | Yank `oxc-react-docgen-core` 0.2.0 from your account |
| R2 | Update orin-dx.com/tools/caliper (published packages, `caliper-docgen` command names, remove "built, unpublished") |
| R3 | Diff the hand-written `release.yml` against what callisto 0.11 generates (napi roster-only builds, recovery fixes) |
| R4 | Docs guides: CLI reference, `docgen.config.ts`, output format and `PropType` kinds, Vite plugin options, Node API |
| R5 | File upstream callisto issues: verification window shorter than npm's new-package lag; no tag-push credential input |
| R6 | Release hygiene: do not merge workflow-changing PRs while a release is in flight |

## Dependency graph

```
0.1 -> 0.2 -> 2.3 -> 3.4
0.5 -> 1.5 -> 2.1 -> 2.4 -> 3.3 -> 3.4 -> 3.5
0.6 -> 1.1, 3.2
2.2 -> 3.1 -> 3.2, 3.4
2.6 -> 3.4
1.6 + 3.4 -> 3.6
4.1 -> 4.2 -> 4.3 -> 4.4 -> 4.5     (starts after 2.1)
5.x and Track R are independent
```

## Release shape

| Release | Contents | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.2.2 | Metadata, license, README rewrite (PR #45 merged; release PR #46 open) | Merging #46 publishes; the first release where package names already exist, so it tests the single-run publish |
| 0.2.3 | Phase 0 and Phase 1 | No user-visible behavior beyond fixed defects; cache version bump |
| 0.3.0 | Phase 2 and Phase 3 (3.1 to 3.4) | New components appear in output: a behavior change, call it out in the changeset. Tier 2 stays off |
| 0.4.0 | Phase 4 | Opt-in semantic backend |
| as ready | Phase 5 items | Each with measured numbers |

## Quality gates

| Gate | Threshold (proposed) |
| --- | --- |
| Component recall vs RDT, plausible components, source-only mirrors | Mantine at least 85%, Chakra at least 80%; shadcn, spectrum, antd not lower than 98%, 98%, 88% |
| Prop recall on found components | Mantine and Chakra at least 80% (inferred target, not yet measured) |
| Precision | At least 95% on a hand-labeled sample of about 50 new emissions per project, reported per false-positive family |
| With dependencies installed | Mantine and Chakra re-run with `node_modules` (dependencies installed with scripts disabled) |
| Time and memory | No project more than 15ms or 20% slower than the current figure; peak RSS tracked |
| Determinism | Reversed and repeated input order give byte-identical output; clean and incremental agree |
| Parity | `extract()`, `update_file`, `create_session` agree on components, props and diagnostics, including callee-only edits |
| Hygiene | Zero production `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`; no `use crate::pipeline` in the resolver; no accepted-but-unread options |

## Decisions

Recommended defaults, assumed until confirmed.

| Id | Decision | Recommended default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Does tier 2 (type-shape guess) emit by default? | No. Opt-in flag; tier 1 and `@component` emit by default |
| D2 | Declarative wrapper list in `docgen.config.ts`? | No for now; `@component` is enough. Revisit after Phase 3 data |
| D3 | May the semantic backend discover components? Wire `tsc-client`? | Yes (ADR 0007), runtime opt-in, wired in Phase 4, after Phase 3 shows what structural leaves |
| D4 | Provenance in output? | Info diagnostic with position; add an additive `schemaVersion` field to `ExtractionOutput` |
| D5 | Thresholds | As in Quality gates |
| D6 | Parity target | Plausible components (PascalCase, not hooks), not every RDT entry |
| D7 | Plain `.ts` files and underscore-leading names | Include underscore-leading names (`_3D`); keep `.ts` out |
| N1 | Adopt callisto's "no cargo features in shipped crates" rule | Yes; amend ADR 0006's "feature-gated" wording in ADR 0007 |
| N2 | Adopt `docs/specs/` and `docs/projects/` | Yes |
| N3 | Forbid spec or criterion IDs in code | Yes; clean up the 117 existing citations in 0.7 |

## Main risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Tier 2 matches the `createContext` family (427 sites in the corpora) | Off by default; structural discriminators; per-family precision; one negative fixture per family |
| Detection lands before props resolve and yields empty components | Order: 2.1, 2.4, 3.3 before 3.4; an unresolved props type emits an Info diagnostic and no entry |
| Phase 3 too large to attribute regressions | Split as above; each item has its own exit criterion |
| Watch staleness for cross-file callee resolution | 3.6, with callee-only parity tests |
| Positional cache decode (new field or variant) | Append last, bump version in the same commit, golden-bytes test (0.5) |
| New components change user output | Info diagnostics only; hand-review snapshot diffs; changeset note; 0.3.0 |
| Recall is measured against an oracle that over- and under-reports | Hand-labeled precision sample; dependency-installed run; per-shape reporting |
| TypeScript 7.1 API churn | 4.1 re-probe first; ADR kept narrow; version check degrades to structural with a diagnostic |

## Out of scope

`lazy` and `dynamic` components (props live in the target module), plugin registration from the CLI, replacing `compact_str` or the cache format (the audit found no case for it), Vue and Svelte, and a Storybook integration.

The default is `'react-docgen'` when `@storybook/react` is installed. https://storybook.js.org/docs/api/main-config/main-config-typescript (v10.6). react-docgen has been the default since Storybook 8: https://storybook.js.org/blog/storybook-8/
  - **New extractor.** Storybook 10.4 (2026-05-18) added `react-component-meta` (RCM), built on Volar and the TypeScript Language Service, behind `features.experimentalReactComponentMeta`. Their figures for Mantine: 154/154 components found, 200ms, against 8698ms for RDT. https://storybook.js.org/blog/storybook-10-4/ , https://medium.com/storybookjs/storybook-10-4-89859d1740da
  - **Docgen server.** `experimentalDocgenServer` runs extraction on the dev server from 10.5 onward. RFC: https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/discussions/35333 , tracking issue: https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/34824
  - **Storybook 11.** 11.0.0-alpha.5 says "Stabilize docgenServer and enable it wherever a provider exists". In the 11.0.0-alpha.7 typings, `features.docgenServer` is on by default when a preset ships a provider. The React worker hardcodes `docgenEngine: "react-component-meta"`. Draft PR #36896 makes react-docgen an optional peer and says the docgen server is "on by default when `typescript` resolves". https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/36896
  - **Extension point (confirmed in the 10.6.3 and 11-alpha `.d.ts` files).**
    - Third parties register through the `experimental_docgenProvider` preset with `{moduleSpecifier, options}`.
    - That module exports `createDocgenProvider(opts) => (next) => async ({entry}) => DocgenPayload`.
    - Later registrants wrap earlier ones, so a provider can fall back to RCM.
    - The payload is `{id, name, path, description?, summary?, jsDocTags: Record<string,string[]>, argTypes?: StrictArgTypes, subcomponents?, error?}`.
    - `argTypes` must already be converted to Storybook's argTypes format.

**A time gate that scales with codebase size.** Gating on absolute milliseconds penalizes finding more components, which is what happened when recall rose: Mantine went from 44 to 85 ms while emitting 8× the components. I'll express the gate as throughput (time per thousand lines and per emitted component) and compute today's baseline.

2. **Props:** compare each matched component's props with RDT, covering extra props, wrong `required` flags and type disagreements.
3. **Who's right:** hand-check a sample of the disagreements, since RDT itself is an imperfect oracle.

Starting with what the RDT oracle data contains.

"""Prop-level agreement with react-docgen-typescript on components both report.

For each corpus: Caliper's `--format rdt` output vs RDT's dump, joined on (file, normalized name). Counts props only
Caliper reports (possible false props), props only RDT reports, `required` disagreements and type-string
disagreements, and writes examples of each to prop_gaps.json. Usage: prop_precision.py BIN
"""
import collections, json, os, re, subprocess, sys

BIN = sys.argv[1]
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
RES = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results'
D = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/precision'


def norm(n):
    n = re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', n).split('/')[-1].split('.')[-1]
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', n.lower())


def canon_type(t):
    # Order-insensitive unions, collapsed whitespace, no quotes style differences.
    t = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', (t or '').replace("'", '"')).strip()
    if ' | ' in t and '(' not in t and '<' not in t and '{' not in t:
        t = ' | '.join(sorted(p.strip() for p in t.split('|')))
    return t


examples = collections.defaultdict(list)
print('| Corpus | Matched comps | Props both | Only Caliper | Only RDT | required differs | type differs |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
for corpus in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    out = f'{D}/{corpus}.caliper.rdt.json'
    subprocess.run([BIN, 'extract', '--src', f'{IN}/{corpus}', '--format', 'rdt', '--out', out], capture_output=True)
    cal = json.load(open(out))
    cal = cal if isinstance(cal, list) else list(cal.values())
    rdt = json.load(open(f'{RES}/{corpus}.rdt.dump.json'))
    by_key = {(c['filePath'], norm(c['displayName'])): c for c in cal}
    matched = both = only_cal = only_rdt = req = typ = 0
    for r in rdt:
        c = by_key.get((r['file'], norm(r['name'])))
        if not c:
            continue
        matched += 1
        cp, rp = c.get('props', {}), r['props']
        for name in cp.keys() - rp.keys():
            only_cal += 1
            examples[(corpus, 'only_caliper')].append((r['name'], name, cp[name].get('type', {}).get('name')))
        only_rdt += len(rp.keys() - cp.keys())
        for name in cp.keys() & rp.keys():
            both += 1
            if bool(cp[name].get('required')) != bool(rp[name]['required']):
                req += 1
                examples[(corpus, 'required')].append((r['name'], name, cp[name].get('required'), rp[name]['required']))
            ct, rt = canon_type(cp[name].get('type', {}).get('name')), canon_type(rp[name]['type'])
            if ct != rt:
                typ += 1
                examples[(corpus, 'type')].append((r['name'], name, ct[:120], rt[:120]))
    print(f'| {corpus} | {matched} | {both} | {only_cal} | {only_rdt} | {req} ({100 * req / max(both, 1):.1f}%) | '
          f'{typ} ({100 * typ / max(both, 1):.0f}%) |')
json.dump({f'{c}:{k}': v[:400] for (c, k), v in examples.items()}, open(f'{D}/prop_gaps.json', 'w'), indent=1)

content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

"""Throughput per corpus: wall time per 1,000 source lines, per file and per emitted component. Usage: size_gate.py BIN"""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile

BIN = sys.argv[1]
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
print('| Corpus | Files | Lines | Components | Props | ms | ms per 1k lines | µs per file | µs per component |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
for p in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    files = lines = 0
    for root, _, names in os.walk(f'{IN}/{p}'):
        for n in names:
            if n.endswith(('.ts', '.tsx')) and 'node_modules' not in root:
                files += 1
                with open(os.path.join(root, n), encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                    lines += sum(1 for _ in f)
    d = json.loads(subprocess.run([BIN, 'extract', '--src', f'{IN}/{p}', '--json'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
    comps = len(d['components'])
    props = sum(len(c['props']) for c in d['components'].values())
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json') as out:
        subprocess.run(['hyperfine', '-w', '2', '-r', '10', '-N', '--style', 'none', '--export-json', out.name,
                        f'{BIN} extract --src {IN}/{p} --json'], capture_output=True, check=True)

# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# caliper-docgen

10-100x faster than react-docgen-typescript. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Commands

```bash
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Decisions

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.

# crates/core

Pure extraction logic — no terminal, no NAPI, no async. Everything here must be `Send + Sync` for rayon.

## Module layout

```
types/          — shared data types (the contract between phases)
extractor/      — OXC AST visitor → SourceData
resolver/       — SourceData + GlobalSourceData → ComponentEntry
pipeline/       — orchestration: discover → parse → merge → resolve
cache.rs        — DTS parse cache (mtime+size invalidation, msgpack)
import_map.rs   — import resolution map
known.rs        — library-specific type shortcuts (SxProps, VariantProps…)
react_types.rs  — React builtin recognition + notable HTML attrs
```

## Types discipline

When adding a public type, run through the checklist in the `rust-types` skill. Canonical reference: `src/types/diagnostic.rs`.

## Resolver

`resolve_component()` is called in parallel via rayon. All inputs must be owned or `Arc`-wrapped — no borrowed data crosses thread boundaries. `ResolveState` accumulates diagnostics and visited-type tracking for a single resolution call; it is not shared.

## Panic containment

Anything reachable from a rayon `.map()` or a `DocgenPlugin` impl must go through `panic_guard::contain_panic` — see `pipeline/mod.rs` and `plugin.rs` for the call sites, and `docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md` for why.

## Snapshot tests

Seven fixtures in `crates/core/tests/snapshots/`. If a change affects output, regenerate with `/snapshot` before committing.

# crates/cli

Thin command layer — no extraction logic. Each command parses args and delegates to `caliper-docgen-core::pipeline`.

## Layout

```
main.rs              — Cli struct, Command enum, *Args structs, main(), init_tracing()
commands/            — one file per subcommand (extract, watch, inspect, check, completions)
config.rs            — docgen.config.ts loading, maps to PipelineOptions
output.rs            — comfy-table formatting helpers
```

## Rules

Command payloads go to stdout with `println!`; diagnostics, progress and everything on stderr go through `output.rs` or the tracing subscriber — never `eprintln!`. Error display uses `miette`. Progress uses `indicatif`.

Config loading (`config.rs`) runs the user's `docgen.config.ts` via node+tsx. The config file path is passed via env var, not embedded in a shell string — command injection risk otherwise.

"""Throughput per corpus: wall time per 1,000 source lines, per file and per emitted component. Usage: size_gate.py BIN"""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile

BIN = sys.argv[1]
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
print('| Corpus | Files | Lines | Components | Props | ms | ms per 1k lines | µs per file | µs per component |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
for p in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    files = lines = 0
    for root, _, names in os.walk(f'{IN}/{p}'):
        for n in names:
            if n.endswith(('.ts', '.tsx')) and 'node_modules' not in root:
                files += 1
                with open(os.path.join(root, n), encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
                    lines += sum(1 for _ in f)
    d = json.loads(subprocess.run([BIN, 'extract', '--src', f'{IN}/{p}', '--json'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
    comps = len(d['components'])
    props = sum(len(c['props']) for c in d['components'].values())
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json') as out:
        subprocess.run(['hyperfine', '-w', '2', '-r', '10', '-N', '--style', 'none', '--export-json', out.name,
                        f'{BIN} extract --src {IN}/{p} --json'], capture_output=True, check=True)
        ms = json.load(open(out.name))['results'][0]['summary']['time_wall_clock']['mean'] * 1000
    print(f'| {p} | {files:,} | {lines:,} | {comps:,} | {props:,} | {ms:.0f} | {1000 * ms / lines:.2f} | '
          f'{1000 * ms / files:.0f} | {1000 * ms / max(comps, 1):.0f} |')

"""Seeded sample of props only Caliper reports, with the component file and the declaring file, for labelling."""
import json, random, re, subprocess

BIN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/caliper-docgen-next'
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
RES = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results'
D = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/precision'
PER = {'mantine': 13, 'chakra': 9, 'antd': 13, 'shadcn': 12, 'spectrum': 13}
rng = random.Random(20261021)


def norm(n):
    n = re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', n).split('/')[-1].split('.')[-1]
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', n.lower())


items = []
for corpus, k in PER.items():
    canonical = json.loads(subprocess.run([BIN, 'extract', '--src', f'{IN}/{corpus}', '--json'], capture_output=True,
                                          text=True).stdout)['components']
    by_key = {(c['filePath'], norm(c['displayName'])): c for c in canonical.values()}
    pool = []
    for r in json.load(open(f'{RES}/{corpus}.rdt.dump.json')):
        c = by_key.get((r['file'], norm(r['name'])))
        if not c:
            continue
        for name in sorted(c['props'].keys() - r['props'].keys()):
            p = c['props'][name]
            pool.append({'corpus': corpus, 'component': c['displayName'], 'component_file': c['filePath'], 'prop': name,
                         'declared_in': (p.get('parent') or {}).get('fileName'),
                         'declared_by': (p.get('parent') or {}).get('name'),
                         'rdt_prop_count': len(r['props'])})
    items += rng.sample(pool, min(k, len(pool)))
for i, it in enumerate(items):
    it['id'] = i
for b in range(2):
    json.dump(items[b::2], open(f'{D}/onlycal{b}.json', 'w'), indent=1)
json.dump(items, open(f'{D}/onlycal_sample.json', 'w'), indent=1)
print(len(items), 'sampled')

"""Prop-level agreement with react-docgen-typescript on components both report.

For each corpus: Caliper's `--format rdt` output vs RDT's dump, joined on (file, normalized name). Counts props only
Caliper reports (possible false props), props only RDT reports, `required` disagreements and type-string
disagreements, and writes examples of each to prop_gaps.json. Usage: prop_precision.py BIN
"""
import collections, json, os, re, subprocess, sys

BIN = sys.argv[1]
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'
RES = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results'
D = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/review/precision'


def norm(n):
    n = re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', n).split('/')[-1].split('.')[-1]
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', n.lower())


def canon_type(t):
    # Order-insensitive unions, collapsed whitespace, no quotes style differences.
    t = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', (t or '').replace("'", '"')).strip()
    if ' | ' in t and '(' not in t and '<' not in t and '{' not in t:
        t = ' | '.join(sorted(p.strip() for p in t.split('|')))
    return t


examples = collections.defaultdict(list)
print('| Corpus | Matched comps | Props both | Only Caliper | Only RDT | required differs | type differs |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
for corpus in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    out = f'{D}/{corpus}.caliper.rdt.json'
    subprocess.run([BIN, 'extract', '--src', f'{IN}/{corpus}', '--format', 'rdt', '--out', out], capture_output=True)
    cal = json.load(open(out))
    # `--format rdt` has no filePath (RDT's own ComponentDoc does); take it from the canonical output's same keys.
    canonical = json.loads(subprocess.run([BIN, 'extract', '--src', f'{IN}/{corpus}', '--json'], capture_output=True,
                                          text=True).stdout)['components']
    rdt = json.load(open(f'{RES}/{corpus}.rdt.dump.json'))
    by_key = {(canonical[k]['filePath'], norm(c['displayName'])): c for k, c in cal.items() if k in canonical}
    matched = both = only_cal = only_rdt = req = typ = 0
    for r in rdt:
        c = by_key.get((r['file'], norm(r['name'])))
        if not c:
            continue
        matched += 1
        cp, rp = c.get('props', {}), r['props']
        for name in cp.keys() - rp.keys():
            only_cal += 1
            examples[(corpus, 'only_caliper')].append((r['name'], name, cp[name].get('type', {}).get('name')))
        only_rdt += len(rp.keys() - cp.keys())
        for name in cp.keys() & rp.keys():
            both += 1
            if bool(cp[name].get('required')) != bool(rp[name]['required']):
                req += 1
                examples[(corpus, 'required')].append((r['name'], name, cp[name].get('required'), rp[name]['required']))
            ct, rt = canon_type(cp[name].get('type', {}).get('name')), canon_type(rp[name]['type'])
            if ct != rt:
                typ += 1
                examples[(corpus, 'type')].append((r['name'], name, ct[:120], rt[:120]))
    print(f'| {corpus} | {matched} | {both} | {only_cal} | {only_rdt} | {req} ({100 * req / max(both, 1):.1f}%) | '
          f'{typ} ({100 * typ / max(both, 1):.0f}%) |')
json.dump({f'{c}:{k}': v[:400] for (c, k), v in examples.items()}, open(f'{D}/prop_gaps.json', 'w'), indent=1)

# Vanguard Research Skill

<overview>
Vanguard builds a documented evidence base before committing to a solution direction. It separates what is known from what is assumed, surfaces contradictions, and delivers a recommendation a spec writer can act on directly.

One skill, one pipeline — not a menu of separately-invokable modes. `recon` maps sources (internal specs/docs/code, dependency manifests, external references), `reader` reads only what the map points at, `synthesizer` resolves the findings into one report, `risk-assessor` reviews the resulting approach. The pipeline narrows itself to what's asked: a question answerable from internal sources alone gets `scope: internal` from recon and never touches external search; a request for risk review of an already-decided approach can hand `risk-assessor` that approach directly.
</overview>

---

<language_agnostic_note>
Recon detects the workspace language from manifest files present (Cargo.toml → Rust, package.json → Node/TypeScript, pyproject.toml → Python, etc.), then loads the appropriate shared/references search heuristics for that ecosystem. The skill is not language-specific.
</language_agnostic_note>

---

<subagent_dispatch_matrix>

| Agent | Role | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **recon** | Source mapper | haiku / low | Start every research task here. Maps internal sources, external keywords, and existing implementations. |
| **reader** | Evidence extractor | sonnet / medium | Given the source map, reads each source and extracts findings with citations and confidence levels. |
| **synthesizer** | Recommendation producer | sonnet / medium | Given findings, synthesizes a research-report@1 with a falsifiable recommendation and confidence level. |
| **risk-assessor** | Risk prioritizer | sonnet / medium | Given a proposed approach or research-report@1, identifies and prioritizes technical risks with mitigations. |

</subagent_dispatch_matrix>

---

<output>
All research concludes in a `research-report@1` (schema: `shared/schemas/research-report@1.json`). The report distinguishes:
- **confirmed** — read directly from source
- **likely** — strong inference from evidence
- **assumed** — unverified, flagged explicitly

The recommendation is falsifiable: a spec or plan written from it will not be surprised by implementation reality.
</output>


ARGUMENTS: How should caliper-docgen detect and resolve React components declared through wrapper calls (e.g. Mantine factory/polymorphicFactory/genericFactory<XFactory>(...), Chakra v3 withContext<El, Props>/withRootProvider<Props>(...), tableElement<T>, createEdgeComponent, createIconLoader("x")), without hardcoding library names, while preserving the architecture and semantic models (docs/architecture/, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/adr/, crates/core extractor/resolver/types, ADR 0006 semantic backend)? Evidence so far: a 5-project benchmark (mantine, chakra-ui, ant-design, shadcn-ui, react-spectrum) in /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results (accuracy.md, rdt.dump.json, caliper.dump.json) with scripts in /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench (recall2.py, patterns.py, samples.py) and mirrored inputs in /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs. Component recall vs react-docgen-typescript on source-only mirrors: shadcn 98%, spectrum 98%, antd 88%, mantine 29%, chakra 9%; ~72% of misses are the shape `const PascalName = wrapperCall<TypeArgs>(fn)` with props carried as a type argument or as a `props` member of a payload type argument. Open items: 29 plain arrow-function misses, 67 name mismatches (displayName property, default exports), calls with no type argument (createIconLoader, lazy) which need return-type resolution (ADR 0006 semantic backend), Mantine's ElementProps<'input', ...> generic helper not resolving, and why Chakra forwardRef components lose props. Questions to answer: (1) what are all the distinct declaration shapes and where does the props type come from in each; (2) how does the current extractor (crates/core/src/extractor/component.rs, visit.rs, mod.rs) and resolver decide what is a component and resolve props, and where would a shape-based detector fit without breaking the layering and 'no reverse dependency' rules; (3) how should the semantic types (SourceData, ComponentMapping, PropType, Diagnostic) represent an inferred component and its provenance; (4) how does this interact with ADR 0006's semantic backend and what is each one's job; (5) how do RDT, react-docgen, Storybook docgen and the TypeScript checker decide what a component is, for prior art; (6) false-positive risks and the guard design; (7) test and CI strategy for recall by shape. Do not change any code; produce a research report.

definition.name: SendFeedback
definition.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
