# Architecture Decision Records

Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [4. Defer full type-checker integration](0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md) — superseded by 0006.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.

- [7. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default](0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) — do not feature-gate the backend crate, run it by default, or let it replace a structural entry on a clash.
- [8. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs](0008-parse-cache-keyed-by-build.md) — do not load cache entries without checking the payload's header against the running build.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |

**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.

**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.

**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.

**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.

**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.

## What good looks like

Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

# 0009. Write each distinct prop once in the canonical output

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21

## Context

Inherited props repeat on every component that inherits them. On Mantine, 19,506 props hold 3,137 distinct values, and the canonical JSON is 19.3 MB. The Vite plugin serves that whole output as its virtual module and re-serves it after every edit, so the browser downloads and parses all of it (34 ms in `JSON.parse` on Mantine) each time. Storybook does not read this format: both its build-time `__docgenInfo` and its Storybook 11 docgen providers take RDT-shaped props, which an integration converts to.

## Decision

The canonical JSON (CLI `--json` and `--format canonical`, NAPI `extractAll` and `initializeSession`, watch updates) writes each distinct prop once, in a top-level `props` table, and components refer to it by id.

- `components[key].props` and `components[key].notableInherited` map a prop name to an id; `props[id]` is the full prop.
- An id is the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the prop's compact JSON, as 16 hex digits. The same prop gets the same id in every output and update a build writes, so a client can merge tables. Two different props with one id fail serialization instead of one silently replacing the other.
- An `IncrementalUpdate` carries `props` with every entry its `updatedComponents` reference. A client merges it into its table and may drop ids no component references any more.
- Interning is a wire-format concern only. The Rust types keep each `ComponentEntry`'s props inline, and `ComponentEntry` on its own still serializes them inline.
- `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` stay inline: they exist to match other tools' shapes.

## Consequences

- Mantine's output drops from 19.3 MB to 3.6 MB and its parse from 34 ms to 4.5 ms; Spectrum's from 6.9 MB to 4.2 MB.
- Breaking for every reader of the canonical format: a prop is now one lookup away. `packages/napi/index.d.ts` types the table, and readers that want inline props expand them.
- Ids are opaque. They change when a prop's serialized form changes, including across versions, so nothing may store one beyond the output it came from.
- A hash collision fails the whole write. At 100,000 distinct props the chance is about 3 in 10 billion.

## Alternatives considered

- **Positional ids** (index into a table array): shorter, but the same prop moves between revisions, so every watch update would have to resend the table.
- **Interning only types**: the type is half of a repeated prop; descriptions, parents and tags repeat too. Mantine stays at 10.4 MB.
- **Compression only**: gzip already shrinks the output to 0.83 MB in transit, but the reader still parses 19.3 MB.

# Architecture Decision Records

Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [4. Defer full type-checker integration](0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md) — superseded by 0006.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.

- [7. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default](0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) — do not feature-gate the backend crate, run it by default, or let it replace a structural entry on a clash.
- [8. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs](0008-parse-cache-keyed-by-build.md) — do not load cache entries without checking the payload's header against the running build.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |

**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.

**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.

**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.

**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.

**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.

## What good looks like

Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.

# 0009. Write each distinct prop once in the canonical output

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21

## Context

Inherited props repeat on every component that inherits them. On Mantine, 19,506 props hold 3,137 distinct values, and the canonical JSON is 19.3 MB. The Vite plugin serves that whole output as its virtual module and re-serves it after every edit, so the browser downloads and parses all of it (34 ms in `JSON.parse` on Mantine) each time. Storybook does not read this format: both its build-time `__docgenInfo` and its Storybook 11 docgen providers take RDT-shaped props, which an integration converts to.

## Decision

The canonical JSON (CLI `--json` and `--format canonical`, NAPI `extractAll` and `initializeSession`, watch updates) writes each distinct prop once, in a top-level `props` table, and components refer to it by id.

- `components[key].props` and `components[key].notableInherited` map a prop name to an id; `props[id]` is the full prop.
- An id is the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of the prop's compact JSON, as 16 hex digits. The same prop gets the same id in every output and update a build writes, so a client can merge tables. Two different props with one id fail serialization instead of one silently replacing the other.
- An `IncrementalUpdate` carries `props` with every entry its `updatedComponents` reference. A client merges it into its table and may drop ids no component references any more.
- Interning is a wire-format concern only. The Rust types keep each `ComponentEntry`'s props inline, and `ComponentEntry` on its own still serializes them inline.
- `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` stay inline: they exist to match other tools' shapes.

## Consequences

- Mantine's output drops from 19.3 MB to 3.6 MB and its parse from 34 ms to 4.5 ms; Spectrum's from 6.9 MB to 4.2 MB.
- Breaking for every reader of the canonical format: a prop is now one lookup away. `packages/napi/index.d.ts` types the table, and readers that want inline props expand them.
- Ids are opaque. They change when a prop's serialized form changes, including across versions, so nothing may store one beyond the output it came from.
- A hash collision fails the whole write. At 100,000 distinct props the chance is about 3 in 10 billion.

## Alternatives considered

- **Positional ids** (index into a table array): shorter, but the same prop moves between revisions, so every watch update would have to resend the table.
- **Interning only types**: the type is half of a repeated prop; descriptions, parents and tags repeat too. Mantine stays at 10.4 MB.
- **Compression only**: gzip already shrinks the output to 0.83 MB in transit, but the reader still parses 19.3 MB.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Interned props: ADR 0009
content.description: Write docs/adr/0009 for the canonical output's prop table (content-hash ids, update carries referenced entries, rdt stays expanded) and index it.

content.subject: Interned props: Rust serialization
content.description: Custom Serialize/Deserialize for ExtractionOutput and IncrementalUpdate writing a top-level props table and prop ids in components (props and notableInherited). FNV-1a 64 of compact prop JSON; collision is a serialization error. Snapshots stay expanded. Tests: round-trip, id stability, collision, update table completeness. Update schema command.

content.subject: Interned props: JS consumers and docs
content.description: Update packages/napi/index.d.ts types, Vite plugin update payload (props), apps/validate normalize, docs describing the canonical format; measure size and time on corpora; open stacked PR on perf/output-path.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Interned props: ADR 0009
content.description: Write docs/adr/0009 for the canonical output's prop table (content-hash ids, update carries referenced entries, rdt stays expanded) and index it.

content.subject: Interned props: Rust serialization
content.description: Custom Serialize/Deserialize for ExtractionOutput and IncrementalUpdate writing a top-level props table and prop ids in components (props and notableInherited). FNV-1a 64 of compact prop JSON; collision is a serialization error. Snapshots stay expanded. Tests: round-trip, id stability, collision, update table completeness. Update schema command.

content.subject: Interned props: JS consumers and docs
content.description: Update packages/napi/index.d.ts types, Vite plugin update payload (props), apps/validate normalize, docs describing the canonical format; measure size and time on corpora; open stacked PR on perf/output-path.

content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Interned props: ADR 0009
content.description: Write docs/adr/0009 for the canonical output's prop table (content-hash ids, update carries referenced entries, rdt stays expanded) and index it.

content.subject: Interned props: Rust serialization
content.description: Custom Serialize/Deserialize for ExtractionOutput and IncrementalUpdate writing a top-level props table and prop ids in components (props and notableInherited). FNV-1a 64 of compact prop JSON; collision is a serialization error. Snapshots stay expanded. Tests: round-trip, id stability, collision, update table completeness. Update schema command.

content.subject: Interned props: JS consumers and docs
content.description: Update packages/napi/index.d.ts types, Vite plugin update payload (props), apps/validate normalize, docs describing the canonical format; measure size and time on corpora; open stacked PR on perf/output-path.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Interned props: ADR 0009
content.description: Write docs/adr/0009 for the canonical output's prop table (content-hash ids, update carries referenced entries, rdt stays expanded) and index it.

content.subject: Interned props: Rust serialization
content.description: Custom Serialize/Deserialize for ExtractionOutput and IncrementalUpdate writing a top-level props table and prop ids in components (props and notableInherited). FNV-1a 64 of compact prop JSON; collision is a serialization error. Snapshots stay expanded. Tests: round-trip, id stability, collision, update table completeness. Update schema command.

content.subject: Interned props: JS consumers and docs
content.description: Update packages/napi/index.d.ts types, Vite plugin update payload (props), apps/validate normalize, docs describing the canonical format; measure size and time on corpora; open stacked PR on perf/output-path.

# caliper-docgen-vite-plugin

A Vite plugin that exposes your React components' props on a virtual module and updates it through HMR as you edit.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

```ts
import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen'

docgen.components['Button'].props
```

On every change the virtual module reloads with the same output a fresh extraction would give, including removed components, enums and diagnostics. To apply changes yourself, listen for the update event:

```ts
import.meta.hot?.on(
  'caliper-docgen:update',
  ({ updatedKeys, updatedComponents, removedKeys, diagnostics, removedDiagnostics }) => {
    // Events arrive in revision order, each a delta from the one before: delete removedKeys, set updatedKeys[i] to
    // updatedComponents[i], drop removedDiagnostics and add diagnostics.
  },
)
```

In `vite build --watch`, a change to any file under `srcDirs` triggers a rebuild, even one no bundle module imports. A build fails if extraction fails.

Extraction runs on OXC through [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi), so a single-file update takes about 2ms. Requires Vite 7 or 8. The module uses the canonical output format, not the `react-docgen-typescript` shape.

Docs and benchmarks: [orin-dx.com/tools/caliper](https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/). Source: [github.com/orin-dx/caliper](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper).

## License

FSL-1.1-MIT. Each version becomes MIT two years after its release.

content.subject: Detection precision: render evidence, non-destructive renames, wrapper evidence
content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Interned props: ADR 0009
content.description: Write docs/adr/0009 for the canonical output's prop table (content-hash ids, update carries referenced entries, rdt stays expanded) and index it.

content.subject: Interned props: Rust serialization
content.description: Custom Serialize/Deserialize for ExtractionOutput and IncrementalUpdate writing a top-level props table and prop ids in components (props and notableInherited). FNV-1a 64 of compact prop JSON; collision is a serialization error. Snapshots stay expanded. Tests: round-trip, id stability, collision, update table completeness. Update schema command.

content.subject: Interned props: JS consumers and docs
content.description: Update packages/napi/index.d.ts types, Vite plugin update payload (props), apps/validate normalize, docs describing the canonical format; measure size and time on corpora; open stacked PR on perf/output-path.

200	**Invariant 5:** `DiagnosticSeverity` has no derived `Ord` — `max_severity()` on `ExtractionOutput` (output.rs:33-35) ranks severities explicitly via a private `severity_rank` function (`Error` = 2, `Warning` = 1, `Info` = 0) rather than relying on enum declaration order. The doc comment is explicit about why: declaration order isn't a promise about severity ranking, and a future contributor reordering the enum's variants (e.g. alphabetizing) would silently invert exit-code behavior if ranking were derived from `Ord`. `exit_code(strict: bool)` (output.rs:42-55) is the single shared mapping reused as-is by `extract`, `watch`, `check --strict`, and `inspect` in the CLI — changing this mapping changes exit-code behavior for every subcommand at once, not just one.
201	
202	## `ExtractionOutput`, `ComponentEntry`, `ParsedProp` — the top-level shape
203	
204	**Source:** `crates/core/src/types/output.rs:11-232`
205	
206	```rust
207	pub struct ExtractionOutput {
208	    pub components: BTreeMap<String, ComponentEntry>,
209	    pub enums: BTreeMap<String, Vec<EnumEntry>>,
210	    pub diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic>,
211	    pub stats: ExtractionStats,
212	}
213	
214	pub struct ComponentEntry {
215	    pub display_name: String,
216	    pub file_path: Utf8PathBuf,
217	    pub description: String,
218	    pub props: BTreeMap<String, ParsedProp>,
219	    pub inheritance: Vec<InheritedLayer>,
220	    pub notable_inherited: BTreeMap<String, ParsedProp>,
221	    pub discriminant_prop: Option<String>,
222	    pub composes: Vec<String>,
223	    pub tags: BTreeMap<String, String>,
224	    pub methods: Vec<()>,
225	    pub detected_by: DetectionRule,
226	}
227	```
228	
229	`detected_by` (`detectedBy` in JSON) is the extractor rule that recognized the component, so a consumer can tell an explicit declaration form (`functionDeclaration`, `forwardRef`, `fcAnnotation`, `classComponent`, ...) from an inference (`typedFunctionExpression`, `wrapperTypeArgument`). It is the grouping the per-rule precision sample uses (`docs/precision.md`).
230	
231	**Invariant 6:** `components`, `enums`, `props`, and `notable_inherited` are `BTreeMap`, not `FxHashMap` — this is AGENTS.md non-negotiable #2 (`FxHashMap` for internal maps, `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps) applied at the type level. `ExtractionOutput` and everything nested inside it that's part of the JSON contract is output-facing, so it gets deterministic key order for free from `BTreeMap`'s iteration order — output diffing, snapshot tests, and any consumer that hashes or compares the JSON depend on this being stable across runs, not just correct.
232	
233	**Invariant 7:** `methods: Vec<()>` is always empty. The doc comment says exactly why: "Always empty for functional components; present for RDT compat." This isn't a placeholder for a future feature — this codebase only extracts functional components, so there's nothing to ever put in this field. Its only purpose is matching the shape react-docgen-typescript consumers already expect (a `methods` array key must exist and be an array, even if empty) so drop-in consumers don't need a schema branch for "the field react-docgen used for class-component methods."

print('| Corpus | Time before | Time after | Size before | Size after | gzip after | JSON.parse before | after |')

Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.description: Typed function/arrow/HOC-arg and function declarations require render evidence (JSX/createElement/children/null body or React return type); declare function with JSX return accepted; wrapper first-arg evidence (render fn, tag + element type arg, PascalCase reference); reject createContext; diagnostic for rejected recorded candidates; remove empty-props guard (dropped 84 real Chakra comps); renames never delete an exported base. Negative families in shapes.rs; fix tests that pinned silent drops.

content.subject: Type-text P0s: quoted substitution, Infinity/NaN, Required extends, key sets, typeof props, generic alias in prop, cache bump
content.description: Done in #72 (structured args, typeof props, Required extends, quoted substitution, Infinity) and #73 (key sets). Generic alias in prop position moved to task 5 with the memo.

content.subject: Discovery and small correctness: relative excludes, export-default misses, Required unwrap, PropsWithChildren children
content.description:
Match .test./.stories. excludes relative to src dir; detect export default arrow/memo/forwardRef/class; stop treating Required

as transparent; children from PropsWithChildren.
content.activeForm: Fixing discovery and small correctness issues

content.subject: Watch revision model shared with cold path, Vite plugin and CLI watch fixes
content.description: One immutable Revision, single writer, assemble shared with extract(), real dependency edges (barrels, ../, aliases, .js), deltas with removals, seeded diagnostics, filters/plugins in watch; Vite: removals, keys, invalidation, build --watch, build errors; CLI: write --out at start, r re-extracts. Gate: snapshot()==extract() property test.

content.subject: Diagnostics identity and dedup, resolution memoization, cache fingerprint
content.description: Dedup by (code,file,span,subject) with affected components; memoize type resolution per run; cache keyed on crate version + extractor fingerprint with versioned payload; diagnostics on cache decode failure.

content.subject: Docs, DX and ADR 0007 amendment; restate #64 figures
content.description: Docs, DX and the semantic merge contract (Codex #4): ADR amending 0007 with component identity, field-level precedence (structural identity, checker props), diagnostic retirement, provenance and disagreement handling; triggers that do not rely only on visible incompleteness; schemaVersion vs mode/provenance fields. One reproducible scorecard (recall own/any, hand-labelled precision, prop type/required/default/description agreement, time, RSS, watch parity, with and without deps). Reconcile benchmarks.md, STATUS.md and roadmap figures; CLI DX items.

content.subject: Replace name-based special cases with structural rules
content.description: Revised per Codex: symbol origin (not every @types declaration terminal, record why resolution stopped); wrapper detection from callee signature where structural data permits, else labelled inferred and measured; library shortcuts need a type-resolution adapter boundary before moving out of core; finite keyof/mapped evaluator within a stated budget with opaque diagnostics; React tables from installed @types/react only when requested, curated fallback. Blocked by symbol precedence and the precision gate.

content.subject: Delta contract: every changed key and diagnostic in IncrementalUpdate
content.description: Codex #3. updated_keys must include kept components whose key or entry changed (name-collision key shifts on delete/create); add removed diagnostics; Vite drops updates older than the newest revision across files. Test: apply every emitted delta to the previous output and assert it equals snapshot(), including collisions, diagnostic disappearance and cross-file reordering.

content.subject: Symbol precedence: resolve the binding before builtin or utility names
content.description: Codex #1. named.rs checks React builtins and chain.rs checks TS utilities before source lookup, so a local ReactNode/Partial is misread. Resolve the binding first; apply builtin meaning only when the origin is React/TS lib, or as a reported fallback when resolution fails. Tests with local ReactNode, CSSProperties, Partial, Required.

content.subject: Render evidence: count only returned JSX and resolved element types; precision gate
content.description: Codex #2. JSX must be in a returned expression, not any nested callback; element return annotations resolve their origin; wrapper/rename name heuristics frozen. Add a hand-labelled precision sample per detection family (roadmap 95% gate) before any detector expansion.

content.subject: Silent degradations: tsconfig parsing, RenderProps shortcut, cache size bound
content.description: Codex #5/#6. Parse tsconfig with a JSONC-aware parser and report read/parse failures; RenderProps keeps the function form or reports opacity; bound the DTS cache file size before decoding. Silence list records why resolution stopped.

content.subject: Interned props: ADR 0009
content.description: Write docs/adr/0009 for the canonical output's prop table (content-hash ids, update carries referenced entries, rdt stays expanded) and index it.

content.subject: Interned props: Rust serialization
content.description: Custom Serialize/Deserialize for ExtractionOutput and IncrementalUpdate writing a top-level props table and prop ids in components (props and notableInherited). FNV-1a 64 of compact prop JSON; collision is a serialization error. Snapshots stay expanded. Tests: round-trip, id stability, collision, update table completeness. Update schema command.

content.subject: Interned props: JS consumers and docs
content.description: Update packages/napi/index.d.ts types, Vite plugin update payload (props), apps/validate normalize, docs describing the canonical format; measure size and time on corpora; open stacked PR on perf/output-path.

input.content:
Stacked on #94.

Inherited props repeat on every component that inherits them: Mantine's canonical output was 19.3 MB for 3,137 distinct props. The Vite plugin's virtual module is `export default <whole output>` and is re-served after every edit, so the browser downloaded and parsed all of it each time. Decision and trade-offs: `docs/adr/0009-canonical-output-interns-props.md`.

## Format

- Top-level `props: { [id]: ParsedProp }`; a component's `props` and `notableInherited` map prop name → id.
- id = FNV-1a 64 of the prop's compact JSON, 16 hex digits: the same prop has the same id in every output and update of a build. Two different props with one id fail serialization (compared by JSON bytes, not `PartialEq`, so `NaN` literals compare correctly).
- `IncrementalUpdate` (and the Vite plugin's `caliper-docgen:update`) carries `props` with every prop its `updatedComponents` refer to.
- Covers `extract --json`, `--format canonical`, NAPI `extractAll`/`initializeSession`, watch `--out`. `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` keep props inline.
- Interning is serialization-only: the Rust types and `ComponentEntry`'s own serde keep props inline. `ExtractionOutput`'s `Deserialize` expands ids.

## Measurements

`extract --src DIR --json`, fastest of 30 runs, before = main:

| Corpus | Time before | Time after | Size before | Size after | Node `JSON.parse` before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mantine | 81.8 ms | 44.0 ms | 19.3 MB | 3.6 MB | 41.3 ms | 6.0 ms |
| chakra | 21.2 ms | 18.6 ms | 0.8 MB | 0.6 MB | 1.2 ms | 0.9 ms |
| antd | 34.3 ms | 25.4 ms | 2.0 MB | 1.6 MB | 3.6 ms | 3.1 ms |
| shadcn | 36.9 ms | 32.6 ms | 3.9 MB | 2.5 MB | 6.0 ms | 3.3 ms |
| spectrum | 61.8 ms | 48.4 ms | 6.9 MB | 4.3 MB | 12.4 ms | 7.3 ms |

Time includes #94. On top of #94 alone, Mantine costs about 3 ms more, because every prop is serialized once to compute its id.

## Verify

- Fixture snapshots are unchanged (they render props inline), and `snapshots.rs` asserts every fixture's canonical JSON reads back into the same output.
- `types::output::interned::tests`: FNV-1a test vectors, sharing and distinct defaults, expanded ids equal `ComponentEntry`'s own JSON, round trip, missing id, collision.
- `pipeline::watch::tests::an_updates_props_are_exactly_the_ones_its_components_refer_to_and_applying_it_matches_the_session`
- `just test-rust`, `just test-ts`, `just test-integration`, `just lint doc-check machete typos`

**CI on #93:** the run actually took 1 minute 47 seconds. GitHub's status for one job, "Changesets", got stuck: every step finished, but the job never reported done, so the PR showed it as pending for hours. I re-ran that one job and it passed in 49 seconds. None of my workflow changes were involved; that job dates from 2026-09-26 (`9fb77d85`). Separately, my local test runs were slow because the machine was loaded by other jobs and I piped the suite into `head`. The full Rust suite takes 4.5 seconds.

**Deduplication is up as #95** (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/95), stacked on #94 because both change the same serialization code. All its checks pass in about 2 minutes, and so do #94's.

- **Format:** the output now has a top-level `props` table. Each component's `props` and `notableInherited` map a prop name to an id: a 16-hex hash of the prop's JSON, so the same prop has the same id across runs and watch updates. If two different props ever hashed to the same id, the write fails instead of mixing them up.
- **Watch updates** carry only the props their changed components use. A test applies an update the way a client would and checks it ends up identical to the session.
- **What changes:** `--json`, `--format canonical`, the NAPI functions and the Vite plugin's virtual module. `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` stay expanded. The Rust types are unchanged.
- **The extracted data is the same:** all eight fixture snapshots are unchanged, and each fixture's new JSON reads back to the same output.
- **Also updated:** ADR 0009, the JSON schema, the NAPI typings, the Vite plugin payload and README, `apps/validate`, the architecture docs, and a changeset marking it a breaking minor release.

| Corpus | Time (main → #95) | Output size | Node `JSON.parse` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mantine | 81.8 → 44.0 ms | 19.3 → 3.6 MB | 41.3 → 6.0 ms |
| spectrum | 61.8 → 48.4 ms | 6.9 → 4.3 MB | 12.4 → 7.3 ms |
| shadcn | 36.9 → 32.6 ms | 3.9 → 2.5 MB | 6.0 → 3.3 ms |

Most of the time saving is #94's. On its own, #95 costs Mantine about 3 ms, because every prop is turned into JSON once to compute its id.

I also added the changeset that #94 was missing.

result: PR #95 (stacked on #94, all CI green) writes each distinct prop once in the canonical output: Mantine's output drops from 19.3 to 3.6 MB and Node parses it 7× faster with the same data. #93's "3-hour CI" was a run that finished in under 2 minutes but showed a GitHub job stuck as pending; re-running that one job cleared it.

"""Wall time and peak RSS: stored RDT and react-docgen results vs a Caliper binary measured now. Usage: vs_rdt.py BIN"""
import json, subprocess, sys, tempfile

BIN = sys.argv[1]
RES = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-results'
IN = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-inputs'


def stats(result):
    s = result['summary']
    return s['time_wall_clock']['mean'] * 1000, s['memory_peak_resident']['mean'] / 1e6


def stored(path):
    try:
        return stats(json.load(open(path))['results'][0])
    except (OSError, KeyError, IndexError):
        return None, None


print('| Corpus | RDT ms | RDT MB | react-docgen ms | Caliper ms | Caliper MB | Time vs RDT | Memory vs RDT |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
for p in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    rdt_ms, rdt_mb = stored(f'{RES}/{p}.rdt.time.json')
    rdg_ms, _ = stored(f'{RES}/{p}.rdg.time.json')
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json') as out:
        subprocess.run(['hyperfine', '-w', '2', '-r', '10', '-N', '--style', 'none', '--export-json', out.name,
                        f'{BIN} extract --src {IN}/{p} --json'], capture_output=True, check=True)
        cal_ms, cal_mb = stats(json.load(open(out.name))['results'][0])
    f = lambda v: f'{v:,.0f}' if v else 'n/a'
    print(f'| {p} | {f(rdt_ms)} | {f(rdt_mb)} | {f(rdg_ms)} | {cal_ms:.0f} | {cal_mb:.0f} | '
          f'{rdt_ms / cal_ms:.0f}x | {rdt_mb / cal_mb:.1f}x |')

import json, subprocess, sys, tempfile

print('| Corpus | RDT ms | Caliper ms | Speed | RDT MB | Caliper MB | Memory |')

speed, memory = [], []
for p in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:

    cal = f'{BIN} extract --src {B}/bench-inputs/{p} --json'
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json') as out:
        subprocess.run(['hyperfine', '-N', '-w', '2', '-r', '10', '--style', 'none', '--export-json', out.name, rdt, cal],

        (r_ms, r_mb), (c_ms, c_mb) = ((r['mean'] * 1000, r['memory_usage_byte'][0] / 1e6) if 'memory_usage_byte' in r else
                                      (r['summary']['time_wall_clock']['mean'] * 1000,
                                       r['summary']['memory_peak_resident']['mean'] / 1e6)

gmean = lambda xs: __import__('math').prod(xs) ** (1 / len(xs))

"""RDT and a Caliper binary measured in the same hyperfine run per corpus: wall time (mean and min) and peak RSS.
Usage: vs_rdt_live.py BIN"""
import json, subprocess, sys, tempfile

BIN = sys.argv[1]
B = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp'
NODE_STARTUP = 'node -e 0'

print('| Corpus | RDT ms | Caliper ms | Speed | RDT MB | Caliper MB | Memory |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |')
speed, memory = [], []
for p in ['mantine', 'chakra', 'antd', 'shadcn', 'spectrum']:
    rdt = f'node {B}/bench/rdt-run.mjs {B}/bench-inputs/lists/{p}.txt {B}/bench-inputs/tsconfigs/{p}.json'
    cal = f'{BIN} extract --src {B}/bench-inputs/{p} --json'
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json') as out:
        subprocess.run(['hyperfine', '-N', '-w', '2', '-r', '10', '--style', 'none', '--export-json', out.name, rdt, cal],
                       capture_output=True, check=True)
        (r_ms, r_mb), (c_ms, c_mb) = ((r['mean'] * 1000, r['memory_usage_byte'][0] / 1e6) if 'memory_usage_byte' in r else
                                      (r['summary']['time_wall_clock']['mean'] * 1000,
                                       r['summary']['memory_peak_resident']['mean'] / 1e6)
                                      for r in json.load(open(out.name))['results'])
    speed.append(r_ms / c_ms)
    memory.append(r_mb / c_mb)
    print(f'| {p} | {r_ms:,.0f} | {c_ms:.0f} | {r_ms / c_ms:.0f}× | {r_mb:,.0f} | {c_mb:.0f} | {r_mb / c_mb:.1f}× |')
gmean = lambda xs: __import__('math').prod(xs) ** (1 / len(xs))
print(f'\nmean speed {sum(speed) / 5:.1f}×, geometric {gmean(speed):.1f}×; mean memory {sum(memory) / 5:.1f}×, '
      f'geometric {gmean(memory):.1f}×')
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.json') as out:
    subprocess.run(['hyperfine', '-N', '-w', '3', '-r', '20', '--style', 'none', '--export-json', out.name, NODE_STARTUP],

On average, Caliper (with #94 and #95) is now about **31× faster than react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and uses about 7× less memory**, across the five benchmark corpora. I measured both in the same run, 10 runs each, so load was the same:

| Corpus | RDT | Caliper | Speed | RDT memory | Caliper memory | Memory |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mantine | 1,195 ms | 42 ms | 29× | 473 MB | 126 MB | 3.8× |
| chakra | 570 ms | 18 ms | 31× | 315 MB | 41 MB | 7.6× |
| antd | 811 ms | 26 ms | 31× | 411 MB | 53 MB | 7.8× |
| shadcn | 1,270 ms | 34 ms | 38× | 620 MB | 60 MB | 10.3× |
| spectrum | 1,223 ms | 49 ms | 25× | 539 MB | 85 MB | 6.3× |

- **Speed:** 30.7× on average, up from about 23× on current main. Mantine, the worst case, went from 15× to 29×.
- **Memory:** 7.2× less on average, about the same as on main. mimalloc uses a bit more memory, which offsets the savings from freeing less; Mantine's own ratio improved from 3.2× to 3.8×.
- **Both times are full process runs.** Node itself starts in 41 ms; the rest of RDT's time is loading TypeScript and parsing.
- **These corpora have no `node_modules`.** RDT can't resolve dependencies here, so it does less work than in a real project. A comparison with dependencies installed is still to be run, and both tools would be slower there.

# Build identical inputs for all three tools: a filtered mirror of each project's component source.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT=/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp
CORPUS=$ROOT/bench-corpus

mirror() {
  local name=$1 srcdir=$2
  local dest="$OUT/$name"
  rm -rf "$dest"; mkdir -p "$dest"
  rsync -a --prune-empty-dirs \
    --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='__tests__' --exclude='__snapshots__' --exclude='test' --exclude='tests' \
    --exclude='stories' --exclude='__stories__' --exclude='demo' --exclude='__demo__' --exclude='docs' \

{
